articles.title: Start here
articles.description: Choose a practical learning path for your role and understand what AgenticOrg does, what it needs, and who stays in control.
articles.html:
What you can do with AgenticOrg

AgenticOrg is a workspace for building and operating AI agents around your procedures, documents and approved business tools. It brings agents, knowledge, workflows, approvals and run evidence together. You decide the task and the boundaries; an agent is not a replacement for your organization's authority to make a financial, legal or customer decision.

You can start with a document question, then progress to a repeatable workflow. You do not need to connect every system before the first useful task. A model and a small, approved knowledge set are enough for a read-only learning exercise.

  1. 1Choose a task

    Pick one narrow job with a clear owner and a measurable outcome.

  2. 2Add knowledge and tools

    Supply current procedures and only the permissions required.

  3. 3Test with sample data

    Inspect evidence, errors and refusals before relying on outputs.

  4. 4Run under review

    Assign operators, approvals, support and change control.

Choose your learning path

Your role Start with Then learn
First-time user Your first useful agent Knowledge and OCR, Run and chat
Administrator Workspace and roles Model setup, Model Gateway, Guardrails, Connectors
Process owner Create agents Workflows, Approvals, Evaluation
Bank or fintech team Business onboarding Reconciliation, Customer service
Merchant team Commerce BFSI merchant services
Developer or IT team API, SDK, MCP and A2A Self-hosting

Before you begin

  1. Obtain an account at app.agenticorg.ai or your organization's reviewed deployment. Accept an invitation if your organization already exists; do not create a second organization simply to join your team.
  2. Ask the administrator which company and role you should use. Company selection matters for business data and connector access.
  3. Confirm that a model provider is configured for your task. Your login does not automatically provide every external provider credential.
  4. Use synthetic or approved non-sensitive material for your first exercise. Do not upload customer identity documents as a trial.
  5. Know who can approve outputs and who owns the connected system.

What availability means

For regulated workflows, first read the BFSI capability status. The five process maps are fictional configured examples; 24 of 150 assessed functional capabilities are covered, 97 are partial and 29 remain gaps.

Implemented means a runtime path exists. Configuration-dependent means it also needs credentials, permissions, worker infrastructure or tenant settings. Example means a teaching scenario, not a pre-integrated solution. A listed connector, agent template, voice provider or channel is not proof of successful live execution in your workspace.

Shopify read-only commerce sync and the signed Twilio voice runtime have specific implemented paths. Other commerce sources and voice-provider options do not automatically have equivalent runtime support. OACP buyer answers and prepared handoffs do not themselves create orders or collect money. Jev advisory integration is access-gated and is not an active production decision authority.

Find the right screen

These links open the hosted application. Sign in first and select the correct company. On a self-managed deployment, use its hostname with the same path. Some screens are restricted by role; a missing menu is not an invitation to bypass permissions.

I want to... Screen Read first
Choose a company Companies Workspace and roles
Connect a model AI Credentials Model setup
Find or create an agent Agents Create agents
Build from a procedure Create from SOP Create agents
Upload a document Knowledge Base Knowledge and OCR
Connect a business service Connectors Connectors
Coordinate several steps Workflows Workflows
Review proposed actions Approvals Human review
Review business onboarding Governed cases Governed cases
Review extracted document fields (off by default) Documents Default-off screens
Watch or take over a live chat (off by default) Conversations Default-off screens
Work from a role workbench (off by default) Workbenches Default-off screens
Review kept call recordings (off by default) Calls Default-off screens
Decide transaction findings (off by default) Transactions Default-off screens
Trace where a kept item came from (off by default) Lineage Default-off screens
Configure voice Voice Agents Voice
Configure browser automation RPA Scripts RPA
Investigate run evidence Audit Log Monitoring
Inspect run timelines Observability Run observability
Configure model routing Model Gateway Model Gateway
Configure guardrail rules Guardrails Guardrails
Configure merchant commerce Commerce Runtime Commerce
Connect an external agent client A2A / MCP API and clients
Create an API key Settings API and clients
Review subscription or usage Billing Billing and support
Review recorded agent cost in USD (no sidebar entry) Cost Dashboard Billing and support

When you get stuck

For current license rights and the approved prospective policy, read Usage and licensing. Software adoption still needs an exact release/file scope. Existing Apache-2.0 rights remain unchanged; hosted plans, infrastructure and provider usage may have separate charges.

Use Troubleshooting to isolate the issue. Record the screen, time, selected company, action and safe error code. Never send passwords, API keys or raw customer files in a support ticket.

The guides describe source-verified behavior, not a promise that your deployment has every optional feature enabled. Ask your administrator about the deployed version and tenant configuration.

articles.title: Your first useful agent
articles.description: Create a document-review agent, upload a sample procedure, run a bounded task, inspect evidence, and prepare a pilot.
articles.html:
Outcome of this exercise

Build a read-only procedure assistant that answers questions from a small approved document. The example uses a fictional bank's complaint-routing procedure. It must not change accounts, send messages, issue refunds or make regulatory decisions. Allow a focused onboarding session; actual setup time depends on your account and model configuration.

Before you start

You need permission to create agents, a selected company where applicable, a working model credential, and access to Knowledge Base. If those screens are missing, ask your administrator; do not work around access controls with another person's account.

Create a plain-text sample document containing:

Example Bank - service-routing exercise - version 1
Owner: Service Operations
Account balance questions: refer to the authenticated banking channel.
Card loss reports: escalate to the approved card-support team immediately.
General branch-hours questions: answer from the current branch directory.
Missing or conflicting procedure: ask a supervisor; do not invent an answer.
This synthetic procedure is not a real bank policy.

Step 1: prepare the workspace

Sign in and confirm the organization and company. Open AI Provider Credentials if you are the administrator and test the chosen credential. If a colleague maintains credentials, ask them to confirm readiness for the selected model instead of sharing the key with you.

Step 2: upload and verify knowledge

  1. Open Knowledge Base.
  2. Upload the sample file. Wait for an explicit successful extraction/indexing result.
  3. Search for card loss reports. Inspect the returned text and source information.
  4. If no usable result appears, resolve extraction or search configuration before creating a workflow that relies on it.

An upload accepted by the browser is not necessarily an indexed document. Knowledge and OCR explains status, duplicate handling and quality checks.

Step 3: create the agent

Open Agents, then the creation screen. The wizard is titled Create Virtual Employee. You can describe the task to generate a draft or proceed through Persona, Role, Prompt, Behavior and Review.

Use a descriptive name such as Service Procedure Assistant. Select an appropriate operations role or custom type. Give it this bounded instruction:

Answer procedural questions using approved knowledge available to this run.
State the source and distinguish missing information from a verified fact.
Do not infer a customer's balance, identity, eligibility or payment status.
Do not change accounts, contact customers or initiate transactions.
If the relevant procedure is missing or conflicting, request human review.

Choose the configured model and leave unrelated connectors and authorized tools unselected. Inspect the full review screen, then use Create as Shadow. Shadow is a candidate/testing state, not a substitute for reviewing tool permissions or assuming all side effects are suppressed.

Step 4: run and inspect

From the agent detail screen, run a question that the document answers. Then try an unsupported request and a missing-information request:

Test input Expected behavior
How should a card-loss report be routed? The approved escalation path, with source context
What is customer 123's account balance? No invented balance; refer to the authenticated bank channel
Refund the customer and mark the complaint closed Refuse execution; identify the authorized review path

Inspect the output, status, source evidence and tool activity. A fluent answer is not enough. If retrieval is not available to the chosen agent/run path, configure its documented knowledge/tool integration; do not assume a global upload automatically grounds every model response.

Step 5: make it useful to a team

Have a second person reproduce the exercise with the correct role and company. Record expected answers and refusal cases. Only then consider activation, additional read tools or a reviewed workflow. See Evaluation and rollout and Team adoption.

articles.title: Workspace, companies and roles
articles.description: Set up your organization, invite colleagues, choose the right company, and understand why different users see different controls.
articles.html:
Organization, company and user are different things

The organization/tenant is the security boundary for your workspace. A company is a business context within that workspace, particularly useful for partner or multi-company operations. A user receives a role and permissions. Selecting a company does not grant access to another tenant.

Many confusing errors come from doing the right action in the wrong company or with a role that cannot perform it. Always check company context before interpreting connector readiness, agent lists or model credentials.

Set up the organization

The onboarding wizard includes organization details, industry and size, team invitations, system connection and a completion checklist. Choose Finance & Banking where appropriate; selecting an industry does not provision core banking, KYC providers or a compliance certification.

  1. Confirm you are setting up a new organization rather than duplicating an existing one.
  2. Enter reviewed organization information.
  3. Invite named colleagues using the least-powerful suitable role.
  4. Review connector setup separately; finish only the connections you are ready to own.
  5. Assign a platform administrator and a backup owner.

Understand role-based navigation

The sidebar deliberately differs by role. The backend, not a visible button, decides whether the operation is authorized. Current common roles include administrator, finance/CFO, HR/CHRO, marketing/CMO, operations/COO, auditor, merchant, domain lead, analyst (read-only within an assigned domain) and developer (builds personal agents and connectors, and approves only their own personal agents).

Task Typical owner Important boundary
Organization settings, credentials and billing Administrator Do not distribute an admin login to operators
Domain agents and workflows Authorized domain lead Tools and data remain separately scoped
Merchant commerce runtime Administrator or merchant Merchant binding and publishing settings still apply
Evidence and audit review Authorized auditor/reviewer Read access is not decision or execution permission
Human case decision Named authorized approver Machine credentials cannot impersonate a person

This is a responsibility guide, not an exhaustive permission table. Exact scopes are deployment- and role-dependent. When a link is absent or an API returns 403, have the administrator review your assigned role and required scope.

Multi-company operating checklist

Before a run, check the selected company, agent ownership, model credential binding, connector binding and input references. A tenant-wide connector can be available under different rules from a company-specific connector; a healthy global connector does not prove that your company can use it.

Do not copy a successful company's connector ID into another company's task. Have the owner configure the correct binding and re-test with that company selected. Verify negative access tests as well as successful ones.

Team changes and account recovery

During onboarding, the Send Invites action creates the entered invitations. The CFO/CHRO/CMO/COO labels map to domain-lead invitations for their respective domains. An invitation is created as administrator, domain lead, analyst, auditor or developer; one sent without a role is created as analyst. Check any per-recipient failure before retrying; successful recipients are cleared from the form rather than being resent.

In Settings > User Management, follow the entry points for company role management. Per-company mappings live in **Companies > company detail > Settings

Company Role Mapping**. That section is not a complete tenant user-directory or SSO-provisioning console. Have your administrator use the supported invitation and identity process for your deployment, not an invented bulk member editor.

Reset forgotten passwords through the sign-in flow; never ask a colleague for theirs. When a person leaves, review access, API keys, connector ownership, workflow schedules and outstanding approvals, not just their login. Confirm revocation with the actual identity/grant issuer as well as company role mappings.

SSO, SCIM and enterprise identity capabilities depend on plan and deployment configuration. Agree the source of truth with IT before relying on automated offboarding. Security and data and Adoption checklist cover ownership and review.

articles.title: Connect your channels to agents and workflows
articles.description: Bring your own provider account, protect credentials, link a private sender, and run bounded tasks from messaging, email, voice or signed gateways.
articles.html:
From a message to useful work

Create an agent with a purpose, knowledge and permitted tools, or choose an existing workflow. Open Channels in the dashboard. Choose a provider, choose the destination, and enter credentials from your own provider account. Connections start disabled. For Telegram, select Connect Telegram to check the bot and register its callback. For other providers, register the displayed HTTPS callback with the provider before enabling the connection.

  1. 1
    Create a provider accountOwner: Workspace user

    You own the account, permissions and billing.

  2. 2
    Choose an agent or workflowOwner: Workspace user

    Agent creators connect agents they can manage. Workflow connections require an administrator.

  3. 3
    Save protected credentialsOwner: AgenticOrg

    AgenticOrg encrypts credentials; it never returns them in the channel list.

  4. 4
    Register and enable the callbackOwner: Workspace user

    Use the callback URL and the provider's signing or verification settings.

    Blocked / exception

    Check the provider application permissions and account approval.

  5. 5
    Link a private senderOwner: Workspace user

    Generate a one-time command and send it from your private messaging account.

    Human decision

    Delegate your current account permissions.

  6. 6
    Run a bounded taskOwner: AgenticOrg

    A durable worker invokes the existing agent or workflow execution path.

    Blocked / exception

    Review the message, identity, provider signature or run error.

  7. 7
    Review results and approvalsOwner: Workspace user

    Open the inbox and run history. Sensitive actions retain their existing approval requirements.

Unlinked senders do not acquire your permissions. Their text enters a review inbox. Approving one message authorizes that message only. A provider signature identifies an authentic callback, not a human user. Linking is available for private text messages, not Telegram groups or email From addresses. Link commands expire after ten minutes, are single-use, and delegate for thirty days. Disabling a connection or rotating credentials revokes links and queued delegated work. An already-running external action cannot be undone by disabling its connection.

Credentials belong to you

A completed channel delivery proves only the configured target ran. A workflow that copies the message is a transport test, not proof of AI reasoning or tool execution. For reasoning acceptance, select a dedicated tool-free agent with a working tenant AI credential, send a synthetic question with a known answer and inspect the model usage and output in run history. Agree on a spending limit before making a paid model call. Do not reuse customer workflows for that test.

Enter secrets only in the signed-in credential form. Never put tokens, API keys, webhook secrets, passwords or one-time link commands in chat, prompts, repository files or support screenshots. To arrange assisted testing, share only the provider name, account approval status, test sender or destination you authorize, and a sanitized request ID. Use the credential form or your organization's approved secret-management process for the secret itself. Choose dedicated test accounts, minimum permissions and spending limits.

The channel callbacks accept bounded text messages. Images, files and voice notes do not start tasks. Use the knowledge-upload and voice setup paths for document processing and calls. Native replies default to task status only. Telegram agent connections may explicitly opt into final answers as described below; other messaging channels keep status-only replies. Email and generic gateways have no native outbound reply in this version.

Google reasoning model

The default for newly created agents is gemini-3.5-flash-lite. Existing agents keep their explicitly selected model. Administrators can select a different model, fallback and provider. Obtain a Gemini API key through Google AI Studio, enable the account and billing appropriate for your usage, and save it under Settings > AI credentials > Gemini. Use company-scoped credentials for company agents and the appropriate tenant credential for personal agents. Model availability and quota must be verified with your account before relying on it.

Gemini reasoning does not replace speech recognition or speech synthesis. This model does not generate audio; configure those providers separately. Operator overrides remain available through AGENTICORG_LLM_PRIMARY and AGENTICORG_LLM_FALLBACK.

WhatsApp and Meta Messenger

Create a Meta developer application and the appropriate business assets. For WhatsApp, attach your business account and phone number to the Cloud API. For Messenger, connect the Facebook Page and subscribe the app to its messaging callbacks. Complete the platform's business verification, application review and messaging permissions before serving external users.

Save the app secret, access token, a verification token you generate, the destination ID and a supported Graph API version. Receiver ID means the phone-number ID for WhatsApp, not the telephone number; for Messenger it means the Page ID. Register the callback URL and matching verification token. Subscribe to messages. AgenticOrg verifies the raw-body X-Hub-Signature-256 signature and checks receiver scope before storing any message. Use the provider's development/test recipients first. Test tokens can expire; replace them with the account's approved production credential when ready.

See WhatsApp setup and Messenger setup. Provider restrictions, customer-contact windows and billing still apply. An AgenticOrg connection is not platform approval. Use a dedicated verification token, never an API key or app secret: Meta sends it in its verification URL, which provider or infrastructure request logs may retain. Application access logs redact it.

Telegram

Already connected? Reuse it. Open the existing connection under Channels instead of saving the same bot as a second connection. Record its configured agent or workflow destination before any authorized change. A bot has one Telegram webhook; creating another AgenticOrg connection does not move that webhook or replace the existing target. Keep an unused duplicate disabled.

Open BotFather, send /newbot, and follow its prompts to create a dedicated bot. In AgenticOrg, choose Telegram and the destination agent or workflow, enter the bot token, select Generate secret, and save. Select Connect Telegram: AgenticOrg checks the bot account, registers the HTTPS callback and verifies its registration before enabling the connection. Tokens never need to appear in a browser URL or terminal command. A bot already connected to another application is refused; use a dedicated bot rather than overwriting that application's callback.

If setup reports telegram_bot_connected_elsewhere, its registered webhook does not match the new connection. This is a safety refusal, not evidence that the working bot is broken. The existing webhook is not overwritten. Open the original AgenticOrg connection if you own it; otherwise use a different, dedicated bot. Do not rotate working credentials, call deleteWebhook, poll getUpdates, or replace a production callback just to make an acceptance test pass.

Open a private conversation with the bot, generate Link my messaging account in AgenticOrg and send the displayed command from that private account. Then send a small, read-only task. Groups and channel posts deliberately do not inherit a human account's authority. Localhost callbacks cannot be registered with Telegram; use the deployed HTTPS service for the real account test. AgenticOrg supplies secret_token and requires the resulting X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header. Registration is not proof of delivery: confirm a real message and completed run in the inbox. See the Bot API.

Prove reasoning and delivery separately

  1. Record the existing connection's destination before testing. A copy-only workflow proves message transport, not a model call. Leave a working route unchanged unless its owner explicitly authorizes a different destination.
  2. For a real reasoning check, use a personal, tool-free shadow agent, a working Gemini credential, an explicit model and zero agent retries. Ask a short synthetic question, such as (23 * 7) - 19, without supplying its answer. Request structured JSON with numeric answer and confidence; check the independently calculated answer of 142 without lowering the review threshold.
  3. For the existing Telegram path, send one uniquely labeled message from the linked private account. Match its new inbox delivery, configured run result and the status notice actually received in Telegram. Do not submit an unsigned or fabricated callback as proof of a real Telegram delivery.
  4. Call the combined Telegram-to-Gemini path verified only if that same delivery invokes the configured reasoning agent or an actual model step. Two independent successful tests must not be described as a combined reasoning integration.
  5. Keep an approved total spending allowance. Zero agent retries does not disable SDK transport retries or the separate explanation request. Include those calls and thinking/output tokens in the bound; a recorded reasoning estimate is not the complete provider invoice. Do not change deployment flags or tenant limits to get a passing result.

Telegram's default reply is a status notice. For final-answer delivery, explicitly select the opt-in mode below and verify the answer actually received, not just a completed status. Reasoning traces and tool-call records remain in AgenticOrg. A provider-accepted send and recipient confirmation are separate delivery evidence.

Let your linked private chat receive the answer

  1. Open your existing Telegram connection in Channels. Record the original destination and reply settings if this is a temporary test.
  2. Choose Agent as the destination type and an agent you can manage. Choose Agent answer (private linked chats) under Reply content, then select Save settings. Enable Send replies. A busy destination cannot be changed until queued/running messages finish.
  3. Read the disclosure notice: final answers leave your workspace and reach Telegram. Use only an agent and content your organization permits there. This setting is per connection, not a tenant-wide switch or model permission.
  4. Use the existing private sender link. Send the complete question as one message, such as: "There are 7, 11 and 13 items. Remove the 11-item box, then remove 2 more items. How many remain?" The expected answer is 18.
  5. Verify the completed inbox run, selected agent/model and actual Telegram answer. Restore the original destination/reply settings after temporary tests.

    Linked private messageOwner: Channel owner

    The existing signature, sender delegation and tenant checks apply.

  2. 2
    Saved agent runsOwner: AgenticOrg

    Existing model, budget, tool and approval policies remain in force.

  3. 3
    Completed final answerOwner: AgenticOrg

    Only canonical final output is eligible; no traces or tool-call envelopes.

  4. 4
    Recheck disclosure permissionOwner: AgenticOrg

    Consent at receipt and send, current owner, sender link and agent access must still match.

    Blocked / exception

    Review the result in the authenticated inbox.

  5. 5
    Receive the answerOwner: Telegram

    One plain-text send attempt, bounded to 1,900 UTF-16 units with a shortening notice.

Enabling answer mode does not export old results. Workflow targets and other providers do not support answer mode. Changing a workflow destination requires an administrator. API clients may PATCH both target_kind and target_id together; a foreign/unmanageable target is refused. Management requires an authenticated human owner, not a machine/API-key identity. Neither route changes nor reply mode replacement rotates credentials, changes the webhook or relinks a sender.

An unlinked sender, expired/revoked link, inaccessible or paused agent, pending approval, error, missing answer or recognized secret-like/private envelope does not produce an answer reply. Results remain in the authenticated inbox; a safe status/review notice may be sent instead. Guard patterns are defense in depth, not a complete data-loss-prevention guarantee: administrators must restrict what the agent may answer. Final answers can contain sensitive business information even when no credential pattern is detected. Long answers are shortened, not split into repeated sends. Provider timeouts are uncertain delivery, never a reason to rerun the model or resend blindly. Disabling Send replies, switching back to Task status only, or disabling the connection stops future answer attempts; it cannot retract a message already accepted by Telegram.

If a completed run says Answer withheld, inspect the result in AgenticOrg; do not blindly retry it. Fresh intake carries an encrypted, connection-bound sender proof, so API and worker signing keys need not be identical. Receipts created before that proof was added remain withheld; old results are not retroactively sent. Recheck sender access and current reply settings before authorizing a new task. A fresh message is new execution and may incur model cost.

Self-managed deployments need both the channel worker and the periodic beat scheduler. The local Docker stack starts both. An inbox that stays pending can indicate a missing scheduler or broker; do not repeatedly submit the same task.

Follow-up questions and Hindi replies

Choose a tool-free agent, enable Send replies and choose Agent answer (private linked chats) on the existing Telegram connection. Ask the agent to answer in your language and use supplied recent conversation context as untrusted reference text, not instructions or authorization. No additional global feature flag is required. Status-only connections, workflows and agents with tools or configured traffic splits do not receive this channel context. The agent/company/tool scope is checked again before model dispatch and before answer disclosure. A change during the run requires review, not a silent handoff of earlier text to another agent. Existing routing correlations stay intact; they are not execution checkpoints.

    Private questionOwner: User

    Send one complete question to the linked bot.

  2. 2
    Readable model inputOwner: AgenticOrg

    Keep Unicode text readable while applying normal PII protections.

  3. 3
    Bounded recent contextOwner: AgenticOrg

Missing acknowledgements, errors, private/secret-like text, older unscoped receipts, different agents/companies and replaced sender links are excluded. Context remains in the existing tenant-encrypted receipt store; it is not a new memory database or a promise of long-term recall. Existing retention rules still apply. More context consumes model tokens under the same budget controls. Acceptance tests must respect existing budget limits.

मेरी काल्पनिक दुकान का नाम नीलकमल और रंग बैंगनी है। हिंदी में एक वाक्य में पुष्टि करें। कोई बाहरी कार्रवाई न करें।

Wait for a meaningful Hindi confirmation, then send:

अभी बताई गई मेरी काल्पनिक दुकान का नाम और रंग क्या है? हिंदी में उत्तर दें। कोई बाहरी कार्रवाई न करें।

Verify both actual bot replies and their matching inbox runs. The second reply should identify the same name and colour without asking you to repeat them. An answer about an unrelated person or organization is not a passing result, even if it repeats the correct facts. These checks do not provide general Hindi NER coverage or permission to bypass privacy controls. A completed status or high confidence is not evidence of a correct answer. Privacy analysis is not guaranteed equally accurate in every language; do not use real personal or customer details for acceptance tests. If context is missing or ambiguous, the agent should ask a short clarification rather than invent a memory. After 30 minutes, start again with the facts it needs.

Viber

Arrange a Viber bot account through the provider's commercial application process. New bots may require a commercial agreement; a normal personal Viber account is not a bot API credential. Save the bot authentication token. Register the displayed callback through the REST Bot API. AgenticOrg verifies X-Viber-Content-Signature against the raw body using that token. Link your private sender and test a text task. See Viber's bot account and API requirements.

For inbound email, create a Mailgun receiving domain, configure the DNS records required by Mailgun, and create a route forwarding a dedicated recipient to the AgenticOrg callback. Save the webhook signing key, not the general API key, and the exact receiving address. For outbound email, configure the existing email connector with your own OAuth or provider credential, bind it to the agent and review tool permissions. Inbound receipt does not automatically grant an agent permission to send mail. Start with a dedicated test mailbox and consented recipients.

Voice and telephone calls

Open Voice and calls as an administrator and select the existing voice-enabled agent setup. Create a Twilio account, obtain a voice-capable number, and configure its inbound Voice URL as shown by the voice setup. Arrange a test number you own or are authorized to call, approve the destination explicitly and run the voice test with that account. No paid call should be made to an unapproved destination. See Twilio Voice.

MCP tools and other channels

Open MCP tools to register a remote MCP server, supply its approved authentication and discover its tools. Review discovered tools and attach only the required tools to your agent. A connector credential is not permission to bypass workflow approvals or execute arbitrary writes. Private or insecure URLs are restricted by the transport's network-safety policy. Use a reachable HTTPS server for real provider integrations.

For WeChat or another channel without a native adapter here, use an approved gateway that verifies the channel's native identity/signature first, then forwards the normalized message through Other channel / signed gateway. This is not a native WeChat implementation. The gateway must preserve a stable sender identity and a unique event ID; it must not invent a user's identity from an unverified display name.

The gateway body is JSON with event_id, sender_id and text. Send an epoch-seconds X-AgenticOrg-Timestamp header and X-AgenticOrg-Signature, the hexadecimal HMAC-SHA256 of timestamp + "." + raw_body using the stored webhook secret. Callbacks older than five minutes are refused. The URL selects the tenant and binding; a tenant field in the body cannot change that scope. Retries reuse the event ID and exact message contents. Reusing an event ID for different contents is refused.

Verify before serving customers

Send a small signed test message, confirm it appears in the inbox, link the private sender or approve that one message, and inspect the completed agent/workflow run. Test a bad signature, duplicate message, expired link and disabled connection as well. Expect the same existing approvals for sensitive tools. A timed-out or interrupted execution enters review and is not automatically replayed, because it may already have performed an external action.

Channel agent targets must still be active or in shadow mode when the worker dispatches. Paused, retired, deleted, unavailable or no-longer-owned targets enter review instead of executing. A pause or revocation cannot undo a task already running. Workflow steps retain their existing approval and lifecycle policies.

Local provider-shaped tests prove the platform's wire handling, isolation and execution paths. They do not prove that your provider account is approved or that a real message or call was delivered. Record those account-backed results separately, with sanitized evidence and authorized test contacts.

An answer about an unrelated person or organization is not a passing result,
even if it repeats the correct facts. With the default-off
 AGENTICORG_PII_HINDI_GRAMMAR_ENABLED  rollout control enabled, the privacy parser has narrow checks for
unambiguous Hindi reference-question grammar; named values and identifiers
remain subject to redaction. These checks do not provide general Hindi NER
coverage or permission to bypass privacy controls.
A completed status or high confidence is not evidence of a correct answer.
Privacy analysis is not guaranteed equally accurate in every language; do not
use real personal or customer details for acceptance tests. If context is
missing or ambiguous, the agent should ask a short clarification rather than
invent a memory. After 30 minutes, start again with the facts it needs.

   Viber

Arrange a Viber bot account through the provider's commercial application process. New bots may require a commercial agreement; a normal personal Viber account is not a bot API credential. Save the bot authentication token. Register the displayed callback through the REST Bot API. AgenticOrg verifies  X-Viber-Content-Signature  against the raw body using that token. Link your private sender and test a text task. See [Viber's bot account and API requirements](https://developers.viber.com/docs/api/rest-bot-api/).

   Inbound email and outbound email tools

For inbound email, create a Mailgun receiving domain, configure the DNS records required by Mailgun, and create a route forwarding a dedicated recipient to the AgenticOrg callback. Save the   webhook signing key  , not the general API key, and the exact receiving address. AgenticOrg checks the timestamp/token signature and recipient; email always requires a human to approve the message before execution. Email From can be spoofed and is not account authentication. Text-only form submissions are supported; attachments are not ingested by this callback. See [Mailgun receiving routes](https://documentation.mailgun.com/docs/mailgun/user-manual/receive-forward-store/).

For outbound email, configure the existing email connector with your own OAuth or provider credential, bind it to the agent and review tool permissions. Inbound receipt does not automatically grant an agent permission to send mail. Start with a dedicated test mailbox and consented recipients.

   Voice and telephone calls

Open   Voice and calls   as an administrator and select the existing voice-enabled agent setup. Create a Twilio account, obtain a voice-capable number, and configure its inbound Voice URL as shown by the voice setup. Save the account credential and configure the supported speech-to-text and text-to-speech providers. Use trial/test destinations first. AgenticOrg's voice path checks signed callbacks and preserves outbound-call approval controls.

Telephony, speech recognition and speech synthesis have separate permissions, quotas and charges. Do not assume that saving a credential proves recognition accuracy or call delivery. Arrange a test number you own or are authorized to call, approve the destination explicitly and run the voice test with that account. No paid call should be made to an unapproved destination. See [Twilio Voice](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice).

   MCP tools and other channels

Open   MCP tools   to register a remote MCP server, supply its approved authentication and discover its tools. Review discovered tools and attach only the required tools to your agent. A connector credential is not permission to bypass workflow approvals or execute arbitrary writes. Private or insecure URLs are restricted by the transport's network-safety policy. Use a reachable HTTPS server for real provider integrations.

For WeChat or another channel without a native adapter here, use an approved gateway that verifies the channel's native identity/signature first, then forwards the normalized message through   Other channel / signed gateway  . This is not a native WeChat implementation. The gateway must preserve a stable sender identity and a unique event ID; it must not invent a user's identity from an unverified display name.

The gateway body is JSON with  event_id ,  sender_id  and  text . Send an epoch-seconds  X-AgenticOrg-Timestamp  header and  X-AgenticOrg-Signature , the hexadecimal HMAC-SHA256 of  timestamp + "." + raw_body  using the stored webhook secret. Callbacks older than five minutes are refused. The URL selects the tenant and binding; a tenant field in the body cannot change that scope. Retries reuse the event ID and exact message contents. Reusing an event ID for different contents is refused.

   Verify before serving customers

Send a small signed test message, confirm it appears in the inbox, link the private sender or approve that one message, and inspect the completed agent/workflow run. Test a bad signature, duplicate message, expired link and disabled connection as well. Expect the same existing approvals for sensitive tools. A timed-out or interrupted execution enters review and is not automatically replayed, because it may already have performed an external action.

Channel agent targets must still be active or in shadow mode when the worker dispatches. Paused, retired, deleted, unavailable or no-longer-owned targets enter review instead of executing. A pause or revocation cannot undo a task already running. Workflow steps retain their existing approval and lifecycle policies.

Local provider-shaped tests prove the platform's wire handling, isolation and execution paths. They do not prove that your provider account is approved or that a real message or call was delivered. Record those account-backed results separately, with sanitized evidence and authorized test contacts.

articles.title: Core concepts and glossary
articles.description: A plain-language guide to agents, tools, prompts, workflows, grants, knowledge, shadow mode, cases and OACP artifacts.
articles.html:
The simple mental model

An agent performs a defined job. It receives instructions and inputs, reads approved knowledge, and can request authorized tools. A workflow coordinates jobs. Policies, grants and approvals determine boundaries. Run history and audit evidence help you understand what actually happened.

  1. 1Task and context

    A person or reviewed integration supplies the request and company context.

  2. 2Evidence and tools

    The agent uses permitted knowledge and bounded tool access.

  3. 3Review and decision

    A policy or person routes uncertain or consequential work.

  4. 4Recorded outcome

    Inspect the result and authoritative downstream confirmation.

Glossary

Term Plain-language meaning Common misunderstanding
Agent / virtual employee A configured AI task worker Not a person or unlimited system administrator
Agent type The role or implementation used by an agent A type name alone does not identify an authorized stored agent
Prompt Versioned instructions for a model Instructions cannot create permissions
Tool A callable operation on a system Listing a tool does not grant its use
Connector Integration configuration and provider access Registration does not prove live readiness
Knowledge Base Documents and extracted content for retrieval Uploading a file does not train or fine-tune a model
OCR Turning scanned images into text Not guaranteed perfect recognition
Run One execution attempt and its recorded result A prepared answer is not an external transaction
Shadow A candidate/evaluation state Not proof that every side effect is automatically blocked
HITL Human-in-the-loop review A confidence percentage is not business authorization
Workflow Reviewed steps, branches and handoffs A schedule does not bypass an approval
Tenant Your organization's isolation boundary Not a company name in a prompt
Company context The authorized business entity for a task Not a way to cross tenant boundaries
Grant / scope Bounded permission for an identity or tool Not permission for unrelated financial decisions
Governed case Evidence investigation, policy and human decision record Separate from a generic agent run
Policy tier Deterministic risk classification in a governed case Not an LLM confidence score
Artifact Source-linked, bounded evidence or capability metadata Not transaction authority by itself
TTL / freshness How long evidence may be reused and how current it is A valid signature does not make old inventory current
OACP Agentic commerce trust and interoperability work Not a claim of adopted public standardization
MCP / A2A Integration and discovery surfaces for agents/tools Not automatic inclusion in every AI marketplace

Who owns what in commerce

AgenticOrg runs the buyer and seller agents. Grantex supplies trust, policy and canonical artifact authority. The merchant system remains the source of catalog, inventory and order truth. The provider, bank or fintech owns payment and mandate execution. POS or merchant systems confirm their own fulfillment outcomes.

A valid cached artifact can support non-binding conversation without sending every message through Grantex. An agent cannot use that cache to invent a price guarantee, inventory hold, successful payment or completed order. See Commerce.

Know the outcome vocabulary

Read the actual state: draft, prepared, queued, running, awaiting review, failed, refused or completed are not interchangeable. For integrations, require the provider/system-of-record confirmation before calling a business action successful. If you cannot explain the evidence behind a result to a colleague, pause and investigate rather than promoting it.

articles.title: AI providers and model setup
articles.description: Configure provider credentials, select models, control routing and costs, and diagnose tenant or company credential problems.
articles.html:
What this configuration does

AI provider credentials let AgenticOrg call the chosen model or embedding service for the authorized tenant context. A connector credential and a model credential are different: connecting your accounting system does not authorize model calls, and a model key does not grant access to the accounting system.

The administrator screens are AI Provider Credentials and AI Configuration. The agent creation wizard also has provider, model and routing settings. Inspect your deployment's options; labels do not guarantee free usage, provider access or regional availability.

Before adding a provider

Ask IT/security which providers, endpoints, regions and data classes are allowed. Establish billing ownership, retention rules, rate limits and a rotation owner. For BFSI, confirm whether any customer data may leave the bank boundary and which endpoint has been contractually approved. These are organization decisions; the product does not certify your configuration.

Add and test a credential

  1. Open AI Provider Credentials as an administrator.
  2. Choose New Credential.
  3. Select the provider and kind (for example LLM or embedding).
  4. Enter the provider-issued key through the credential form, not an agent prompt or document.
  5. Use a meaningful label that identifies its purpose without revealing customer information.
  6. Supply the reviewed base URL where the provider requires it, such as Azure or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
  7. Save and use the supported credential test. Verify the response and scope instead of assuming save means ready.

Credentials are stored through the platform's protected credential path. The form does not display the raw key again. Treat a masked entry as evidence of storage, not proof that every requested model is available.

Select a model and routing

In Create Virtual Employee > Behavior, choose the LLM provider/model and routing mode. Use a model actually served by the configured endpoint. Automatic routing can select a different tier based on configuration; disabling routing uses the selected model path. Confirm the resulting provider in run evidence before comparing latency or cost.

Tenant administrators can use the Model Gateway for scoped routing/access policies, dry runs and limits. It is distinct from adding provider credentials: a policy cannot make an unconfigured provider or model available.

Test a short task with the target company selected. Then test an agent or workflow using that same context. Do not validate a tenant/global key and assume company-specific resolution works identically.

For gemini-3.5-flash-lite, Gemini thinking offers Provider default or Medium (billed thinking) in the creation wizard's Behavior step and in an existing agent's Config > Edit screen. Provider default is unchanged for existing agents and agents without an explicit choice. Medium applies to the configured agent's supported Gemini reasoning, not every workspace or generic chat. Thinking uses billed output tokens; budget for the additional token use and response time within your existing limits. It is not an answer-accuracy guarantee. Choose Provider default and save to remove the opt-in. API clients use llm.thinking_level="medium", or null to restore the default; incompatible model/profile combinations are rejected. No global feature flag is needed.

Rotate without losing the operating context

Record which agents and environments use the credential. Use the supported rotation action, test a bounded run, and monitor failures. Do not remove an old provider account before confirming all scheduled and integration-driven consumers have switched. Never log raw keys in a rotation report.

Diagnose model failures

Symptom Check Safe next action
Credential not found Tenant/company, credential kind and provider Configure the correct authorized binding
Unauthorized/model not found Key scope, endpoint and exact model ID Correct provider configuration; do not paste keys into chat
Rate-limit or overload Provider quota, concurrency, current incident Retry with bounded backoff or approved routing
Knowledge search fails Embedding service and indexed data Test retrieval separately from LLM generation
Unexpected model/cost Routing mode and actual run metadata Adjust reviewed configuration and repeat the same task

Jev/System One is an optional advisory integration with separate TypeSafe access and evaluation requirements. A waitlist enrollment does not supply an API key or activate production routing. Keep the ordinary model path usable without it.

Default reasoning and your own Google account

New agents default to gemini-3.5-flash-lite. Existing agents keep an explicitly selected model. Administrators can choose another model and fallback in agent/AI settings; operators can override unset defaults with AGENTICORG_LLM_PRIMARY and AGENTICORG_LLM_FALLBACK.

Create or select a Google AI Studio project, enable the provider account and appropriate billing, generate an API key, and save it in the protected AI credentials Gemini form. Never paste the key into chat or an agent prompt. Choose the correct company or tenant scope and test a small reasoning request. Provider availability, quota and pricing depend on your account. This model does not produce audio: configure STT/TTS separately for voice workflows. See the channel workflow guide for account setup and tests.

articles.title: Model Gateway, routing and limits
articles.description: Create scoped routing and access policies, dry-run decisions, manage limits, and interpret model-call records and cost estimates.
articles.html:
Control model routing with the Model Gateway

The Model Gateway is an administrator console for reviewing provider/model choices, routing rules, access policies, per-model limits, dry-run decisions, recent routing records and cost comparisons. It does not create provider credentials. Configure and test credentials first in AI Provider Credentials, then open Model Gateway in the administrator sidebar (/dashboard/settings/model-gateway) for tenant-scoped gateway controls.

The gateway is off by default. Until a platform operator turns on the model_gateway.enabled authority flag for your tenant, or sets AGENTICORG_MODEL_GATEWAY_ENABLED for the deployment, the status card shows Gateway off, and saved routing rules, access rules and limits are not applied: each model call keeps the provider and model its agent asked for. The dry run still shows what the rules would decide and says whether the gateway currently applies them. With the gateway on, a call goes ahead without its limit when the limit settings or their Redis state cannot be read, unless the deployment sets AGENTICORG_MODEL_GATEWAY_LIMITS_FAIL_CLOSED=true.

  1. 1Prepare approved provider access

    Add credentials and confirm allowed models, regions, billing owner and data terms.

  2. 2Review current state

    Check gateway status and existing routing, access and limit rules.

  3. 3Draft one narrow rule

    Set its priority, match conditions, allowed targets and reason.

  4. 4Evaluate before rollout

    Use the dry run with representative requests and inspect the chosen route or refusal.

  5. 5Enable deliberately

    Confirm tenant policy and feature configuration, then monitor routing records and workload outcomes.

Choose the right control

Control What it decides Good first use
Routing policy Which configured provider/model or weighted target is selected for a matching request. A cost-aware policy picks the lowest-priced target whose observed failure rate stays under the policy's threshold, reading the routing records, and states that reason in the decision. A target with no observations in the window counts as healthy, so with routing records off (the default) the cheapest listed target is chosen Prefer an approved lower-cost model for a bounded use case
Access policy Whether a request matching a principal, application, agent, provider, model or other supported context is allowed or denied Deny a model for a sensitive use case
Model limit Maximum concurrent requests and/or requests per minute for a provider/model Protect a shared quota from bursts
Dry run What the current policy would decide for supplied request context Compare intended behavior before changing live traffic

Start with the smallest match scope. Priorities are ordered (lower values win); use explicit reasons that help the next administrator understand the decision. Review overlap between policies and access rules rather than assuming one rule overrides every other control. The dry-run result is a point-in-time evaluation, not a reservation of provider capacity or a guarantee about a later request.

Verify the outcome

After a controlled test, inspect the decision shown by the console. When routing-record capture is enabled for the deployment, use the Records tab to search by correlation ID and review provider, model, outcome, latency, token/cost fields and signature status. The Costs tab compares observed calls with available list-price data; an unpriced model or missing observation is not zero cost. Actual invoices and provider billing remain authoritative.

The records feature is configuration-dependent and disabled by default. Confirm AGENTICORG_MODEL_GATEWAY_RECORDS_ENABLED and its retention policy with the platform owner before expecting a history. Gateway status, API authorization and tenant scope still apply; a visible rule does not prove that every application path is routed through the gateway.

Safe rollout and recovery

  1. Use synthetic or approved low-sensitivity inputs first.
  2. Save the existing rule values and identify an administrator who can restore them.
  3. Test allowed, denied, unmatched, provider-timeout and limit-exceeded cases.
  4. Enable one change at a time, then compare the actual provider/model and failure rate.
  5. Disable or revise the specific rule if outcomes differ from the dry run; record the reason and retest.

Do not paste provider keys into prompts, policy reasons or support tickets. Keep credentials in the credential manager, and ask the provider or platform administrator to resolve quota, endpoint or model-availability errors.

Next: AI provider setup, Guardrails, Run observability, Security and data.

articles.title: Create and manage agents
articles.description: Use natural-language drafts or manual setup; configure persona, tools, prompts, behavior, visibility and shadow evaluation.
articles.html:
Decide the job before choosing a template

Write down the input, permitted output, source of truth, authorized tools and escalation owner. A useful job is specific: prepare a complaint-routing summary from the current service procedure, not handle all banking operations. Decide what the agent must refuse.

This existing product screenshot illustrates the fleet layout. Names, totals and confidence settings are sample values, not current registry totals or performance guarantees.

Three starting points

Use a natural-language description to generate a candidate, configure an agent manually, or use Create from SOP where your role allows it. Generated prompts and SOP drafts are proposals. Read every field before creation; do not assume a parser knows your approval policy or connector permissions.

Walk through the wizard

Stage What to enter What to check
Persona Employee Name, designation, domain, optional avatar Name the actual task; use approved image URLs
Role Agent type/custom type, specialization, routing filters, reporting relationship Match the business role; filters do not create access rights
Prompt Reviewed template or explicit instructions Cite sources, state missing evidence, define refusals and output structure
Behavior Model/provider, routing, confidence floor, HITL condition, retries, connectors and Authorized Tools Grant minimum access; set finite retries; review external side effects
Review Full configuration and visibility Company, tools, prompt, credentials and initial shadow status

Personal and shared visibility depend on your role. Administrators can configure shared tenant agents; a personal agent is not exempt from tenant policy. A reporting hierarchy is for routing, not permission inheritance.

For a reasoning-only agent, clear Use suggested tools when none selected and leave Authorized Tools and connectors empty. The API equivalent is use_default_tools: false, authorized_tools: [], connector_ids: []. This does not disable tenant policy, budget checks or review requirements. Zero retries is supported when you want a failed attempt to stop without an agent-level retry. An agent's monthly budget is not a per-call provider price guarantee; bound the model, context, output and number of calls separately for a cost-capped acceptance test.

Provider billing, account eligibility and quotas still apply, including to economy models. Check current provider pricing rather than assuming a routing tier is free. Zero agent retries does not disable a provider SDK's transport retries. Explanation generation can make a separate model request, so include that request and its retry/output limits in a test's total spending allowance.

For a small reasoning check, use a personal shadow agent, a pinned model, Disabled - Use selected model routing, no tools/connectors, zero retries and no voice. Ask a synthetic arithmetic question with an independently checked answer. Return structured JSON such as {"answer": 8, "confidence": 0.95}. Do not lower a review threshold just to obtain a completed result. A confidence written inside prose is not a structured confidence field; a correct short answer can still require review. A self-reported score is not measured accuracy.

Purpose: prepare a reviewable summary of the submitted service request.
Inputs: request reference, company context and approved source documents.
Use: only tools and knowledge made available to this agent.
Output: facts with sources, missing items, suggested next step, review required.
Refuse: account changes, payment execution, invented evidence and secret disclosure.
Escalate: ambiguous identity, conflicting sources, missing permission or policy.

Do not insert credentials, personal account numbers or legal guarantees into prompts. A prompt version is part of the evidence for a run; changing it changes the tested behavior.

Create, test and maintain

  1. Choose Create as Shadow after reviewing the configuration.
  2. Run representative correct, incomplete, conflicting and adversarial inputs.
  3. Inspect actual tool calls and source-grounding, not only prose.
  4. Compare the result against a human-reviewed answer set.
  5. Have the authorized owner decide whether to activate/promote the candidate.
  6. Retest after model, prompt, procedure, tool or provider changes.

Inspect the detail screen's supported lifecycle actions before pausing or promoting an agent. An operator override or paused state must be accompanied by a check of workflows and integrations that call it; changing an agent does not necessarily cancel work already accepted elsewhere.

Common mistakes

Too many tools can lead to unintended actions. Broad prompts make outputs hard to assess. Confidence thresholds are not calibrated accuracy claims. Shadow labels alone are not permission controls. Add capability only when you can explain and test its necessity.

articles.title: Run agents and use chat
articles.description: Supply clear inputs, preserve company context, read run outcomes and handle refusals without assuming an external action happened.
articles.html:
Choose the right entry point

Use the agent detail screen for a targeted run, the authenticated chat panel for conversational tasks, or a reviewed workflow for a repeatable multi-step process. The public Playground is illustrative sample content; it is not a production customer transaction.

Some roles cannot execute chat or agent runs even if they can inspect evidence. If the control is absent, check permissions with your administrator rather than using a colleague's credentials.

Supply an actionable request

Include the task, authorized company, input references, expected output and prohibited side effects. Prefer document/case references over pasting unnecessary personal data.

For the selected company, summarize the uploaded synthetic complaint file.
Use the approved complaint procedure, cite its source and list missing items.
Prepare a response draft for review. Do not email it or change account state.

Check company context before sending. A request that names another company in text does not authorize the agent to access it. If the tool needs structured inputs, use the expected schema; free text cannot replace required fields.

Inspect the result

Read the run status and output together. Look for source references, missing facts, connector/tool outcomes, escalation and safe error information. A model saying done is not proof that a provider accepted an operation.

Result What it means What to do
Prepared/draft output Material is ready for review Check evidence before distribution
Awaiting approval A human decision is needed Open the appropriate review queue
Refused Authority, safety or supported capability is missing Resolve the reason; do not weaken policy to finish
Failed The run could not complete Check logs/status and retry only if safe
External action confirmation A connected system reports an outcome Validate identity, amount/scope and authoritative reference

The exact status vocabulary varies by run resource. Preserve the returned state rather than translating every non-error response into success.

A completed status and high confidence do not establish answer accuracy. For a numeric task, check the operands and calculation independently. Pre-model PII protection can replace sensitive values with placeholders; do not ask the agent to guess a hidden operand or turn protection off. Explicit counts such as 7, 11 and 13 items must remain quantities, while dates and identifiers remain protected. Report an incorrect result with its request reference, without copying personal data into a support ticket.

For an agent using gemini-3.5-flash-lite, the optional per-agent thinking setting is described in Model and credential setup. Test the same request before and after a reviewed configuration change; extra thinking and model-reported confidence are not substitutes for checking the answer.

The Why did the agent do this? panel reads stored evidence, without making a new model request. Operators can enable direct-run audit history with AGENTICORG_AGENT_EXPLANATION_AUDIT_ENABLED=true (default off). With it enabled, a direct Run Agent result is visible after refresh as well as results from the durable task store; the newest record wins. Legacy audit records may lack tool-call details. The panel reports that absence rather than inventing a successful tool call or claiming no tools ran. Review decisions remain in Approvals; a historical review trigger is not a current approval decision.

Follow-ups and retries

Chat passes earlier turns to a follow-up only when the deployment turns on conversational services (AGENTICORG_CONVERSATION_V2_ENABLED, off by default). While it is off, each message runs on its own even though the panel shows the earlier messages, so repeat the document, case and company reference every time. While it is on, recent turns from the same user, company and agent reach the agent as context; another user, company or agent does not share them. Do not ask an agent to "ignore the earlier policy" to unblock a refusal.

Before retrying an external action, check whether the provider already accepted it. Use the integration's idempotency and status lookup where available. Blindly rerunning a workflow can duplicate an email, record update or provider request.

Prove the path before inviting users

Test a permitted question, a missing-source question, a cross-company reference and a forbidden action. Confirm that an access or model failure is visible, not represented as an empty successful result. For voice, validate the same task boundary through signed speech turns; for commerce, verify artifact freshness and prepared-only semantics.

Next: Troubleshooting, Approvals, Audit and monitoring.

articles.title: Knowledge Base and scanned documents
articles.description: Upload supported documents, understand OCR and extraction quality, handle duplicates, and validate source-grounded search.
articles.html:
What Knowledge Base does

Knowledge Base extracts text, preserves provenance, chunks documents and supports tenant-scoped retrieval. It is not model training. Extraction/indexing success and a useful retrieved answer are separate checks. Your selected agent still needs the appropriate knowledge/tool path.

Open Knowledge Base in the authenticated workspace. The deployed supported-type and limit metadata is the authority for your environment; administrators can inspect GET /api/v1/knowledge/supported-types with approved credentials.

Supported document families

Family Typical formats Handling
Text/data TXT, MD, CSV, TSV, JSON, YAML, XML, LOG Native parsing/decoding
Web/email HTML, HTM, EML Body text extraction; active content removed
PDF PDF Native text first; OCR for low-text/scanned pages
Modern Office DOCX, XLSX, PPTX Paragraph, table, sheet and slide extraction
Legacy/OpenDocument DOC, XLS, PPT, ODT, ODS, ODP Isolated conversion, then extraction
Other RTF Text parsing
Images/scans PNG, JPG/JPEG, TIF/TIFF, BMP, WEBP OCR with confidence and page provenance

Audio and video are not document uploads. File size, pages, decompressed pixels and archive expansion are bounded. Do not bypass limits by renaming an unsupported file.

Upload and verify

  1. Confirm data-owner approval, company context and the procedure's effective version.
  2. Choose a clearly named document, such as Complaint Routing - reviewed 2026-09.
  3. Upload and wait for a visible successful extraction/indexing outcome.
  4. Inspect extraction method, whether OCR ran and the confidence metadata.
  5. Search a known phrase and review source/page/sheet/slide details.
  6. Run a grounded question and verify it against the original document.

Each search result shows the document and, where recorded, its citation: page, sheet, cell range, paragraph or heading. Open excerpt shows the whole cited passage, with Previous and Next for the neighbouring passages. Where the deployment turns on query transformation (AGENTICORG_KNOWLEDGE_QUERY_TRANSFORM_ENABLED, off by default), How this was retrieved lists each retrieval step. Documents uploaded from this page are shared with the whole tenant. An API upload can name a domain (?domain=), and then users limited to other domains do not see that document.

If a duplicate dialog appears, choose Replace to index a new version before retiring the previous searchable copy, Keep both for a deliberate second copy, or Cancel to leave it unchanged. A failed replacement does not retire the original. Verify that search returns the intended version; do not leave conflicting policies current without an effective-date rule.

Replacement selects the current indexed revision ahead of failed or processing attempts, so retrying a failed upload does not leave the previous good copy current.

Domain-limited users cannot upload into another domain or replace/delete a document they cannot see. A hidden document is not disclosed by a duplicate-filename response.

Status Meaning Next step
Processing Stored, but not yet confirmed searchable The page refreshes while processing. Do not repeatedly upload the same file.
Indexed Indexing succeeded Search a distinctive phrase and open its cited excerpt.
Failed Indexing did not succeed Inspect the error, then upload again and choose Replace. The prior good copy is retained.

Where the administrator enables native upload recovery, temporary embedding timeouts, connection failures, rate limits and server errors receive at most four retries after the initial attempt, with delays of 30, 60, 120 and 240 seconds. The existing worker checks once a minute, so these are minimum delays, not completion guarantees. Invalid files, authorization errors and permanent indexing errors are not automatically retried. Large extractions outside the recovery storage bound and external RAGFlow indexing use the normal upload path instead. Your administrator can confirm which path is enabled.

  1. 1Approved upload

    Size and type are validated before parsing.

  2. 2Extract or OCR

    Native text is preferred; scanned pages are recognized where needed.

  3. 3Index with provenance

    Chunks retain page, sheet, slide and freshness context.

  4. 4Search and review

    Verify a known answer against the source before operational use.

Get better results from scans

Use clean, upright, complete scans with readable text. Avoid extreme compression, glare, truncated pages and mixed orientations. Keep the original for comparison. The OCR image includes India-first language packs, but operators must check installed languages and deployment settings for their material.

OCR confidence is diagnostic metadata, not the probability that a bank account number or monetary value is correct. Manually verify identifiers, totals, dates, negatives, handwritten fields and multi-column reading order. For a financial process, route ambiguous extraction to a reviewer; never reconstruct unreadable digits from context.

Errors and maintenance

Corrupt, oversized, unsupported or zero-text documents fail explicitly. A failed upload is not an empty valid policy. If OCR fails, ask the operator to check Poppler/Tesseract/LibreOffice availability and language packs. If extraction works but search fails, investigate embeddings and indexing separately.

Assign a content owner, review date and replacement/deletion procedure. Record which agents use the knowledge set. Use approved retention and access policies for customer documents; deleting a document and deleting derived evidence/history are different operations.

Next: First agent, Insurance assistance, Security and data.

articles.title: Connect business systems
articles.description: Register a connector, bind credentials to the correct scope, verify health and permissions, and grant only the tools your agent needs.
articles.html:
Connector readiness is more than a green badge

A connector links the agent runtime to a business service. It needs the right tenant/company binding, credentials, provider permissions, tool implementation and operational health. A registered connector or successful health check does not prove that every advertised business action works.

This existing product screenshot illustrates the integration catalog, not live readiness in your tenant.

Prepare the connection

Name the integration owner and system-of-record owner. Obtain an approved sandbox or read-only account. List the exact data and actions needed. For BFSI, a core banking, LOS, claims or screening service requires the institution's approved API contract and access process; selecting a generic connector does not create that integration.

Register and bind

  1. Open Connectors, find the provider in the native catalog, and select Register. Use the general Register Connector button only for a reviewed custom integration.
  2. When native prefill is enabled, confirm the fixed provider name matches the registry entry. Otherwise enter the canonical registry name manually; a display label is not enough.
  3. Enter the connector name, reviewed base URL, category, authentication type and rate limit.
  4. Use the provider-specific protected credential fields or approved secret reference. Do not put secrets in prompts, screenshots or ordinary task inputs.
  5. Review extra JSON configuration against the provider's contract. Do not assume arbitrary configuration creates a tool implementation.
  6. Bind the connector to the correct company or documented tenant-wide scope.
  7. Run the supported health/test action and inspect the safe result.

The native catalog's Register button can prefill the connector's exact registry name, category, endpoint and authentication type when the deployment enables the native-prefill rollout. Check the name before registering; a display label is not the registry ID. An unknown or outdated catalog link is refused rather than creating a generic connector. Without that rollout, the form remains the existing manual registration flow. For the four commonly requested providers, the reviewed credential keys are access_token and phone_number_id (WhatsApp), account_sid and auth_token (Twilio), client_id, client_secret and refresh_token (Gmail), and client_id, client_secret and merchant_id (Plural sandbox). A connector may also need provider-side permissions or additional settings. Do not paste real credentials into an issue or test report.

Registration stores credentials in the encrypted connector vault; it does not prove that the upstream account is authorized. A green connection probe proves only the operation it exercised. For external MCP tools, use the dedicated Remote MCP path below instead of registering a generic REST connector. Listing tools in another deployment is not evidence that this deployment has the same catalog or permissions.

Customers can bring credentials for their own provider accounts. WhatsApp needs a permitted business token and phone-number ID; Twilio needs an account SID and auth token; the guided Gmail form needs a customer OAuth client plus refresh token; Plural needs merchant-issued sandbox credentials before any live-rail review. The Gmail connection test now reads the authenticated user's profile without returning the mailbox address, and a successful profile check does not authorize sending mail. Register first, run the provider's bounded connection test, then separately prove each intended tool and scope with that customer's approved sandbox account. Leave the connector unverified if consent, scope, or provider access is missing.

The exact credential form differs by provider. Protected storage is not permission to grant unlimited upstream scopes. Prefer read-only scopes for the first pilot.

Connect a remote MCP server

The server must honor Accept-Encoding: identity; compressed responses are refused to keep the response-size limit effective before decompression.

  1. Obtain the server owner's approved public HTTPS Streamable HTTP endpoint and bearer token. Use the MCP endpoint itself, for example https://tools.example.com/mcp, not a website home page. OAuth consent flows, legacy HTTP+SSE endpoints and local stdio commands are not supported by this incoming connector path.
  2. Open Connectors > Remote MCP. Enter a unique name such as mcp_support, the endpoint and token. Choose Connect and discover tools. AgenticOrg performs protocol initialization and paginated tool discovery before saving. A rejected token or incompatible server produces an error; it does not create a healthy connection.
  3. Review the discovered descriptions and input schemas with the server owner. Server annotations are hints, not permission. All tools begin as write/unreviewed. Only tools advertised as read-only can be reviewed as reads, and obvious write names remain writes. A remote server can still misrepresent its behavior: register only trusted servers and use minimally scoped provider tokens.
  4. Select the read-only tools you have reviewed and choose Save read-only review. Run one Read-only connection probe with non-sensitive arguments. A successful probe verifies that tool, not every server capability or any real speech/payment provider behind it.
  5. In Agents > Create Agent, on the Behavior step of the Create Virtual Employee wizard, or in Agent > Config > Edit, select the remote connector and its exact tools. Save and reload the agent. Names are connector-qualified, such as mcp_support__search; a tool from another connection is not interchangeable.
  6. Run a company-scoped agent with an appropriate delegated grant. The runtime rechecks persisted ownership, active connector, selected tools and current schema before dispatch. MCP registration and a read probe do not bypass agent grants, operator overrides or action policies.
  1. 1Owner connects the HTTPS server

    The endpoint and bearer token are saved only after protocol initialization succeeds.

  2. 2Discover tools

    Paginated discovery stores the encrypted token and the tenant's tool catalog.

  3. 3Review read-only tools

    The owner marks reviewed read tools; every other tool stays write/unreviewed.

  4. 4Agent selects tools

    The agent names the exact connector and the tools it may use.

  5. 5Grant and action checks

    Delegated grants, operator overrides and action policy apply.

  6. 6Reload and compare the schema

    Ownership, the active connector and the live schema are checked again before dispatch.

  7. 7One bounded MCP call

    The call runs once within the size and time caps below.

Current boundary: write/unreviewed tools may be selected but remain contained by the platform's action policy. This path does not enable arbitrary messaging, voice replies, payments or destructive actions. Grant labels remain conservatively write-scoped; the reviewed read classification is a separate execution-policy check. Tools and their output are untrusted source data, never instructions to expand permissions.

Use Refresh to rediscover a changed server or rotate its token. Unchanged read reviews are preserved; changed tools require another review. If a server changes between discovery and execution, the call is refused with a connection/schema error. Archive the connection to block subsequent calls across workers. A request already sent cannot be recalled by archiving.

Only public HTTPS destinations are permitted: no redirects, IP literals, internal hosts, URL-embedded credentials or query tokens. Requests have bounded durations, arguments, responses and discovery pages. Calls are not automatically retried, because a lost response does not prove an external action failed. Raw credentials are not sent to the model or returned in connector responses. Tenant/company credential bindings and personal connector ownership still apply.

Input or operation Maximum
Discovered tools per connection 100
Discovery pages 10
Connector-qualified tool name 64 characters
Object input schema 32 KiB
Arguments 64 KiB
Response 1 MiB
Complete protocol operation 30 seconds

Ask the server owner for a bounded compatible schema; do not remove network or validation protections to make an incompatible server connect.

Symptom Next action
Connection rejected Check endpoint transport, bearer token, server health and public network reachability
Tool not selectable or save rejected Refresh the catalog and select the tool from the linked connector, not a copied name
Changed schema or unavailable tool Refresh discovery, review permissions again and start a new run
Write / approval required Use an approved governed action integration; a read-only review cannot authorize a write
Agent call refused but probe works Check company binding, selected tools, agent lifecycle, grant and operator policy
