Grant the agent only what it needs

Open the agent configuration and select the appropriate connector and Authorized Tools. Verify that a permitted read call works for the selected company. Then verify that an ungranted tool and another company's resource are refused. Model access and connector access must be tested independently.

Validate the real contract

Check Evidence to collect
Authentication A successful bounded provider request, without logging its secret
Scope Required read/action allowed; forbidden action rejected
Mapping Identifiers, dates, amounts, currencies and pagination are correct
Freshness Timestamp/source state reaches the user-facing output
Failure Rate limit, expired credential and unavailable provider are visible
Recovery Safe retry/idempotency and an accountable escalation path

Health freshness and credential presence are readiness signals, not an error-budget or sustained-sync guarantee. Run representative volume tests before relying on a connection operationally.

Maintain and troubleshoot

Rotate credentials through the approved secret path. Re-test after provider API, schema, scopes or tenant-binding changes. Monitor latency, failures and rate limits. Disable dependent schedules when the source contract changes.

If company A works and company B does not, inspect binding before changing the code or copying IDs. If a custom URL is rejected by network policy, have security approve the legitimate endpoint; do not turn off SSRF or private-network protections.

headings.title: Connector readiness is more than a green badge

articles.searchText:
Connector readiness is more than a green badge

A connector links the agent runtime to a business service. It needs the right tenant/company binding, credentials, provider permissions, tool implementation and operational health. A registered connector or successful health check does not prove that every advertised business action works.

Name the integration owner and system-of-record owner. Obtain an approved sandbox or read-only account. List the exact data and actions needed. 2. When native prefill is enabled, confirm the fixed provider name matches the registry entry. Otherwise enter the canonical registry name manually; a display label is not enough.
3. Enter the connector name, reviewed base URL, category, authentication type and rate limit.
4. Use the provider-specific protected credential fields or approved secret reference. Do not put secrets in prompts, screenshots or ordinary task inputs.
5. Review extra JSON configuration against the provider's contract. Do not assume arbitrary configuration creates a tool implementation.
6. Bind the connector to the correct company or documented tenant-wide scope.
7. Run the supported health/test action and inspect the safe result.

The native catalog's   Register   button can prefill the connector's exact registry name, category, endpoint and authentication type when the deployment enables the native-prefill rollout. Check the name before registering; a display label is not the registry ID. An unknown or outdated catalog link is refused rather than creating a generic connector. Without that rollout, the form remains the existing manual registration flow. For the four commonly requested providers, the reviewed credential keys are  access_token  and  phone_number_id  (WhatsApp),  account_sid  and  auth_token  (Twilio),  client_id ,  client_secret  and  refresh_token  (Gmail), and  client_id ,  client_secret  and  merchant_id  (Plural sandbox). A connector may also need provider-side permissions or additional settings. Do not paste real credentials into an issue or test report.

Registration stores credentials in the encrypted connector vault; it does not prove that the upstream account is authorized. A green connection probe proves only the operation it exercised. For external MCP tools, use the dedicated   Remote MCP   path below instead of registering a generic REST connector. Listing tools in another deployment is not evidence that this deployment has the same catalog or permissions.

Customers can bring credentials for their own provider accounts. WhatsApp needs a permitted business token and phone-number ID; Twilio needs an account SID and auth token; the guided Gmail form needs a customer OAuth client plus refresh token; Plural needs merchant-issued sandbox credentials before any live-rail review. The Gmail connection test now reads the authenticated user's profile without returning the mailbox address, and a successful profile check does not authorize sending mail. Register first, run the provider's bounded connection test, then separately prove each intended tool and scope with that customer's approved sandbox account. Leave the connector unverified if consent, scope, or provider access is missing.

The exact credential form differs by provider. Protected storage is not permission to grant unlimited upstream scopes. Prefer read-only scopes for the first pilot.

The server must honor  Accept-Encoding: identity ; compressed responses are
refused to keep the response-size limit effective before decompression.

2. Open   Connectors > Remote MCP  . Enter a unique name such as  mcp_support , the endpoint and token. Choose   Connect and discover tools  . AgenticOrg performs protocol initialization and paginated tool discovery before saving. A rejected token or incompatible server produces an error; it does not create a healthy connection.
3. Review the discovered descriptions and input schemas with the server owner. Server annotations are hints, not permission. All tools begin as write/unreviewed. Only tools advertised as read-only can be reviewed as reads, and obvious write names remain writes. A remote server can still misrepresent its behavior: register only trusted servers and use minimally scoped provider tokens.
4. Select the read-only tools you have reviewed and choose   Save read-only review  . Run one   Read-only connection probe   with non-sensitive arguments. A successful probe verifies that tool, not every server capability or any real speech/payment provider behind it.
5. In   Agents > Create Agent  , on the   Behavior   step of the Create Virtual Employee wizard, or in   Agent > Config > Edit  , select the remote connector and its exact tools. Save and reload the agent. Names are connector-qualified, such as  mcp_support__search ; a tool from another connection is not interchangeable.

articles.title: Build and run workflows
articles.description: Turn a process into reviewed steps, conditions, approvals and durable runs; test failures before enabling schedules.
articles.html:
Turn a process into explicit steps

A workflow coordinates agent tasks, conditions, waiting, notifications and human review. Start with a process map and a system-of-record owner. Decide what happens when inputs are missing, a provider fails or a person rejects the proposed action.

The screenshot illustrates the existing workflow view. Your available definitions and execution state depend on workspace configuration.

Create a definition

Open Workflows > Create Workflow. Choose Describe in English to generate a draft from a description of the business process, or Use Template to enter or edit a reviewed definition. The definition form includes name, version, domain, trigger type, optional cron schedule and JSON steps. Generated output is not an approved operational process.

A third tab, Build visually, appears only where the deployment turns on the visual builder (AGENTICORG_WORKFLOW_BUILDER_V2_ENABLED, off by default). It draws agent steps, human checkpoints, conditions and failure paths, lists every validation problem, and copies valid steps into the definition form. With the setting on, saving a definition that cannot be drawn and run is refused with each problem named.

The available step options include agent, condition, human-in-loop, parallel, wait, wait-for-event, notify, transform and collaboration. Review each option against the runtime implementation and selected integration. Do not infer that selecting a step type provisions its external system.

  1. Give the workflow a task-specific name and version.
  2. Choose the domain and start with a manual trigger.
  3. Select authorized agents and define structured inputs.
  4. Add a condition for missing/invalid evidence.
  5. Add human review before a consequential action.
  6. Define success and failure routing, bounded retries and a time limit.
  7. Validate the JSON steps; where Build visually is available, check the drawn paths and its validation list.
  8. Save and run with synthetic inputs before scheduling.

Worked process: complaint response preparation

  1. 1Intake

    Accept the complaint reference in the authorized company.

  2. 2Triage

    Classify the request and retrieve the current procedure.

  3. 3Evidence check

    Route missing or conflicting information to a reviewer.

  4. 4Human review

    Approve a response draft, not an unverified account action.

  5. 5Handoff

    Send only through an explicitly configured and authorized integration.

If no email or CRM action has been implemented and approved, stop at the prepared output. Do not rename it "sent". Workflow notification and business action permissions are independent.

Run and inspect history

Open the definition/detail page, supply the expected payload and start a run. Inspect the workflow run screen for each step's status, output, errors and waiting conditions. A waiting approval is not a hung workflow. A failed provider step should not be presented as successful completion.

Test condition branches and review rejection as deliberately as the happy path. Use a missing document, unavailable connector, duplicate event and rejected approval. Check that no unauthorized next step runs after a refusal.

Schedules and recovery

Only schedule a workflow when the operator has confirmed worker/scheduler availability, timezone, frequency, permissions, retries and duplicate handling. A saved cron string is not proof that a background worker is deployed. Begin with a low-frequency schedule and inspect actual runs.

Before rerunning, inspect whether any external step already completed. Resume at the documented safe step rather than replaying a money-moving or communication action blindly. Pause schedules during provider outages, schema changes and credential rotation where needed.

Next: Approvals, Audit and monitoring, Evaluation.

articles.title: Voice, speech-to-text and text-to-speech
articles.description: Configure the signed Twilio runtime, validate speech turns and call history, and test calls only with approved destinations.
articles.html:
Shipped voice path

The implemented voice runtime is a signed Twilio webhook loop using provider-managed speech recognition and text-to-speech. It uses the agent's instructions, tools and tenant boundaries. Selecting another voice/STT/TTS option in configuration does not prove that its runtime worker is shipped or ready.

The administrator accesses Voice Agents / Voice Setup. You need a Twilio account, approved number, credentials, active mapped agent, reachable callback URLs and a budget owner. Phone calls may incur charges.

Configure and validate

  1. Select the target agent and Twilio provider.
  2. Enter the account SID, auth token and provider number through the protected form.
  3. Test provider credentials.
  4. Select Provider speech recognition and Provider text-to-speech.
  5. Choose the call language and save.
  6. Configure the displayed inbound/status callback URLs in the provider console where provisioning is not automated.
  7. Check runtime health for the exact agent, not merely credential storage.
  1. 1Caller speaks

    Twilio collects a speech turn for the configured number.

  2. 2Signed callback

    AgenticOrg verifies the signature and tenant/agent binding.

  3. 3Bounded agent turn

    Approved model/tools prepare a safe text response.

  4. 4Spoken reply

    Escaped TwiML returns speech and the next input prompt.

  5. 5Call evidence

    Status and encrypted bounded text are recorded; history is masked.

Run a safe end-to-end test

Agree a test phone destination and time window with the owner. Use a synthetic script: ask a supported question, stay silent, ask an ambiguous question and ask for a prohibited account/payment action. Verify recognition, spoken reply, escalation wording, actual provider call status and masked call history.

Never place a paid outbound call to an unapproved number. A local signed-webhook simulation tests software behavior but not the PSTN connection, acoustic quality or provider routing. Both forms of evidence have different purposes.

Privacy and service boundaries

AgenticOrg does not store call audio in this path or expose full transcripts in the call-history API. Bounded conversation text is encrypted. The separate Calls screen (speech intelligence, off by default) keeps uploaded recordings and their transcripts encrypted; see Calls. The provider's recording, retention and regional settings are separate and must be reviewed with your data owner.

For BFSI, general policy answers and complaint-routing assistance are appropriate starting points. Voice identity, balance disclosure, account access, transfer instructions and card actions need institution-approved authentication and integrations. A caller saying an account number is not identity verification.

Troubleshoot

No callback: verify provider URLs and routing. Signature rejection: inspect canonical URL/signing configuration; do not disable validation. Provider-ready but no answer: test model/agent activity and tool permissions. Bad transcription: inspect language, microphone/network and a representative test set. Business failure: return a safe spoken error, never claim the action succeeded.

Next: BFSI customer service, Troubleshooting.

articles.title: Browser RPA and schedules
articles.description: Run reviewed browser scripts with approved domains, inspect durable history, and resume from a reviewed step after target-site changes.
articles.html:
When to use browser automation

Use RPA for a reviewed task on an authorized web-only system when a supported API is not suitable. Prefer an API for stable structured integration. RPA is an explicit external action, not a way around permissions, website policy, MFA or CAPTCHA.

The administrator screens are RPA Scripts and RPA Schedules. Available scripts come from the configured catalog. A visible script is not permission to run it against a real customer system.

Prepare a reviewed script

Document target system/domain, intended action, business owner, required inputs, credentials, success signal and recovery procedure. Approve the destination through normal egress policy. Private/loopback/metadata destinations and unsafe DNS behavior are guarded; do not disable those controls to complete a test.

Run one bounded task

  1. Select the reviewed script in RPA Scripts.
  2. Inspect its expected inputs and whether it reads or changes data.
  3. Use approved test credentials and synthetic records first.
  4. Run explicitly and wait for the structured result.
  5. Inspect durable history, duration, timeout/failure state and supported screenshots/evidence references.
  6. Confirm the business outcome in the target system.
  1. 1Operator selects task

    The script and inputs describe an intended authorized action.

  2. 2Egress and input checks

    Tenant permissions and destination policy are enforced.

  3. 3Browser execution

    Playwright performs the bounded script with a timeout.

  4. 4Result and history

    Success, refusal or failure is recorded with supported evidence.

  5. 5Business verification

    Confirm the authoritative target record before retrying or expanding.

Browser navigation success does not prove a submission or account change completed. A screenshot can show what was visible, but a durable target reference/status is stronger evidence for a business action.

Schedule only after reproducible tests

Confirm a worker/browser runtime is installed, reviewed schedule frequency and timezone, concurrency, credential handling and retry policy. A saved schedule is not proof that a runner is deployed. Verify real scheduled executions and an operator-owned alert path.

Test a selector change, expired session, missing field, blocked destination, timeout and duplicate request. Keep screenshots and logs free of unnecessary customer data and secrets. Use protected credential custody, not source-code constants.

Recover safely

When a site changes, pause dependent schedules and inspect the changed contract. Do not blindly replay a possibly completed submit. Verify whether the target system already changed and use its documented recovery/idempotency path. A CAPTCHA or MFA step should move to an authorized human process, not an evasion mechanism.

For BFSI, first use a read-only internal/test portal task with approved network and data access. A core banking or payments portal is not an appropriate target merely because it is reachable from a browser.

Next: Connectors, Security and data, Evaluation.

articles.title: Industry packs and business dashboards
articles.description: Use available packs as reviewed starting points and understand the finance, HR, marketing, operations and partner workspaces.
articles.html:
Packs are starting points, not automatic integrations

An industry pack can supply available agent definitions, prompts or workflow starting points for a domain. Inspect exactly what the selected pack installs. Its presence does not provision external accounts, certify a workflow or guarantee a business outcome.

The Industry Packs screen is administrator-oriented. Department users work through permitted agents, workflows and role-specific dashboards after configuration.

Use a pack responsibly

  1. Choose a pack aligned with a real process and accountable owner.
  2. Inspect the agents, tools, prompts, dependencies and intended outputs.
  3. Review installed/created candidates in the correct company context.
  4. Configure model credentials and required business connectors separately.
  5. Replace example procedures with approved, current content.
  6. Test with synthetic data and explicit refusal scenarios.
  7. Promote only the tested components needed for your pilot.

If a pack or template names an unconfigured provider, it is not ready to run. A template's confidence setting is not measured accuracy.

articles.title: Approvals and human review
articles.description: Review evidence and permissions before a decision, handle escalations, and distinguish workflow approvals from governed-case decisions.
articles.html:
What human review should answer

Review means understanding the evidence, authority, proposed action and possible effect. It is not clicking approve because an agent has a high confidence score. Assign the reviewer before enabling a workflow; an unowned queue creates operational delay.

Open Approvals with an authorized role. The standard queue supports reviewing agent/workflow escalations. Governed business cases use a separate case queue and decision-grant process described in Governed cases.

Review a standard escalation

  1. Confirm the company, run/agent reference and requested action.
  2. Read source evidence and any missing/conflicting information.
  3. Check the policy/HITL reason and connector/tool scope.
  4. Verify whether the action is a draft, an external change or a business decision.
  5. Approve or reject through the supported control only within your authority.
  6. Inspect the recorded result and downstream status. Approval does not prove that the provider action completed.

A failed queue load must not be interpreted as "no pending approvals". Resolve an error and refresh the authoritative state before making a decision.

Standard approval versus governed-case decision

Path What it reviews Who supplies decision authority
Agent/workflow HITL A run's proposed task or escalation Authorized workflow/business reviewer under the configured rules
Governed-case screening review Accept/override a screening proposal with evidence Authenticated human analyst; an override requires a reason
Governed-case final decision Exact current case version and semantic action External decision-grant issuer and named approvers

Do not use a generic approval button as a substitute for a governed-case decision. The case console cannot mint decision authority. Machine credentials cannot sign in as a human reviewer.

Handling changed or incomplete evidence

If a source changes while you review, inspect the current version again. A governed-case decision request can expire, be superseded or be refused because the case changed; create a new request for the current memo instead of reusing old approval evidence.

Request missing information or reject an unsafe proposal. Do not ask the agent to fill gaps with assumptions. A refusal is a useful safety outcome when authorization or evidence is absent.

Multi-person approval rules

When an approval policy applies to an item, the person who requested it cannot decide it (403). Each person votes once per item across every step: a second vote returns 409, so a policy that needs the same person at two steps cannot complete. A step whose condition cannot be evaluated for the item, for example because the item lacks a field the condition names, still applies and needs its own approvers. If the item's policy is deleted, replaced, or loses the step the item is waiting on, decisions return 409 and the item stays pending until it expires.

Where the platform operator sets the stricter condition mode (authority flag approvals.unevaluable_condition.deny, off by default), an approval on an item with such a step returns 409 approval_decision_refused with reason code approval_condition_unevaluable and is not counted; a rejection is still accepted. These refusals are the policy working. Ask the policy owner to correct the policy or assign another reviewer; do not sign in twice as different identities.

Operating the queue

Assign primary and backup reviewers, a review target, an escalation contact and absence coverage. Track queue age and rejection reasons. Separate preparation from approval wherever your policy requires it. Reviewers need training in the task domain, not only product navigation.

For BFSI, loan, onboarding, claim, sanction, account-change and payment decisions remain with the institution's authorized process. Product functionality is not regulatory approval or certification.

articles.title: Governed business onboarding cases
articles.description: Investigate a business, inspect cited evidence and deterministic policy scores, review screening proposals, and request a human decision.
articles.html:
What a governed case is

A governed business case brings read-only investigation, cited evidence, deterministic policy results, screening proposals and human decision authority into one traceable record. An agent may investigate and prepare a recommendation. It cannot approve, decline, close, file or pay through this case path.

This feature is tenant-gated and configuration-dependent. Your operator must configure the active case-role agents, reviewed provider manifest, reviewed policy, Grantex grants and decision issuer. Shipped example policies are not production-approved bank policies.

Where to work

The case queue is at /dashboard/approvals/cases. Open a case at /dashboard/approvals/cases/{case_ref}. These screens require the relevant scopes and tenant feature flag. governed_cases_disabled means the feature is not enabled; it is not an empty successful queue.

  1. 1Application submitted

    A reviewed API/workflow supplies the authorized business application.

  2. 2Read-only investigation

    Registered tools check permitted evidence under grants and exact purpose controls.

  3. 3Memo and policy

    Findings carry citations, missing items, risk tier and fired rules.

  4. 4Analyst review

    A person reviews screening proposals and requests missing information.

  5. 5Human decision

    Named approvers use the configured issuer; AgenticOrg records verified grants.

  6. 6Signed handoff

    The operator's system receives the current case outcome; it owns the business action.

Read the case correctly

Inspect each memo section: complete, partial, not available and provider error mean different things. Missing evidence is not a clean result. Citations identify the provider, upstream record, field and retrieval time. Where retained, Show the passage retrieves encrypted, digest-checked evidence as text.

The policy section shows the policy ID/version, score, tier, input digest and fired rules. Model confidence is metadata and gates nothing in this case path. A recommendation marked requires_human_decision is a proposal, not approval.

Review screening proposals

Compare identifiers and evidence. Accept preserves the proposed outcome; Override requires a different outcome and a written reason. The server records the signed-in human identity. A review is written once and only while the case is awaiting decision. It does not close the upstream screening hit automatically.

Request and record the final decision

  1. Choose the outcome to request. Supply a reason if it differs from the recommendation.
  2. Open the issuer's approval page. The person authenticates and performs required step-up there.
  3. Watch approval progress, including a distinct second approver when required.
  4. Record the decision only when valid grants exist for the current exact case version/action.

If the issuer is unconfigured, the default verifier refuses decisions. decision_required, same_approver, case_changed and decision_service_not_configured are meaningful reasons, not errors to hide.

Integrate with the institution

Applications and signed case handoffs require reviewed API integration. The console is not a universal application-intake form or core-banking adapter. The signed outbox and REST case record provide evidence to your system of record; the institution controls account opening, monitoring, reporting and retention.

Provider events reach a tenant-specific address. A tenant administrator signed in as a person reads it from GET /api/v1/case-push/provider-webhook-inbox?provider=<name> and gives it to the provider; treat it as a credential. It has the form /api/v1/webhooks/providers/{tenant_id}/{provider}/{token}; the earlier tokenless path answers 404. A delivery to that address within the 256 KiB body cap is answered with 202 while governed cases are on for the tenant (a larger body gets 413), and one that cannot be verified is recorded without being acted on. Rotating AGENTICORG_SECRET_KEY changes every tenant's address, so re-point the providers after a rotation.

Deciding, withdrawing, requesting a decision, reviewing a screening disposition and approving an information request need a person's session. An API key or agent token gets 403 human_session_required.

AgenticOrg pins the Grantex Python SDK (grantex==0.7.1) and calls its enforcement check with the grant token, connector, tool and any numeric amount. It does not pass a case id or case purpose, so a token's case purpose and per-case caps are not checked on this path. The role's case-purpose allowlist is a local AgenticOrg control, and pooled grants are not bound to one case. Evaluate that boundary explicitly before enabling a production process.

Next: BFSI onboarding walkthrough, Security and data.

articles.title: Documents, conversations, calls and workbenches
articles.description: Find and use the Documents, Conversations, Workbenches, Calls, Transactions and Lineage screens, each off until an operator turns on its setting.
articles.html:
Six screens that ship switched off

Six console screens belong to services that are built into the product but switched off in a default installation. Each needs its own deployment setting, which a platform operator turns on. While a service is off, it processes nothing and its other routes answer as not found.

Screen Sidebar entry and who sees it Deployment setting (off by default) While it is off
Documents Always listed for roles that can open the approval queue AGENTICORG_IDP_ENABLED The page shows "Document processing is off for this deployment"; the API answers 404 idp_disabled
Conversations Always listed for administrators AGENTICORG_CONVERSATION_V2_ENABLED The page shows "Conversational services are off for this deployment"; the API answers 404 conversation_disabled
Workbenches Always listed for every role except merchant AGENTICORG_WORKBENCH_V2_ENABLED The page says "Workbenches are off for this deployment."
Calls Administrator, COO and auditor; hidden until the service is on AGENTICORG_SPEECH_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED No sidebar entry
Transactions Administrator, CFO, COO and auditor; hidden until the service is on AGENTICORG_TRANSACTION_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED No sidebar entry
Lineage Administrator, CxO roles, auditor and domain lead; hidden until the service is on AGENTICORG_LINEAGE_ENABLED No sidebar entry

An "off for this deployment" message is configuration, not an empty queue. Ask the platform owner whether the service is meant to be on; do not treat it as "nothing to review". The sidebar only offers a page; the server still checks each request against your role and scopes.

  1. 1Choose one service

    Pick the screen a pilot needs and name its business owner and reviewer.

  2. 2Agree the data terms

    Confirm what the service keeps, who may read it and how it is removed.

  3. 3Turn on the setting

    The platform operator sets the service's deployment setting.

  4. 4Confirm the screen

    Reopen the screen and check that the off message has gone.

  5. 5Test with fictional material

    Run one synthetic document, call or record through the service.

  6. 6Review before relying on it

    A named person checks each output before anyone acts on it.

Documents: review extracted fields

With document processing on, a file sent to POST /api/v1/idp/analyse?store=true is split into typed documents (bank statement, salary slip, invoice, identity document and other types in the catalogue), and its fields and tables are extracted with the place on the page each came from. The screen has no upload button; files arrive through that API.

Filter the list by Needs review, Processed, Approved, Rejected or All. Open a file to see each page with a box drawn around every field. The box colour shows whether a field was read with high or low confidence, is missing, or has been corrected. Click a field to jump to its page, type a correction and choose Save; the extracted value stays visible beside your correction. Then Approve or Reject the whole file. The review reasons at the top say why a file was routed to a person, for example a missing required field or a page whose text could not be read.

A confidence colour is a hint, not a verified value. Check account numbers, amounts, dates and identity numbers against the page image every time.

Conversations: watch and take over a chat

With conversational services on, an administrator sees every chat conversation in progress or escalated, newest activity first, with who holds each one. Open one to read its transcript. Take over stops the runtime from answering: the user's next messages are shown to you and your replies reach the user's chat. Release hands the conversation back to the runtime. The screen updates through the live feed, which carries only the fact that something changed, never the message text.

The same setting turns on banking intents in chat and passes earlier turns to the agent as context; see Run agents and use chat.

Workbenches: one place per role

With workbenches on, the index lists the workbenches your role holds or an administrator assigned to you. A workbench shows tabs with the number of items waiting behind each. Most tabs open the page they name (for example Documents or Approvals), and that page applies its own permissions. A content-drafts tab lists drafts waiting for a decision with Approve and Reject. Use Refresh counts before reporting a queue size; a dash means the count is not available, not zero.

Calls: recordings, transcripts and summaries

With speech intelligence on, a recording sent to POST /api/v1/speech/recordings is split by speaker and transcribed, by a local engine where the deployment installed one or through the tenant's own speech-provider credential. The audio and the transcript are kept encrypted under the tenant's key. The screen has no upload button.

Open a recording to see each speaker's talk time and turns. Summarise asks a model for the intent, key points and next actions; From the words only builds the same summary from the transcript without a model. Redact spoken data finds spoken card numbers, one-time codes, CVVs and PINs, replaces them in the transcript, silences them in the audio and records only the kinds and times removed. Sentiment, empathy, talk ratio and escalation risk are review aids for a supervisor, not a judgement of the staff member or the customer. Agree retention and removal of recordings with the data owner before turning the service on; see Security and data.

Transactions: findings under human disposition

With transaction intelligence on, transaction records are loaded through the API and detectors look for patterns such as structuring and pass-through movements. Each finding names an entity, a summary, a severity and its supporting records. Filter by Open, Confirmed, Escalated or Dismissed.

Draft narrative writes a draft account of the finding, by a model or from the facts alone, with what is still to check. Download evidence exports the finding with its supporting rows and a digest over the package. Show the fund flow draws the accounts and counterparties around the entity across a chosen number of hops. A reviewer with approval access records Confirm, Escalate or Dismiss; a dismissal needs notes. A narrative is a draft for an investigator, never a regulatory filing, and auditors can read findings without deciding them.

Lineage: where a kept item came from

With lineage on, ingestion records each kept item's source, version and processing steps. Search by kind and reference, choose Upstream (sources), Downstream (uses) or Both and a number of hops, then open an item to trace it. The sync-sources table lists scheduled sources with their last run, and Run now starts one. Items ingested while lineage was off have no recorded chain, so "No provenance kept yet" can mean the item predates the switch.

Next: Approvals, Security and data, Troubleshooting, Self-hosting.

Redact spoken data   finds spoken card numbers, one-time codes, CVVs and PINs, replaces them in the transcript, silences them in the audio and records only the kinds and times removed. Sentiment, empathy, talk ratio and escalation risk are review aids for a supervisor, not a judgement of the staff member or the customer. Agree retention and removal of recordings with the data owner before turning the service on; see [Security and data](/docs/security-and-data).

   Transactions: findings under human disposition

With transaction intelligence on, transaction records are loaded through the API and detectors look for patterns such as structuring and pass-through movements. Each finding names an entity, a summary, a severity and its supporting records. Filter by   Open  ,   Confirmed  ,   Escalated   or   Dismissed  .

  Draft narrative   writes a draft account of the finding, by a model or from the facts alone, with what is still to check.   Download evidence   exports the finding with its supporting rows and a digest over the package.   Show the fund flow   draws the accounts and counterparties around the entity across a chosen number of hops. A reviewer with approval access records   Confirm  ,   Escalate   or   Dismiss  ; a dismissal needs notes. A narrative is a draft for an investigator, never a regulatory filing, and auditors can read findings without deciding them.

   Lineage: where a kept item came from

With lineage on, ingestion records each kept item's source, version and processing steps. Search by kind and reference, choose   Upstream (sources)  ,   Downstream (uses)   or   Both   and a number of hops, then open an item to trace it. The sync-sources table lists scheduled sources with their last run, and   Run now   starts one. Items ingested while lineage was off have no recorded chain, so "No provenance kept yet" can mean the item predates the switch.

Next: [Approvals](/docs/approvals), [Security and data](/docs/security-and-data), [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting), [Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting).

articles.title: Audit, monitoring and run history
articles.description: Read agent and workflow evidence, understand dashboard limits, investigate failures, and measure your own service outcomes.
articles.html:
What evidence you should inspect

Run evidence helps answer who requested a task, which company/agent handled it, which tools were attempted, what failed, what required review and what outcome was reported. Use Audit Log, Observability, agent history and workflow run detail according to your role. The separate administrator run timeline and workload view is opt-in and has a bounded time window; it is not an exhaustive audit stream.

This screenshot illustrates an existing product view. It is not evidence of your tenant's current activity or a measured delivery guarantee.

Investigate a task end to end

  1. Find the run/case reference and timestamp.
  2. Confirm the tenant/company context and initiating identity.
  3. Inspect the agent and prompt/model version where recorded.
  4. Read tool outcomes and safe failure/refusal reasons.
  5. Verify citations, provider timestamps and missing evidence.
  6. Inspect approval or case-decision authority separately.
  7. Check the system-of-record outcome for any external action.

Do not infer that an absent event means no action occurred. Confirm the view's scope and whether the event writer for that path is implemented.

Understand screen limits

Dashboard Recent Activity and Observatory read audit history. Observatory polls the newest 20 rows every five seconds and labels that scope. This is not an exhaustive live stream or a full-day activity total. An internal resilient feed exists in the repository. Its only writer is the conversation supervisor console (off by default behind AGENTICORG_CONVERSATION_V2_ENABLED), which announces conversation changes, never message text, for the Conversations screen; no other operational event is published to it, so do not represent it as universal real-time monitoring.

In a tenant that keeps spend rate cards, commitments, invoices, reconciliations or spend jobs, the Audit Log hides those audit rows from every reader who is not a human administrator or auditor, including domain roles and machine credentials, even after spend intelligence is turned off. This is AGENTICORG_SPEND_AUDIT_COMMERCIAL_FILTER, on by default; false shows them to every reader as before. Where the deployment turns on the tamper-evident audit chain (AGENTICORG_AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED, off by default), audit rows are linked into a hash chain, and a reader with audit access can read the chain status and verify the links through GET /api/v1/audit/chain and GET /api/v1/audit/chain/verify.

For governed cases, inspect transitions, memo citations, policy inputs/version, analyst reviews, decision-grant evidence and signed handoff delivery history. The case record can retain stronger lineage than a general activity summary.

Establish operational measures

Choose metrics tied to your task: successful and refused runs, correct answers, missing-source rate, approval age, connector error/latency, OCR review rate, workflow retries and actual downstream outcomes. Record the time window, sample size and workload. Do not turn a sample result into a platform-wide accuracy claim.

Incident workflow

Stop the affected external-action schedule or agent path through supported controls. Preserve safe references, isolate the provider/configuration issue, and ask the accountable operator to investigate. Never paste secrets or full customer records into ordinary issue reports.

Check Service Status and your own deployment health separately. A public service status page cannot certify the health of every tenant connector or self-hosted bank environment.

Next: Run observability, Guardrails, Troubleshooting, Security and data, Evaluation.

articles.title: Guardrail rules, dry runs and enforcement
articles.description: Configure tenant-admin guardrail rules through the authenticated API, test detector behavior, and distinguish flag-only from enforced operation.
articles.html:
Configure and test guardrails

Tenant-scoped rules evaluate text at the input, retrieved-evidence, model-output and tool-action stages. A rule names a detector, threshold, optional agent/use-case/risk-tier scope, priority and response. Detector identifiers are sensitive_data, toxicity, pattern, injection, output_policy and grounding. Action values are flag, mask, redact, tokenise and block; API validation enforces detector/action compatibility.

Tenant administrators manage rules on the Guardrails page. It shows the mode in effect (hooks off, flag-only or enforcing), lists the rules with what each applies to, adds, changes, enables, disables and deletes a rule, and dry-runs a stage over a text. Detector options are edited as JSON, starting from an example for the chosen detector. The page changes rules only; hooks and tenant enforcement are switched on through their own approved controls.

The same operations are available under /api/v1/guardrails to an approved client acting as a tenant administrator and holding governance.guardrails.sensitive.read or .write: GET /status, GET/POST /rules, PATCH/DELETE /rules/{rule_id}, POST /evaluate, GET /adversarial and POST /adversarial/run. Do not copy a privileged key into a browser console or commit it to a script.

  1. 1Check effective status

    Open the Guardrails page and read the banner: hooks off, flag-only or enforcing.

  2. 2Create a narrow rule

    Choose one stage, detector, threshold, response and explicit scope.

  3. 3Dry-run examples

    Use the dry run with synthetic allowed and flagged text; inspect the outcomes and the text after the rules.

  4. 4Review detector limits

    Check false positives, missed cases, latency and failure behavior with the domain owner.

  5. 5Enable only through approved controls

    Confirm hooks and tenant enforcement configuration before relying on blocking or transforms.

  6. 6Monitor and revise

    Correlate rule outcomes with run evidence; keep a rollback owner and test after edits.

Understand the modes

Rules can be stored while platform hooks or enforcement are off. Hooks are disabled by default. With hooks enabled but tenant enforcement off, evaluations are flag-only: the request continues unchanged while findings are recorded for observation. The /evaluate endpoint is a dry run: it returns the result the rules would produce, including transformed text or allowed: false, but does not enforce that result on a live call and does not write an audit outcome. A dry run is therefore not evidence that production traffic is protected.

Enforcement is a separate setting. When active, a matching transform changes the text before it continues, and a blocking rule refuses that stage. A strict runtime may refuse a stage if it cannot safely load rules or a detector fails; behavior depends on the deployed strictness configuration. Confirm the effective status, hook configuration and runtime logs with your platform owner rather than inferring enforcement from the existence of a rule.

Scope and detector behavior

Rules match one of four stages: input, retrieval, output or action. Optional agent_id, use_case and risk_tier fields narrow a rule. Without those fields, the rule can apply to every call at that stage. Rules run in priority order, and a block takes precedence over a transform. Pattern rules are bounded and reject known unsafe regular-expression shapes; keep patterns short, specific and reviewed.

Sensitive-data recognition includes configured patterns for common identifiers such as payment cards, Aadhaar, PAN, GSTIN, email, UPI and phone. Recognition quality depends on the active analyzer and fallback recognizers. Toxicity and prompt-injection detection are signals, not proof of intent or a complete security boundary. A grounding rule (output stage; flag or block) compares each sentence of an answer with what the run retrieved and reports claims, and figures, that the retrieved text does not carry. It is a word-level check, not a judgement of meaning: it catches answers written without the retrieved material, and it can flag a faithful paraphrase. In the dry run, paste the retrieved text as the context. Test representative languages, formats, OCR noise and adversarial inputs. Retain a human review path for high-impact decisions.

Operational checklist

  • Start in flag-only mode with synthetic cases and inspect false positives and misses.
  • Run the adversarial set on the Guardrails page against your rules. It reports, per category, the synthetic attacks your rules detect, the ones they miss and the benign texts they wrongly catch. Some attacks are included because pattern-based detectors miss them, so a score below 100% is expected; the result describes that corpus only.
  • Verify exact tenant, agent, use-case and risk-tier matching, including missing-context behavior.
  • Test each action separately; ensure masks/redactions do not destroy required business context.
  • Verify that blocked input, retrieval, output and tool-action cases stop at the intended boundary.
  • Confirm audit permissions, correlation IDs, retention and incident ownership.
  • Keep a rollback rule/configuration and rerun regression cases after every detector or policy change.

Guardrails do not replace access control, data minimization, provider contracts, connector permissions, human approvals or institution policy. They are one control in a layered system.

Next: Model Gateway, Security and data, Audit and monitoring, Troubleshooting.

articles.title: Run timelines and workload observability
articles.description: Use the admin trace waterfall and tenant workload view, understand opt-in tracing and storage, and investigate run failures without overreading missing data.
articles.html:
Inspect run timelines and workload

The administrator-only Observability screen (/dashboard/observability) has Traces, which lists recent instrumented runs and a span waterfall for one run, and Workload, which summarizes review deadlines and selected tenant outcomes. Traces and Workload are read-only views. Where the deployment turns on synthetic checks (AGENTICORG_SYNTHETIC_CHECKS_ENABLED, off by default), a third Checks tab lists the tenant's scheduled probes with their latest results and lets an administrator add or run one. Where the debugging console is on (AGENTICORG_RUNTIME_DEBUG_CONSOLE_ENABLED, off by default), a run recorded while it was on offers Step through to read its checkpoints one step at a time. They help an operator investigate; they do not replace the audit log, provider billing, a system-of-record check or an incident process.

  1. 1Open Observability

    Sign in as an authorized administrator and select the intended company.

  2. 2Check recording state

    Read the tracing/timeline status before interpreting an empty run list.

  3. 3Find a run

    Filter recent runs by agent, then open one run to inspect parent/child spans and events.

  4. 4Compare workload

    Review pending/overdue reviews and the one-hour run, model-call and guardrail summaries.

  5. 5Follow the correlation

    Use run/correlation identifiers to inspect audit details and the downstream system separately.

Traces and timelines

The list requests up to 50 recent stored runs and can filter by agent ID. A run detail displays its stored spans in relative time order, including duration, parent relationship, status and available attributes/events such as model decisions, tool outcomes, guardrail outcomes and exceptions. Data is limited to what that deployment records; missing spans do not prove that no work occurred.

Before a platform owner changes AGENTICORG_TRACING_ENABLED or AGENTICORG_TRACING_TIMELINE_ENABLED, agree on an approved OTLP endpoint and protocol, sampling, data classification, storage and retention. Both controls default to off; strict production-like environments require a valid exporter endpoint when tracing is enabled. Confirm the effective retention setting with the platform owner before relying on historical timelines. Never send sensitive payloads to an unapproved telemetry collector.

Workload view

Workload refreshes about every 15 seconds. Its run, model-call and guardrail summaries cover the most recent hour. Review counts and deadlines come from the tenant's pending human-review queue. Each panel can report unavailable data independently; a dash or an error means unknown/unavailable, not zero. Model-call summaries depend on model-gateway record capture, and guardrail block/transform counts depend on persisted guardrail audit outcomes.

Use the panel's stated time window and generated time when comparing it with another report. This is not a durable event stream, full audit export, cross-tenant dashboard or service-level guarantee. Do not use it as the sole evidence for a financial, compliance or customer-impact decision.

A practical investigation

  1. Capture the run ID, correlation ID, company, agent and approximate time.
  2. Check whether tracing and timeline storage were enabled during that interval.
  3. Follow span status, duration and error events; identify the earliest failing dependency.
  4. Compare guardrail and model-gateway decisions with the audit view.
  5. Confirm any external action with its authoritative system (for example, the provider or connected business application).
  6. Record the safe error code, deployed commit and remediation owner; do not attach credentials or full customer payloads.

If the view is empty, first verify permissions, selected company, feature configuration, retention window and whether the run path emits timeline spans. See Audit and monitoring, Model Gateway, Guardrails and Security and data.

articles.title: Evaluate and roll out safely
articles.description: Build representative tests, compare quality and cost, validate refusals, and promote a bounded pilot with a rollback plan.
articles.html:
Define success before running tests

Choose the task, owner, expected output, permitted tools, prohibited actions and escalation behavior. Use representative examples, not only a single easy prompt. A confidence percentage, template name or passed unit test does not establish business accuracy.

Build a small reviewed test set

Include normal inputs, incomplete files, conflicting procedures, stale evidence, incorrect company references, provider failures and attempts to request forbidden actions. For OCR, include realistic scans; for voice, include accent/noise and silence; for RPA, include expired sessions and changed selectors.

Dimension Example acceptance question
Grounding Is each material fact supported by an authorized source?
Correctness Does the result match the reviewed answer?
Permissions Are cross-company and ungranted requests refused?
Human control Does consequential work stop at the intended review boundary?
Recovery Are retries bounded and duplicate effects prevented?
Usability Can a second operator reproduce the task without the builder?
Operations Are latency, cost, volume and failure handling acceptable for this workload?

Run candidates in a bounded environment

Create candidates in shadow and restrict tools to reads where possible. Shadow is an evaluation state, not proof of universal side-effect suppression. Inspect actual tool activity. Compare versions with the same test inputs and source content. Record provider/model, prompt and configuration so results are reproducible.

The public Evaluations page describes methodology; use the task's actual evaluation/run evidence for promotion. Jev advisory shadow work has its own access and cost/latency gate and does not replace human authority.

Prompt templates, datasets and the agent catalogue

Administrators manage prompt templates on Prompt Templates. Three panels on that screen appear only where the deployment turns them on, and each is off by default:

Panel Setting What it adds
Changes waiting for approval AGENTICORG_PROMPTS_MAKER_CHECKER, or the tenant flag prompts.maker_checker A template create, change, rollback or delete waits for a second person's approval
Evaluation datasets AGENTICORG_EVALS_V2_ENABLED Versioned tenant datasets that can be run and compared run by run
Compare models AGENTICORG_PROMPT_COMPARE_ENABLED One prompt run against several models side by side; these are real, billed model calls

With AGENTICORG_EVAL_PROMOTION_GATE_ENABLED on (off by default), an agent that declares an evaluation gate is not promoted or resumed to active until its prompt has a stored run on the gate's dataset version that meets the gate's pass rate without regressing beyond its allowance. The Agent Catalogue screen lists each agent's registry card and lifecycle state when the agent registry is on (AGENTICORG_AGENT_REGISTRY_ENABLED, off by default); otherwise it says the registry is off in this deployment.

Move to a limited pilot

Agree users, volume, allowed data, hours, review coverage and rollback triggers. Choose a narrow population and a named support owner. Train operators and reviewers separately. Verify that a non-admin user can complete the documented flow with their own account.

Do not enable a provider/payment/channel action simply because read-only Q&A works. Each external action needs its own account, contract, authority, failure tests and operational evidence.

Expand deliberately

Measure actual results and reopened errors. Correct the shared cause when a bug affects multiple paths, then add regression cases that replay the failing user steps. Re-evaluate after changes to model, prompt, policy, document, connector or target site.

For a bank, the institution's risk, security, privacy and business owners approve rollout under their own process. AgenticOrg does not make a regulatory approval, certification or guaranteed service-level claim on the basis of this checklist.

Next: Team adoption checklist, BFSI onboarding.

  ---   ---   ---

  Evaluation datasets    AGENTICORG_EVALS_V2_ENABLED    Versioned tenant datasets that can be run and compared run by run

articles.title: Security, privacy and data handling
articles.description: Choose appropriate data, review provider retention and access, protect credentials, and organize evidence deletion and incident response.
articles.html:
Start with approved data

Use synthetic records when learning. Before real data, identify the data owner, classification, purpose, allowed model/providers, retention and access. Minimize what each task receives. A document being useful to a model is not permission to upload it.

For BFSI, customer identity, financial, health and account information can require institution-specific controls. This guide explains product boundaries; it is not legal advice or proof of regulatory compliance.

Protect access and credentials

Use named accounts and least-powerful roles. Keep company context explicit. Store provider credentials through the approved protected form, secret manager or connector path; never in prompts, scripts, example files or screenshots.

Review API keys and delegated grants by scope, environment and owner. Rotate and revoke through the appropriate control. A machine credential is not a human session and cannot perform human-only case decisions.

Understand where information goes

Path Review requirement
Model and embedding calls Provider endpoint, permitted data, retention and contractual terms
Knowledge extraction File access, extracted chunks, OCR quality, replacement and deletion
Voice Provider recording/retention, approved number and encrypted bounded text
Calls (speech intelligence, off by default) Encrypted audio and transcript kept per tenant, the transcription engine and speech-provider credential used, spoken-data redaction, and how recordings are removed: the speech routes offer no deletion or retention setting
RPA Approved domains, secret custody and screenshot/log content
Governed cases Cited evidence, encrypted excerpts, decision authority and signed handoff
Commerce Merchant scope, artifact freshness, public-safe projection and provider-owned execution

AgenticOrg's controls do not automatically set the provider's retention or your bank's network configuration. Review those separately.

Settings > Compliance & Data > Data Region records the tenant's region (IN, EU or US). It does not move stored data or change where the hosted service runs. Residency enforcement is off by default. When a platform operator turns it on for the deployment (AGENTICORG_RESIDENCY_ENFORCE=true) or for one tenant (authority flag residency.enforce), any AI or integration provider without an active attestation for that region is refused; providers running inside the deployment need none. Administrators record attestations through /api/v1/residency/attestations. Confirm the deployment's actual regions with your platform owner.

Retention and deletion

Decide who can delete source documents, derived knowledge, retained excerpts and operational evidence. These are not identical resources. Governed-case excerpt deletion can remove retained passages while keeping references/digests and the memo. It does not silently erase every downstream copy or the institution's system-of-record obligation.

Ask the operator to verify backup/restore and erasure procedures in the actual environment. A backup configuration file is not proof that restoration works.

Respond to an incident

Stop affected schedules/actions, revoke compromised credentials, preserve safe references and notify the designated incident owner. Report security issues privately through Support or the repository's security process. Do not open a public issue containing customer documents, tokens or exploitable tenant identifiers.

A useful incident record states time, version, resource/run reference, affected path, observed symptom and mitigation. Keep customer material in the institution's approved evidence system.

Next: Workspace and roles, Audit and monitoring, Self-hosting.

articles.title: Agent security deployment and evidence
articles.description: Map CERT-In guidance to product controls, tenant-owned SSO, run authorization, operator responsibilities and negative acceptance tests.
articles.audience: Tenant administrators, security and deployment operators
articles.html:
Agent Security Deployment And Evidence Guide

Use CERT-In CIAD-2026-0049 and CIAD-2026-0046 as primary references. If a detail page is unavailable, CERT-In's official 2026 advisory index lists the titles and issue dates. Detail-page availability was intermittent when checked on 17 October 2026. This guide does not confer certification, legal compliance, bank approval or permission to conduct a live financial transaction.

Responsibility Boundaries

Tenants configure their own approved SSO/OIDC connections and group mappings; they do not receive platform-operator privileges by controlling an IdP. Require MFA in the tenant IdP's application policy, test non-admin and missing-factor refusals, and record the exact issuer, audience, redirect URI and group mapping. An endpoint-discovery test alone proves none of these. Keep machine credentials and recovery access separately protected. This release does not switch any tenant's MFA policy or platform IAM/IAP configuration on automatically.

AgenticOrg coordinates work, applies configured action/tenant policies and records evidence. Grantex supplies delegated authorization primitives. The operator owns deployment isolation, IAM, network policy, identity-provider MFA, security-log storage and incident response. External systems still enforce their own permissions and business rules. None of these boundaries is replaced by a prompt or a model's confidence score.

Existing inventory records do not automatically discover every deployed agent, API or third-party tool. Reconcile the runtime catalog with cloud assets, service accounts, installed packages, scheduled jobs and external credentials. Record an owner and decommission decision for dormant endpoints and identities.

Separate Run Authorization

The source adds an opt-in control; the compatibility default remains off:

AGENTICORG_GRANTS_ISOLATE_RUN_TOKENS=true
AGENTICORG_GRANTS_ENFORCE_CLOSED=deny
AGENTICORG_GRANTS_RUN_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS=900

When isolation is enabled, the run-grant resolver forces deny mode even if the deployment supplied off or warn. It obtains a delegated grant for a server-created run authorization context rather than sharing the same cache entry across separate contexts. Refresh preserves the isolation key. Governed-case calls in one authorizer share that context; another authorizer receives another key.

A legacy static token in agent configuration no longer substitutes for the run's delegated grant. A supplied external token remains an additional restriction; it does not become a shortcut around fresh run authority. Ambiguous supplied and caller tokens are refused. Missing registration, scopes, root authority, issuer availability or valid delegation prevents authorized tool dispatch.

The root credential must come from a secret manager and the configured registered agent/scopes must be reviewed. Tokens expire; this setting does not automatically revoke a grant the moment a run completes. It does not create a separate OS user, container or cryptographic agent key per run. It also does not bind a JWT to one case ID or enforce case-purpose/cap semantics that the SDK call does not receive. Do not describe this as complete per-case authorization or complete advisory coverage. See the governed-case boundary.

Runtime And Network Isolation

Run evaluations with synthetic targets and credentials in disposable infrastructure. Use a network-enforced default-deny policy and allow only reviewed destinations, ports and protocols. Apply it to API workers, model/tool runtimes, browser or code execution and remote-tool transports, not just the public API container.

The public-URL validator and DNS-pinned transport reject unsafe destinations on the paths that use them. They are not a global firewall and do not prevent an unrelated SDK, shell or connector from opening another socket. Cloud Run VPC routing alone is not an allowlist. Use a reviewed firewall or authenticated egress proxy, and test direct-connect bypass. Keep policy changes, cloud role administration and workload restarts outside the agent's permissions.

Do not hand provider keys to the model or persist them in plaintext workflow state. Use tenant-aware encrypted connector configuration or secret references. If an agent encounters an unexpected credential, stop the run, quarantine that credential through the operator's shared suppression/rotation process and investigate. Do not try it against a real endpoint to establish validity. Masking a secret in logs is not revocation or cross-run quarantine.

Human Authority And Containment

Sensitive actions need an approved policy and authenticated human authority at the backend execution boundary. Separate preparation from approval and execution. For financial work, the maker cannot approve their own action; a payment executor must independently verify the approved record, beneficiary, amount, expiry, replay state and cumulative ceilings. A case recommendation is not activation.

Configure independent operator override and upstream revocation. Verify their effect on active workers, resumed work and cached grants. Do not let the same agent change its scopes, remove its own audit trail or restore its root grant. Human decisions, API-key access and service identities have different purposes; an API key is not MFA. Protect privileged administration through private ingress and an approved MFA-enforcing identity provider. Test the backend origin as well as the public domain.

Monitoring, Retention And Evidence

Centralize security-relevant request and action logs. Retain the applicable security logs for at least 180 days, or longer where another requirement applies. Verify the actual bucket and sink, exclusions, access restrictions and legal holds. A seven-year audit setting does not prove a separate cloud request-log bucket has equivalent retention. Extending a bucket cannot restore expired logs.

Capture actor/run/grant references, tool, destination, port, protocol, timestamp and result at the appropriate boundary; exclude tokens, raw credentials and sensitive payloads. Configure per-second bursts, enumeration, bulk-read and automated-registration alerts, and verify alert receipt. Process-local limits are not a deployment-wide ceiling. Hash-linked evidence still needs protected storage and independent verification; it is not proof that a privileged operator cannot delete a database or bucket.

Operational Control Register

Area Required evidence before an enabled production rollout
Inventory Reconciled agents, tools, APIs, workloads, accounts and owners
Secrets Commit/history/build/config/cloud scan, issuer rotation records, credential suppression across future runs
IAM Least-privilege roles, tenant isolation and anonymous read/write denial tests
Privileged access Private ingress, MFA policy, authorized operator mapping and direct-origin bypass test
Runtime authority Separate run grants, scope attenuation, online revocation and denial under issuer/cache failures
Network Enforcing firewall/CNI/proxy, exact allowlist and denied socket test for every execution runtime
Monitoring Live destination/action telemetry, burst/bulk-read alerts and on-call receipt
Retention Bucket read-back, sink routing, exclusions, evidence integrity and custody
Patching Deployed image digest, middleware/dependency scan and retest
Sensitive decisions Human session, step-up and distinct approver tests; exact action binding
Financial execution Approved references, beneficiaries, ceilings, sequence binding, velocity and reconciliation at the payment API
Response Independent stop, evidence preservation, rotation, root-cause remediation, external retest and reporting assessment

The operator must record verified configuration and test artifacts, not mark rows complete because a feature exists in a repository. Unknown and disabled controls remain open. Never call a sandbox merchant pilot a compliance-approved live release.

Incident And Recovery Procedure

Stop and isolate the affected run without destroying evidence. Preserve original timestamps, relevant logs, image digests, authority identifiers and configuration; restrict access and record custody. Revoke affected grants, rotate credentials at every actual issuer and investigate adjacent accounts and persistence. Patch root causes and replay the original failure plus sibling paths in isolation. Retest externally through an authorized independent party before restoring access. The incident commander and legal/security owners assess applicable reporting obligations using the official CERT-In channels. Do not wait for a framework or identity-verification provider to make that decision for the organization.

Safe Adoption Sequence

Start one synthetic workflow locally, set deny enforcement, register the smallest tool set and test cross-tenant, revoked-grant, missing-approval and denied-egress paths. Add run-token isolation after issuer registration/root permissions are validated. Configure private MFA administration, network enforcement, retention and alerts. Capture evidence and approve a staged rollout with rollback and independent containment. Do not enable a sensitive or live onboarding flow while any of its required gates are unresolved.

articles.title: Billing, limits and support
articles.description: Understand hosted plan limits and provider charges, use the billing console, and send a useful support request without secrets.
articles.html:
Understand separate cost sources

Hosted platform plans and external provider usage are different. Models, embeddings, calls, messaging, merchant systems and payment providers can charge independently. Self-hosting adds your infrastructure and operating costs. Do not assume an economy label means the provider is free for your account.

The approved prospective licensing policy has not been adopted by a software release and does not change current Apache-2.0 rights or hosted/provider charges. Commercial agreement inquiries go to sanjeev@orchestrum.in. Existing and new covered users require a commercialization agreement; an older account is not an exemption. Existing hosted customers transition through the notice and acceptance required by their contracts. Self-use remains free of a software license fee; this does not promise free hosting or providers.

Administrators and CFOs can open the Cost Dashboard at /dashboard/costs (it has no sidebar entry). It sums the platform's own recorded USD cost per task and agent; it is not a provider invoice.

The hosted pricing page is generated from the platform's plan catalog. Use Pricing and Billing in your workspace for current plan information rather than relying on a hard-coded price in a guide.

Review a plan

Compare agent/run/storage allowances, required connector access, identity features, support and deployment needs. Ask the account owner to verify subscription status and currency. A plan upgrade does not configure provider keys or activate every optional feature.

Before a pilot, set a provider budget, expected workload, limits and an alert owner. Start with short tasks and read-only tools. For voice, approve destinations and calling windows; for RPA, avoid unnecessarily frequent schedules.

Billing-console procedure

  1. Open Billing with the account-owner/admin role.
  2. Inspect the current plan and supported subscription/usage controls.
  3. Review the requested change and terms before checkout.
  4. Return from the billing-provider flow and confirm the recorded status.
  5. If status is unclear, check the provider reference and contact support; do not repeatedly submit payment.

Platform subscription billing is separate from OACP buyer payment and merchant mandate execution.

Send an actionable support request

Include the affected screen/flow, safe run/case reference, timestamp and timezone, selected company context, deployed version where available, expected versus actual behavior, and steps to reproduce. State whether the issue is hosted or self-managed and whether it blocks an external action.

Do not include passwords, raw API keys, full account numbers, identity documents or unredacted provider payloads. If evidence is sensitive, arrange the approved private support channel first.

AgenticOrg is owned by Orchestrum Technologies LLP. Inventor / Owner: Sanjeev Kumar. Product contact: sanjeev@orchestrum.in or mishra.sanjeev@gmail.com. Use the published Support, Privacy and Terms pages for current policies.

articles.description: Understand free self-use and commercial agreements for existing and new covered users, prior source rights and the separate software-release adoption boundary.
articles.html:
Status: Approved for policy publication; not adopted by a software release. Legal review approval: Received by owner attestation on 12 October 2026. Prepared: 12 October 2026. No effective date or covered release has been approved.

Short notice

Under this policy: personal and internal use is free; commercializing the platform requires an agreement with Orchestrum Technologies LLP. Agreements: sanjeev@orchestrum.in.

The policy covers existing and new users of covered software and Orchestrum-hosted commercial offerings. An older account is not an exemption. Software adoption awaits the release scope below; existing hosted customers require the contractual transition described below, not a backdated obligation.
