promise that every vendor automatically discovers this seller. Payment and
mandate execution are owned by their fintech/provider; AgenticOrg's current
A2A seller conversation is non-binding.

Next: [Guided seller-to-buyer integration](/docs/seller-a2a-commerce-journey),
[Commerce guide](/docs/commerce), [API and A2A integration](/docs/api-sdk-mcp).

articles.title: Seller commerce with an outside A2A buyer
articles.description: An interactive third-party buyer transaction map and six checkpoints covering merchant setup, A2A seller access, sourced answers and the Pine Labs Plural payment boundary.
articles.html:
What this journey proves

An outside buyer agent can ask an AgenticOrg Seller Commerce Agent about a merchant's products over authenticated A2A v1 HTTP+JSON. The buyer can run in a consumer app such as Muse, Instinct or Dots, or in any other service that can make this A2A request. Those names are examples of possible clients, not claims of a built-in plugin, vendor partnership, verified client identity or automatic discovery.

The working seller question path is non-binding. It can return source-labelled product and inventory snapshots, or refuse. It cannot create an order, hold stock, collect money or create a Pine Labs Plural mandate. A complete paid purchase additionally requires merchant and provider integration, human authorization where required, provider confirmation, order creation and reconciliation. Do not tell a buyer they have purchased until those authoritative confirmations exist.

Who can operate this journey. Merchant staff provide product, source-system and payment-provider approvals. An AgenticOrg tenant administrator performs the protected Runtime Actions, connector credential/sync, artifact issuance, capability verification and outside-buyer access issuance described below. The merchant role can manage merchant configuration, but it cannot perform those admin-only actions. Arrange the administrator handoff before starting the checkpoints.

  1. 1Merchant

    Configure the seller, source system, channel approvals and provider reference in AgenticOrg.

  2. 2Shopify

    Sync the merchant's products, variants, prices and inventory read-only.

  3. 3Grantex

    Issue scoped OACP authority artifacts; AgenticOrg validates and caches them.

  4. 4Buyer app

    Receive merchant-approved access and connect to the A2A v1 seller endpoint.

  5. 5Seller agent

    Answer product questions from fresh cached evidence; refuse purchase execution.

  6. 6Plural/P3P

    Verify capability, then use separately approved provider and merchant paths for real authorization and settlement.

Transaction map: from question to a real sale

The interactive map above lets you select an illustrative buyer app and inspect each message. Its selected app name changes the diagram, not the system integration. The same merchant-scoped A2A rules apply to any external buyer implementation. A consumer app operator must explicitly configure the seller endpoint and protect its merchant-issued credential.

Hop Who talks to whom Buyer-visible outcome Current state
1 Outside buyer to AgenticOrg seller The buyer can discover a generic card and use approved seller access. Available with merchant-scoped credential.
2 Seller to buyer, using cached Shopify/Grantex evidence A product answer includes source and freshness; it is not a final offer. Available, non-binding.
3 Buyer to seller: "buy this" The seller refuses execution and can point to a separate prepared handoff. Available refusal; no order or stock hold.
4 AgenticOrg verifier to Plural/P3P Capability evidence says whether a provider-owned path may be available. Available separately; not a charge or mandate.
5 Buyer to provider authorization The buyer reviews terms and authorizes with an approved provider flow. Requires merchant/provider integration; not wired through the current A2A seller route.
6 Provider outcome to merchant order system The buyer sees confirmed only after payment and order/inventory evidence agree. Requires verified callbacks, merchant execution and reconciliation.

Authority boundary. The third-party buyer agent never needs to live on AgenticOrg. AgenticOrg hosts the seller and maintains the sourced cache; Shopify owns current commercial facts, Grantex governs the canonical artifacts, and Pine Labs Plural/P3P owns payment execution. The diagram is an explanatory journey, not a live checkout simulator.

Checkpoint 1: create the seller

Tenant-admin action. Sign in as a tenant administrator and open Commerce Runtime. In Merchant Commerce Configuration, set the merchant ID, seller agent ID, display name, source connector, allowed buyer channels, and payment provider type plural_pine where appropriate. Save the configuration, then use Create under Runtime Actions to create or update the seller onboarding packet. Merchant staff may supply or separately save configuration with their scoped role, but the tenant administrator must perform Create. Keep Public catalog off until both platform and merchant publishing approvals are in place. A public Agent Card does not publish a merchant catalog.

Pass check. Readiness and the onboarding packet show the intended merchant, seller, tenant and source. Keep separate IDs for separate merchants. The packet is not a transaction authority or provider approval.

Checkpoint 2: bring source facts

Shopify and tenant-admin action. Have the Shopify administrator approve the read-only Admin API access and webhook setup. The AgenticOrg tenant administrator then saves the credential through AgenticOrg's protected custody path in Shopify Connector, inspects Status, and runs Sync. Compare a small sample of product IDs, variants, image URLs, amount/currency and inventory timestamps against Shopify. A webhook signals a possible change; it does not itself prove a fresh snapshot. Other configured ERP or commerce systems need their own validated adapter and must not be treated as Shopify-equivalent by default.

Pass check. The sync reports product/variant counts and a source evidence reference for the correct merchant. Prices and stock remain snapshots, not final offers or reservations. Never paste a Shopify token into an A2A message, documentation page or buyer app.

Checkpoint 3: establish authority

Tenant-admin action. After a successful source sync, select Issue in Runtime Actions to request Grantex OACP authority for that evidence. Confirm the returned artifacts are scoped to this tenant, merchant and seller, have source references, have valid expiry/freshness, and are held in AgenticOrg's cache. Use the OACP commerce guide for the trust and cache model.

Pass check. Buyer-facing answers cite the merchant source and freshness. If Grantex is temporarily unavailable, a still-valid cached artifact can support non-binding Q&A; expired, revoked or mismatched authority must fail closed. AgenticOrg does not send every buyer question through Grantex.

Checkpoint 4: admit an outside buyer

Merchant action. Choose one external buyer-agent integration and agree who operates it. The merchant tenant administrator issues a short-lived, merchant/seller/buyer-scoped credential via POST /api/v1/a2a/commerce/buyer-access. The token is shown only when created. Deliver it through a protected channel to the buyer application's secret store. Never put it in a prompt, source repository, URL, chat transcript or public Agent Card. Give each buyer agent a separate credential so it can be rotated or revoked independently.

Buyer-app action. Configure the AgenticOrg base URL and the A2A v1 HTTP+JSON endpoint. Fetch GET /.well-known/agent-card.json for the generic card, then GET /api/v1/a2a/extendedAgentCard with A2A-Version: 1.0 and the merchant-issued bearer credential for the seller-specific card. Discovering the generic card alone grants no merchant access. The buyer app must explicitly configure the endpoint and credential; AgenticOrg cannot make every consumer app route shoppers here automatically.

POST /api/v1/a2a/commerce/buyer-access
Authorization: Bearer <tenant-admin-credential>
Content-Type: application/json

{"merchant_id":"merchant-123","seller_agent_id":"seller-123","buyer_agent_id":"outside-buyer-123","expires_days":7}

The buyer_agent_id is a merchant-assigned label. Today's server authenticates possession of the issued bearer credential, not the claimed vendor brand. A client calling itself Muse, Instinct or Dots is not automatically a verified client of that company. Consult A2A integration details before making external identity claims.

Checkpoint 5: prove the conversation

Buyer-app action. Send a synchronous text question to POST /api/v1/a2a/message:send. The server derives tenant, merchant, seller and buyer scope from the credential. The client cannot override those values with message metadata. Inspect sourceLabel, freshnessLabel, status, refusalReason, allowedToExecute and nonAuthoritativeForTransaction in the response.

POST /api/v1/a2a/message:send
Authorization: Bearer <merchant-issued-buyer-credential>
Content-Type: application/a2a+json
Accept: application/a2a+json
A2A-Version: 1.0

{"message":{"messageId":"question-123","role":"ROLE_USER","parts":[{"text":"Which canvas tote variants are in the latest snapshot?"}]}}

Pass check. The answer is sourced and time-qualified. A request to buy, hold stock or create a payment is refused. A wrong-merchant request is refused, an expired or revoked credential is rejected, and stale or unsupported facts are not promoted to final commitments. An external buyer credential must not grant catalog-admin, task or other tenant APIs. The current transport is synchronous text; streaming, push notifications, file parts and durable A2A conversations are not claimed.

Run the local external-buyer demo to see a separate Python buyer process browse a synthetic seller and test purchase refusal and credential revocation. That demo proves the wire path, not a Shopify/Plural transaction.

Checkpoint 6: hand off payment

Merchant, provider and tenant-admin action. The merchant and provider set up the Pine Labs Plural/P3P relationship and buyer authorization under the provider's terms. The AgenticOrg tenant administrator configures the provider reference and uses Verify to obtain non-sensitive capability evidence. When the buyer asks to proceed, that administrator can use the separate purchase-preparation path to assemble a bounded, source-aware handoff. This is not the A2A question route and it does not create a mandate or payment.

What a real paid journey still needs. The approved provider path must obtain any required human mandate/payment authorization, return a verified outcome, and reconcile with the merchant's order, inventory and receipt systems. AgenticOrg may show a paid or confirmed state only after the authoritative provider and merchant outcomes agree. If capability is unavailable, consent is absent, a price or stock snapshot changed, or confirmation is missing, show a blocker or pending state rather than success. Plural/Pine capability guide explains the current verifier boundary.

Current boundary. AgenticOrg ships a provider capability verifier and non-executing preparation/reconciliation contracts. It does not ship a completed Plural/P3P payment or mandate through this external A2A seller route. Provider approval, merchant authorization, checkout/order execution and production rollout are separate integration work. Do not use a simulated capability response as proof of a paid transaction.

Operational acceptance before inviting buyer traffic

Check Expected result
Merchant and buyer scope Right seller answers; wrong tenant/merchant/seller cannot read.
Product freshness Source, update time and expiry visible; stale or revoked evidence is refused.
Buyer credential Short expiry, per-client scope, safe storage and immediate revocation test.
Purchase request Refused on A2A Q&A; no order, hold, mandate or payment.
Provider handoff Capability evidence is redacted; real provider and merchant outcomes are required for paid state.
Distribution Each consumer app explicitly configures the A2A endpoint, access and UX. No automatic marketplace listing is implied.

For an external buyer client, begin with the generic card and a protected credential, then validate the scoped card, one product question, a purchase refusal and a revocation. For an actual customer purchase, do not launch until the merchant, provider and channel have completed their own integration and production checks.

articles.title: API, SDK, MCP and A2A integration
articles.description: Connect applications and agent clients with authenticated, scoped APIs; distinguish public discovery from permission to execute.
articles.html:
Choose an integration surface

Use REST/OpenAPI for application contracts, the repository SDKs for client access, MCP for compatible tool clients, and A2A v1 HTTP+JSON for synchronous text between agents after merchant or tenant authorization. Older AgenticOrg A2A-shaped card/task routes are proprietary; they are not the v1 wire contract. The authenticated A2A / MCP screen shows integration material. Public discovery does not grant access to business data or actions. See external A2A buyer access.

Surface Suitable first task Boundary
REST/OpenAPI Inspect a resource with an approved credential Deployed API/schema is the contract
Python/TypeScript SDK Company-scoped read or bounded agent run Installed client version may differ from repository source
MCP stdio adapter List agents/tools in a compatible local client Client transport support and scopes are still required
A2A v1 HTTP+JSON Read generic card, obtain scoped credential, send synchronous text Merchant buyer credential permits non-binding seller Q&A only
Commerce bridges Read merchant artifacts and prepare handoffs Channel approval and provider execution remain separate

Authenticate and preserve context

Use a credential issued for the reviewed deployment and minimum scopes. Keep it in environment/secret storage. Supply authorized company context for execution paths that require it. Never accept a company ID from untrusted model content without server-side authorization.

Route scope checks apply to every credential, Grantex agent tokens included, on the route families that have a scope mapping (SCOPE_FAMILIES in api/route_enforcement.py), such as agents, chat, workflows, approvals, audit, connectors, documents, speech, transactions, lineage, spend and content; the A2A and MCP families join them only while their switch is on (see below). On a mapped family an agent token needs the family's scope (for example agents:read or audit:read) or agenticorg:admin, or it gets 403. Other route families, knowledge among them, have no scope mapping yet: there, any authenticated credential of the tenant passes the scope check, API keys and agent tokens are not limited to a domain, and only the route's own checks, such as an administrator requirement, apply. Issue machine credentials with that boundary in mind. A tenant administrator signed in as a person grants an agent route scopes with PATCH /api/v1/agents/{id} and {"route_scopes": [...]}, on a shared agent registered on Grantex. Only canonical route-family scopes are accepted there, never agenticorg:admin (422). Administrator access is the exact scope agenticorg:admin; a look-alike such as agenticorg:admin:full is not an administrator.

Obtain a workspace API key

An authorized administrator opens Settings > API Keys. Enter a meaningful Key Name, choose Expires In, then select Generate Key. A short-lived key is preferable for a first integration exercise. The secret is displayed only once; place it in approved secret storage rather than a shared document. The key table shows its prefix, status, last-used time and creation time. Use Revoke for an unused or compromised key and confirm the client can no longer authenticate.

The current form does not offer a custom per-key scope editor. A named key is not inherently a narrowly scoped business grant. Review server-side credential permissions and use the appropriate delegated-grant path when action-level authority is required. Human case decisions require the named approver's authenticated session; an admin key must not substitute for it.

The Python SDK supports an API key or delegated grant. Example of a read-oriented client:

import os
from agenticorg import AgenticOrg

client = AgenticOrg(
    api_key=os.environ["AGENTICORG_API_KEY"],
    base_url=os.environ["AGENTICORG_BASE_URL"],
)
agents = client.agents.list()

Pin the reviewed Python agenticorg==0.4.0 or TypeScript agenticorg-sdk@0.4.0 release after checking registry availability. These versions include the runtime resources, A2A v1 seller access and machine-safe case methods absent from 0.3.0. The MCP adapter release target is agenticorg-mcp-server@5.0.0; its execution and SOP submission tools require company_id. Verify publication, installed version and backend deployment separately; a repository merge alone does not update an installed client.

Connect MCP

There are two directions. The repository MCP adapter exposes AgenticOrg to external clients. Connectors > Remote MCP instead lets an AgenticOrg agent consume a tenant-owned external server through authenticated Streamable HTTP. Follow the remote connector setup and verification workflow; generic connector registration does not discover remote tools. The incoming path supports bearer authentication and reviewed read execution, not arbitrary write execution.

Use the repository MCP adapter with a client that supports its stdio transport. Configure AGENTICORG_BASE_URL and one accepted authentication value: AGENTICORG_API_KEY or AGENTICORG_GRANTEX_TOKEN. Use the client's secure configuration mechanism instead of committing a key in JSON.

The adapter's execution/SOP-submission tools require company_id. Its run_agent path goes through A2A. Scope checks on the A2A and MCP routes are off by default (AGENTICORG_ROUTE_SCOPE_A2A_MCP). While the setting is off, any authenticated credential reaches POST /api/v1/a2a/tasks, GET /api/v1/a2a/tasks/{id} and POST /api/v1/mcp/call; when it is on, those routes need a2a:read, a2a:write or mcp:write (or agenticorg:admin). Administrators must evaluate and configure it, not assume every discovery route is protected identically.

The seller.* tools read cached commerce artifacts; they do not authorize payment, orders or holds. Governed-case human decisions have no shortcut through the machine-authenticated MCP adapter.

Integration acceptance test

  1. Pin a reviewed SDK/adapter version and endpoint.
  2. Make a bounded permitted read.
  3. Test missing/expired credentials and an insufficient scope.
  4. Test cross-company access refusal.
  5. Inspect error shapes, retry behavior and rate limits.
  6. Prove any external action separately with authoritative confirmation.

A generic MCP bridge is not a universal buyer plugin or marketplace approval. Check the current client/provider documentation before enabling a production surface.

An external A2A buyer agent needs a credential issued by the merchant's tenant admin. This is a bearer capability, not proof that the client belongs to a named third-party vendor. Revocation, artifact freshness, and tenant/merchant binding are checked by the server on each request. No purchase is executed by the synchronous A2A message path.

For a working external client and a temporary synthetic seller catalog, follow the local A2A demo. The buyer process imports no AgenticOrg runtime code and exercises discovery, sourced questions, purchase refusal, and revocation over HTTP.

  REST/OpenAPI   Inspect a resource with an approved credential   Deployed API/schema is the contract  
  Python/TypeScript SDK   Company-scoped read or bounded agent run   Installed client version may differ from repository source  
  MCP stdio adapter   List agents/tools in a compatible local client   Client transport support and scopes are still required  
  A2A v1 HTTP+JSON   Read generic card, obtain scoped credential, send synchronous text   Merchant buyer credential permits non-binding seller Q&A only  
  Commerce bridges   Read merchant artifacts and prepare handoffs   Channel approval and provider execution remain separate  

   Authenticate and preserve context

Use a credential issued for the reviewed deployment and minimum scopes. Keep it in environment/secret storage. Supply authorized company context for execution paths that require it. Never accept a company ID from untrusted model content without server-side authorization.

Route scope checks apply to every credential, Grantex agent tokens included, on the route families that have a scope mapping ( SCOPE_FAMILIES  in  api/route_enforcement.py ), such as agents, chat, workflows, approvals, audit, connectors, documents, speech, transactions, lineage, spend and content; the A2A and MCP families join them only while their switch is on (see below). On a mapped family an agent token needs the family's scope (for example  agents:read  or  audit:read ) or  agenticorg:admin , or it gets  403 . Other route families, knowledge among them, have no scope mapping yet: there, any authenticated credential of the tenant passes the scope check, API keys and agent tokens are not limited to a domain, and only the route's own checks, such as an administrator requirement, apply. Issue machine credentials with that boundary in mind. A tenant administrator signed in as a person grants an agent route scopes with  PATCH /api/v1/agents/{id}  and  {"route_scopes": [...]} , on a shared agent registered on Grantex. Only canonical route-family scopes are accepted there, never  agenticorg:admin  ( 422 ). Administrator access is the exact scope  agenticorg:admin ; a look-alike such as  agenticorg:admin:full  is not an administrator.

    Obtain a workspace API key

An authorized administrator opens   Settings > API Keys  . Enter a meaningful
  Key Name  , choose   Expires In  , then select   Generate Key  . A short-lived
key is preferable for a first integration exercise. The secret is displayed
only once; place it in approved secret storage rather than a shared document.
The key table shows its prefix, status, last-used time and creation time. Use
  Revoke   for an unused or compromised key and confirm the client can no longer
authenticate.

The current form does not offer a custom per-key scope editor. A named key is
not inherently a narrowly scoped business grant. Review server-side credential
permissions and use the appropriate delegated-grant path when action-level
authority is required. Human case decisions require the named approver's
authenticated session; an admin key must not substitute for it.

The Python SDK supports an API key or delegated grant. Example of a read-oriented client:

 import os
from agenticorg import AgenticOrg

client = AgenticOrg(
    api_key=os.environ["AGENTICORG_API_KEY"],
    base_url=os.environ["AGENTICORG_BASE_URL"],
)
agents = client.agents.list()
 
Pin the reviewed Python  agenticorg==0.4.0  or TypeScript
 agenticorg-sdk@0.4.0  release after checking registry availability. These
versions include the runtime resources, A2A v1 seller access and machine-safe
case methods absent from  0.3.0 . The MCP adapter release target is
 agenticorg-mcp-server@5.0.0 ; its execution and SOP submission tools require
 company_id . Verify publication, installed version and backend deployment
separately; a repository merge alone does not update an installed client.

   Connect MCP

There are two directions. The repository MCP adapter exposes AgenticOrg to external
clients.   Connectors > Remote MCP   instead lets an AgenticOrg agent consume a
tenant-owned external server through authenticated Streamable HTTP. Follow the
[remote connector setup and verification workflow](/docs/connectors); generic
connector registration does not discover remote tools. The incoming path supports
bearer authentication and reviewed read execution, not arbitrary write execution.

Use the repository MCP adapter with a client that supports its stdio transport. Configure  AGENTICORG_BASE_URL  and one accepted authentication value:  AGENTICORG_API_KEY  or  AGENTICORG_GRANTEX_TOKEN . Use the client's secure configuration mechanism instead of committing a key in JSON.

The adapter's execution/SOP-submission tools require  company_id . Its  run_agent  path goes through A2A. Scope checks on the A2A and MCP routes are off by default ( AGENTICORG_ROUTE_SCOPE_A2A_MCP ). While the setting is off, any authenticated credential reaches  POST /api/v1/a2a/tasks ,  GET /api/v1/a2a/tasks/{id}  and  POST /api/v1/mcp/call ; when it is on, those routes need  a2a:read ,  a2a:write  or  mcp:write  (or  agenticorg:admin ). Administrators must evaluate and configure it, not assume every discovery route is protected identically.

The  seller.   tools read cached commerce artifacts; they do not authorize payment, orders or holds. Governed-case human decisions have no shortcut through the machine-authenticated MCP adapter.

   Integration acceptance test

1. Pin a reviewed SDK/adapter version and endpoint.
2. Make a bounded permitted read.
3. Test missing/expired credentials and an insufficient scope.
4. Test cross-company access refusal.
5. Inspect error shapes, retry behavior and rate limits.
6. Prove any external action separately with authoritative confirmation.

A generic MCP bridge is not a universal buyer plugin or marketplace approval. Check the current client/provider documentation before enabling a production surface.

An external A2A buyer agent needs a credential issued by the merchant's tenant
admin. This is a bearer capability, not proof that the client belongs to a
named third-party vendor. Revocation, artifact freshness, and tenant/merchant
binding are checked by the server on each request. No purchase is executed by
the synchronous A2A message path.

For a working external client and a temporary synthetic seller catalog, follow
the [local A2A demo](/docs/external-buyer-a2a-demo). The buyer process imports
no AgenticOrg runtime code and exercises discovery, sourced questions, purchase
refusal, and revocation over HTTP.

articles.title: Self-hosting and deployment handoff
articles.description: Understand hosted versus bank-managed operation, local Docker setup, migration-first releases, backups and operational responsibilities.
articles.html:
Hosted versus institution-managed

The hosted workspace and a self-managed deployment share product concepts, but operational responsibilities differ. A bank-managed environment must own network, identities, keys, database, backups, model/provider access, workers, updates, security monitoring and recovery. Self-hosting alone does not establish regulatory compliance or data residency.

For most business users, use the approved hosted or institution-provided URL. This guide is for IT/platform teams, not a requirement before completing Your first agent.

Local learning environment

The repository provides a Docker Compose development stack and GNU Make targets. With reviewed prerequisites installed:

git clone https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org.git
cd agentic-org
make dev
make seed

The current local quickstart binds the console to http://127.0.0.1:3000 and API to http://127.0.0.1:8000. It includes local data services and development verification, identity and model stubs. The default fake/scripted model responses are explicitly synthetic; this environment does not prove a real provider, bank integration or customer transaction.

Use make ps for service status, make logs for logs, make test/make check for repository checks and make e2e for browser tests. make down preserves data; make clean deletes development volumes. Do not run destructive cleanup against a production environment.

Prepare production separately

Responsibility Required decision/evidence
Identity Named users, role/scope model, SSO/SCIM where configured
Network Approved ingress/egress, TLS, provider endpoints and private access
Database PostgreSQL/pgvector, tenant isolation, migrations, backup/restore proof
Runtime API/UI, Redis, workers/schedulers, OCR and browser dependencies
Models Allowed endpoints, credentials, retention, cost and region
Integrations Bank/provider contracts, scopes, test accounts and ownership
Operations Monitoring, alert ownership, capacity tests and rollback

Do not copy development placeholder secrets, fake-model flags or seed identities into production. Air-gapped deployment has additional dependency/model/image and outbound-integration limits; review the operator guide before promising disconnected capability.

Feature switches that ship off

The main feature switches that default to off are listed below; core/config.py lists every setting. A setting that is off leaves the earlier behaviour in place. Some also have a per-tenant flag, shown in parentheses. These are authority flags managed by the platform operator, except prompts.maker_checker, which a tenant admin can set. Set a switch the same way on every service of the deployment, and treat turning one on as a change to plan, test and record like a release.

Setting What it turns on
AGENTICORG_MODEL_GATEWAY_ENABLED (model_gateway.enabled) Routing and access policies and per-model limits on live model calls
AGENTICORG_MODEL_GATEWAY_RECORDS_ENABLED A signed routing record for each gateway-routed model call
AGENTICORG_GUARDRAILS_HOOKS_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_GUARDRAILS_ENFORCE (guardrails.enforce) Guardrail evaluation at every stage, then enforcement instead of flag-only
AGENTICORG_OPERATOR_OVERRIDE_ENABLED (operator_override.enabled) Halting or throttling a model, agent, workflow or the tool pipeline
AGENTICORG_RESIDENCY_ENFORCE (residency.enforce) Refusing providers without an attestation for the tenant's data region
AGENTICORG_TRACING_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_TRACING_TIMELINE_ENABLED OpenTelemetry spans and stored run timelines
AGENTICORG_SYNTHETIC_CHECKS_ENABLED The scheduled synthetic-check sweep and the Observability Checks tab
AGENTICORG_AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED Linking audit rows into a tamper-evident hash chain
AGENTICORG_RUNTIME_LIMITS_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_RUNTIME_MEMORY_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_TOOL_REGISTRY_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_RUNTIME_DEBUG_CONSOLE_ENABLED Per-agent run limits and loop detection, long-term memory, tool schema checks and the step-through debugger
AGENTICORG_WORKFLOW_BUILDER_V2_ENABLED The Build visually tab and definition checks on save
AGENTICORG_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_ENFORCED, AGENTICORG_CONTEXT_WINDOW_MANAGED, AGENTICORG_PROMPT_TYPED_PARAMETERS_ENABLED Checking an agent's final answer against its output schema, with escalation to a person when it stays invalid; leaving older tool results out of a conversation that does not fit the model's window; typed prompt parameters
AGENTICORG_PROMPTS_MAKER_CHECKER (prompts.maker_checker), AGENTICORG_PROMPT_COMPARE_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_EVALS_V2_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_EVAL_PROMOTION_GATE_ENABLED Prompt maker-checker, model comparison, evaluation datasets and the promotion gate
AGENTICORG_AGENT_REGISTRY_ENABLED Agent registry cards, lifecycle states and the Agent Catalogue
AGENTICORG_GOVERNANCE_INVENTORY_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_GOVERNANCE_MODEL_CARDS_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_GOVERNANCE_RISK_TIERS_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_GOVERNANCE_POLICY_CONSOLE_ENABLED AI asset inventory, model cards, risk tiers and the policy console
AGENTICORG_FINOPS_ATTRIBUTION_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_FINOPS_THRESHOLDS_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_FINOPS_FORECAST_ENABLED Use-case cost attribution, thresholds that alert, throttle or suspend runs (they need attribution on), and forecasts
AGENTICORG_SPEND_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED AI spend intelligence
AGENTICORG_KNOWLEDGE_HYBRID_SEARCH, AGENTICORG_KNOWLEDGE_RERANK_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_KNOWLEDGE_QUERY_TRANSFORM_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED Additional knowledge retrieval stages
AGENTICORG_CONVERSATION_V2_ENABLED Banking intents and earlier-turn context in chat, and the Conversations screen
AGENTICORG_CUSTOMER_AGENT_ENABLED The bank-operated customer agent: customer sessions, the autonomy ladder, cards, the permissions page and the embeddable element
AGENTICORG_GRANTEX_REVOCATION_CHECK=feed Refusing grant tokens the authority service has revoked, read from its revocation feed, before they are honoured
AGENTICORG_CONTENT_SERVICES_ENABLED Governed drafting, summarisation and extraction APIs
AGENTICORG_IDP_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_WORKBENCH_V2_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_SPEECH_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_TRANSACTION_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED, AGENTICORG_LINEAGE_ENABLED Document processing, workbenches, call recordings, transaction findings and lineage, with their screens
AGENTICORG_PERSONALISATION_ENABLED Consent-checked personalisation
AGENTICORG_PAUSED_AGENTS_REFUSED Refusing runs, chats and workflow steps for paused agents
AGENTICORG_ROUTE_SCOPE_A2A_MCP Scope checks on the A2A task and MCP call routes

Release handoff

Use the repository's reviewed deployment path and migration-first process. Strict (non-local) runtimes make no schema changes at start-up and refuse to start unless the database is at the migration head the build carries, so apply migrations before the release that needs them. Verify exact commit, migration completion, API/UI revisions, traffic, health, database/Redis and required CI. Then test the institution's actual authorized flow with approved synthetic data. A successful build is not a completed deployment or provider canary.

User documentation domain

The public user manual is available under /docs in the UI build. docs.agenticorg.ai should be a DNS subdomain, not a separate nameserver delegation by default. Hosting/TLS must route that hostname to the reviewed UI/static documentation service before publishing the link. The repository's documentation-domain runbook explains the release checks and ownership; no DNS change is made by reading this guide.

articles.title: What OACP is and why you need it
articles.description: OACP is one trust layer under UCP, ACP, AP2, Visa TAP, MCP and A2A: your facts stated once, signed, decided by fixed rules and recorded, then rendered into each standard.
articles.html:
In 30 seconds

  • AI shopping agents use several standards: UCP, ACP, AP2, Visa TAP, Mastercard Agent Pay, Web Bot Auth, MCP and A2A.
  • Wiring each one on its own leaves you with several copies of your prices, rules and logs.
  • OACP is one trust layer underneath them. You state your facts once, Grantex signs them, and AgenticOrg checks, decides and records.
  • Each standard then receives the same facts in its own format. Revoke a fact once and every channel stops using it.
  • OACP feeds the standards. It does not replace them, and it is not a certification.

The short version

OACP stands for Open Agentic Commerce Protocol.

It is a safety layer for selling to AI agents. It sits under the agent standards you already hear about. It does not compete with them.

Think of it as one source of truth for your shop. Every agent channel reads from it. Every purchase passes through the same rules. Every decision lands in the same record.

Why sellers need it

AI agents now shop for people. One agent compares prices. Another fills a cart. A third pays.

Each of those steps has its own standard. If you connect to each standard separately, four problems appear:

  • Many sources of truth. A price changes in one feed but not another.
  • Many trust set-ups. Each integration has its own keys and its own checks.
  • Many logs. Nobody can show one clean record of what happened.
  • No common off switch. Pull a product in one place and an agent can still buy it somewhere else.

OACP fixes these by putting one layer underneath. You keep your facts in one place. Every channel reads the same signed copy.

The standards, in one line each

You do not need to learn these. OACP renders into them for you.

Standard What it answers What OACP gives it
UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol) Where is the shop, what does it sell, how do I check out? Your business profile, catalog, checkout and orders
ACP (Agentic Commerce Protocol) Which products can an agent buy, and how? A product feed and agent checkout sessions
AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol) What did the buyer allow the agent to spend? Intent, Cart and Payment mandates, mapped to AP2 field names
Visa TAP and Web Bot Auth Which agent is calling, and is it really that agent? Signature checks on agent requests
Mastercard Agent Pay Which card-network agent id does this agent have? The scheme label, recorded from the registry (its wire details are not public)
MCP and A2A How do agents and tools talk to each other? Checkout tools for MCP clients and a seller agent for A2A

What OACP actually is

OACP is three things working together:

  1. Signed facts. Your catalog, prices, stock and policies become small signed records. Grantex signs them. Each one has an expiry date and a revocation slot.
  2. One decision before money moves. A fixed rule set, called the arbiter, says allow or refuse. No allow, no payment.
  3. One record. Every decision and every commerce write is recorded in a signed ledger you can export and check.

Adapters then render those facts into each standard's own format.

Who does what

  1. 1Your shop

    Stays the source of truth for products, prices, stock and orders. Shopify is the supported source today.

  2. 2Grantex

    Signs your facts, publishes the signing keys, runs the revocation list and issues buyer mandates.

  3. 3AgenticOrg

    Checks every signature, decides each purchase with fixed rules, records it and speaks each standard.

  4. 4Payment provider

    Moves money, and only after an allow decision. Plural is the rail built today.

What OACP is not

Honesty matters here, so here is the plain list.

  • Not a replacement. OACP renders into UCP, ACP and AP2. Buyer agents still speak those standards.
  • Not a certification. The groups behind UCP, ACP, AP2 and TAP have not certified or endorsed OACP.
  • Not regulatory approval. OACP helps you keep evidence. It does not establish regulatory compliance on its own.
  • Not AP2's own format. Mandates are signed JWTs that use AP2 field names, not AP2's SD-JWT format. Passkey signing of the cart is a Grantex extension.
  • Not switched on by default. Checkout, payment, mandates and public discovery each sit behind a switch that starts off. See feature switches.

Read next

  • How OACP works, end to end
  • A purchase, step by step
  • Merchant setup checklist
  • The blog post OACP explained: one trust layer under UCP, ACP and AP2
  • The technical reference: OACP runtime docs

  Mastercard Agent Pay   Which card-network agent id does this agent have?   The scheme label, recorded from the registry (its wire details are not public)  
  MCP and A2A   How do agents and tools talk to each other?   Checkout tools for MCP clients and a seller agent for A2A  

Figure: Each standard answers one question. Discovery, checkout, payment permission and agent identity each have their own standard. OACP sits underneath and feeds all of them from the same signed facts.

   What OACP actually is

OACP is three things working together:

1.   Signed facts.   Your catalog, prices, stock and policies become small signed records. Grantex signs them. Each one has an expiry date and a revocation slot.
2.   One decision before money moves.   A fixed rule set, called the arbiter, says allow or refuse. No allow, no payment.
3.   One record.   Every decision and every commerce write is recorded in a signed ledger you can export and check.

Adapters then render those facts into each standard's own format.

   Who does what

 Your shop   Stays the source of truth for products, prices, stock and orders. Shopify is the supported source today.
Grantex   Signs your facts, publishes the signing keys, runs the revocation list and issues buyer mandates.
AgenticOrg   Checks every signature, decides each purchase with fixed rules, records it and speaks each standard.
Payment provider   Moves money, and only after an allow decision. Plural is the rail built today.
 
   What OACP is not

Honesty matters here, so here is the plain list.

-   Not a replacement.   OACP renders into UCP, ACP and AP2. Buyer agents still speak those standards.
-   Not a certification.   The groups behind UCP, ACP, AP2 and TAP have not certified or endorsed OACP.
-   Not regulatory approval.   OACP helps you keep evidence. It does not establish regulatory compliance on its own.
-   Not AP2's own format.   Mandates are signed JWTs that use AP2 field names, not AP2's SD-JWT format. Passkey signing of the cart is a Grantex extension.
-   Not switched on by default.   Checkout, payment, mandates and public discovery each sit behind a switch that starts off. See [feature switches](/docs/oacp-feature-switches).

   Read next

- [How OACP works, end to end](/docs/oacp-how-it-works)
- [A purchase, step by step](/docs/oacp-buyer-journey)
- [Merchant setup checklist](/docs/oacp-merchant-setup)
- The blog post [OACP explained: one trust layer under UCP, ACP and AP2](https://agenticorg.ai/blog/oacp-one-trust-layer-under-ucp-acp-ap2)
- The technical reference: [OACP runtime docs](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/README.md)

articles.description: Follow your shop's facts through seven steps: signed by Grantex, verified and kept by AgenticOrg, decided by the arbiter, recorded in the ledger and rendered for every buyer agent.
articles.html:
In 30 seconds

  • Your shop's facts travel through seven steps before an agent sees them.
  • The shop states the facts. Grantex signs them. AgenticOrg checks every signature before it keeps a copy.
  • When an agent wants to buy, the arbiter applies fixed rules and answers allow or refuse at once. Nobody waits for a person.
  • Every decision is recorded in the commerce ledger. Adapters then speak each standard, so every agent gets the same answer.
  • A payment runs only after an allow decision, and only once.

The whole flow on one page

Each step has one owner. The next sections explain them one at a time.

Step 1. Your shop states its facts

Your shop already knows its products, prices, stock and policies. AgenticOrg reads them. It does not invent them.

  • Shopify is the supported source today. AgenticOrg reads it with read-only access.
  • Your merchant settings add the rest: limits, stores, payment rail and policies.
  • Other systems (WooCommerce, ERP, PIM and others) can be saved as settings. They stay "pending adapter" and are never called.

Step 2. Grantex signs each fact

AgenticOrg sends the facts to Grantex and asks for authority. Grantex turns each fact into a signed record, called an artifact.

Every artifact carries:

  • a signature (ES256) over the exact content;
  • an expiry time, so old facts stop counting;
  • a slot on a public revocation list, so a fact can be withdrawn.

Grantex publishes the keys that check these signatures, and the revocation list. Anyone can check an artifact with those two public things.

Step 3. AgenticOrg checks before it keeps anything

AgenticOrg verifies every artifact before it stores a copy. This is the most important safety step.

In production, staging and preview, one failed artifact means nothing from that batch is kept. This is called strict mode, and it is on by default there.

Step 4. The arbiter decides

When an agent wants to buy, the arbiter decides. It is a fixed set of rules, not a person.

  • It answers allow or refuse. It never answers "pending".
  • An allow is single use. It is bound to the exact cart, price and quantity, and it expires after 10 minutes.
  • A refusal names the first rule that failed, so you know exactly why.

The rules are listed in plain words in Safety and trust.

Step 5. The ledger records it

Every commerce write and every decision is written to the commerce ledger in the same database transaction.

  • Each row is signed.
  • When audit-chain sealing is on, rows are also linked into a hash chain, so a removed or edited row shows up.
  • You can export the ledger and check it on your own computer with scripts/verify_ledger.py.

Sealing and outside witnessing are separate switches. Both start off.

Step 6. Adapters speak each standard

The same verified facts are rendered into each standard's own shape:

  • a UCP business profile at /.well-known/ucp, with catalog, checkout and orders;
  • an ACP product feed and ACP checkout sessions;
  • Intent, Cart and Payment mandates with AP2 field names;
  • checkout tools for MCP clients, and a seller agent for A2A.

Each surface has its own switch, so you can turn on one channel at a time.

Step 7. Buyer agents get the same answer

Because every channel reads the same signed facts, agents see the same price, the same stock and the same refusals. A payment provider moves money only after an allow decision, and only once.

Who does what, at a glance

  1. 1
    States the factsOwner: Merchant

    Products, prices, stock and policies come from your shop.

    Blocked / exception

    Reconnect Shopify or fix the merchant settings, then sync again.

  2. 2
    Signs the factsOwner: Grantex

    Each fact becomes a signed, expiring, revocable artifact.

    Blocked / exception

    AgenticOrg keeps nothing new and asks for a fresh request.

  3. 3
    Verifies and keepsOwner: AgenticOrg

    Signature, key, scope, expiry and revocation are checked before storing.

    Blocked / exception

    The batch is refused with the exact refusal code.

  4. 4
    DecidesOwner: AgenticOrg arbiter

    Fixed rules answer allow or refuse at once.

    Blocked / exception

    The refusal names the first failing rule.

  5. 5
    RecordsOwner: AgenticOrg ledger

    The decision and every commerce write go to the ledger.

    Blocked / exception

    A write route that skips its ledger row is answered as an error.

  6. 6
    PaysOwner: Payment provider

    The provider charges once, against a consumed allow decision.

    Blocked / exception

    Without a registered executor, checkout stops at executor_unavailable.

Where to go deeper

  • A purchase, step by step
  • Safety and trust
  • Technical references: artifact cache guide and arbiter and ledger

articles.description: Walk through one agent purchase: Intent, Cart and Payment mandates, the buyer's passkey, RBI AFA for UPI AutoPay, the arbiter's decision, the payment and the order.
articles.html:
In 30 seconds

  • A buyer's agent finds a product, opens a checkout and asks to complete it.
  • Grantex issues three mandates: Intent (what the buyer allowed), Cart (this exact cart) and Payment (this amount, on this rail).
  • When the buyer is present, their passkey signs the exact cart. In India, a UPI AutoPay payment also needs the buyer's RBI AFA step.
  • AgenticOrg checks the mandates itself, then the arbiter says allow or refuse at once.
  • Only an allow lets the payment provider charge, once. Everything lands in the ledger.

The journey in one picture

The example uses a synthetic shop, Merchant Example, and a buyer who allows up to ₹2,000.

The three mandates, in plain words

A mandate is a signed note of what the buyer allowed. Grantex issues all three. Each lives at most 10 minutes.

Mandate Plain meaning Example
Intent "My agent may spend up to this much, at these shops." Up to ₹2,000 at Merchant Example
Cart "This exact cart, and nothing else." One office tote, ₹1,499, by its hash
Payment "Charge this amount, on this rail, to this token." ₹1,499 by card token on Plural

The Cart mandate binds the cart by a hash. Change one item or one price and the hash changes, so the mandate no longer matches.

The Payment mandate never holds the card or UPI token itself. It holds a fingerprint of it.

Step by step: who does what

  1. 1
    Find the productOwner: Buyer agent

    The buyer agent reads the shop's catalog through UCP or the ACP feed. Prices and stock come from verified facts.

    Blocked / exception

    Without fresh verified facts the catalog answers with no products.

  2. 2
    Open a checkoutOwner: Buyer agent and AgenticOrg

    The agent creates a checkout session. AgenticOrg prices it from the synced catalog and moves it to ready_for_complete.

    Blocked / exception

    An unknown or out-of-stock item keeps the session incomplete.

  3. 3
    Intent mandateOwner: Grantex

    Grantex records what the buyer allowed: the description, the spending cap and the shops.

    Blocked / exception

    Grantex refuses when the buyer's passport cap or consent does not allow it.

  4. 4
    Cart mandate and passkeyOwner: Buyer and Grantex

    Grantex binds the exact cart. When the buyer is present, the buyer's passkey on their own device signs the cart hash.

    Blocked / exception

    A missing, wrong or replayed passkey signature refuses the cart.

  5. 5
    Payment mandateOwner: Grantex

    Grantex binds the amount, the currency, the rail and a fingerprint of the payment token.

    Blocked / exception

    Card data in the request, or an unknown rail, is refused.

  6. 6
    AgenticOrg verifiesOwner: AgenticOrg

    AgenticOrg checks all three signatures, the revocation list and that the chain links to this exact checkout.

    Blocked / exception

    Any failed check stops the purchase with its refusal code.

  7. 7
    Arbiter decidesOwner: AgenticOrg arbiter

    Eight fixed rules run in order. The answer is allow or refuse, at once.

    Blocked / exception

    The first failing rule is the reason, and it is recorded.

  8. 8
    RBI AFA, India onlyOwner: Buyer and their bank

    A UPI AutoPay payment needs the buyer to approve with their UPI PIN in their own UPI app. AgenticOrg returns that step and waits for nothing.

    Blocked / exception

    Completion is refused until verified AFA evidence arrives from the provider.

  9. 9
    PaymentOwner: Payment provider

    The payment provider charges once, against the consumed allow decision. The three mandate hashes travel with the order.

    Blocked / exception

    With payment execution off, checkout stops at executor_unavailable and nothing is charged.

  10. 10
    Order and receiptOwner: AgenticOrg and the merchant

    The order is created and a signed order update goes to the agent platform. The ledger holds the mandates, the decision and every payment call.

    Blocked / exception

    A failed payment returns the session to ready_for_complete.

What the decision can say

When the buyer is not present

Sometimes an agent buys while the person is away. This is called "human not present".

  • There is no passkey step, because nobody is there to touch it.
  • The shop must set stricter limits for these purchases, for example a lower amount cap. Without them, every not-present purchase is refused.
  • The Intent mandate's cap must cover the total.
  • For UPI AutoPay, the AFA exemption never applies.

RBI AFA for India, in plain words

RBI rules ask for an additional factor of authentication (AFA) on some UPI AutoPay payments.

Payment AFA needed?
Setting up the mandate, and the first debit with it Always
A later debit up to ₹15,000 No
A later debit up to ₹1,00,000 for insurance premiums, mutual fund subscriptions or credit-card bills No
A later debit above those amounts Yes
Amount, currency or debit type unknown Yes, to stay safe

A checkout is always a set-up plus a first debit, so AFA always applies there. The limits are settings, so a future RBI change is a configuration change.

What is on by default

The checkout routes, mandates and payment execution each start switched off. With the defaults, a checkout can reach ready_for_complete but never completes, and no money moves. See feature switches.

Related guides

  • Safety and trust
  • Merchant setup checklist
  • Technical references: mandates, UPI AutoPay and RBI AFA and UCP checkout

articles.title: Merchant setup checklist
articles.description: A numbered checklist from Shopify sync and the Grantex allowlist to the DNS TXT step, your UCP profile, checkout, the ACP feed and MCP tools, and what stays off until a payment sandbox run.
articles.html:
In 30 seconds

  • Setup has five phases: connect your shop, connect to Grantex, publish your UCP profile, open sales channels, and payments.
  • Most steps are done once. Each step has an owner and a clear "if blocked" answer.
  • Your UCP profile goes live only after you prove you own the web address with a DNS TXT record.
  • Checkout, the ACP feed and MCP tools each have their own switch, so you can open one channel at a time.
  • Live payment stays off until a payment-provider sandbox run has passed. Nothing charges a buyer before then.

The five phases

You will use the Commerce Runtime page at /dashboard/commerce-runtime. You need the administrator role or the merchant role. A few steps are done by your platform operator, the person who runs your AgenticOrg deployment. Those steps say so.

Phase 1. Connect your shop

  1. 1
    Save your merchant settingsOwner: Merchant

    In Commerce Runtime, fill in your merchant identity, source system, buyer channels, payment provider, public publishing and any stores. You can change these later.

    Blocked / exception

    Check that you have the merchant or administrator role.

  2. 2
    Connect Shopify, read-onlyOwner: Merchant

    Store your Shopify Admin API credentials through the Shopify connector. AgenticOrg encrypts them and never shows them again.

    Blocked / exception

    Reconnect Shopify and confirm the status shows the store without secrets.

  3. 3
    Run the first syncOwner: Merchant

    Sync products, variants, prices, images and stock. Compare a few items with Shopify.

    Blocked / exception

    A missing credential or wrong store domain stops the sync and says why.

  4. 4
    Set your purchase limitsOwner: Merchant

    In your settings, set the largest order amount, the allowed currencies and the most items per order. Add stricter limits for purchases made while the buyer is not present.

    Blocked / exception

    Without limits, the arbiter refuses every purchase with merchant_limits_missing.

Phase 2. Connect to Grantex

  1. 5
    Allow your tenant at GrantexOwner: Platform operator

    Your platform operator gives AgenticOrg its Grantex service token and adds your tenant, and your Grantex commerce tenant, to the Grantex allowlist.

    Blocked / exception

    Without it, Grantex calls answer unavailable and, in production, no allow decision can be used.

  2. 6
    Request authorityOwner: Merchant

    From Commerce Runtime, send the Grantex authority request. Grantex signs your synced facts.

    Blocked / exception

    A 202 answer means connector evidence is missing; sync again first.

  3. 7
    Verify and keep the factsOwner: AgenticOrg

    Cache the returned artifacts. AgenticOrg checks every signature, key, expiry and revocation slot before it keeps anything.

    Blocked / exception

    A 422 artifact_verification_refused lists each refusal code; nothing from that batch is kept.

  4. 8
    Ask a test questionOwner: Merchant

    Ask your seller agent "Which variants are in stock?" and check that the answer shows its source and freshness.

    Blocked / exception

    A missing answer means catalog, price or stock facts are missing; refresh them.

Phase 3. Publish your UCP profile

Your UCP profile tells buyer agents where your shop is and what it offers. It is served at https://<your shop host>/.well-known/ucp.

  1. 9
    Choose your shop hostOwner: Merchant

    Ask AgenticOrg for a challenge for your host, for example shop.merchant.example. It returns a TXT record name and value.

    Blocked / exception

    An IP address or a single-word host is not accepted.

  2. 10
    Add the DNS TXT recordOwner: Merchant

    At your DNS provider, add the TXT record _agenticorg-ucp.shop.merchant.example with the value AgenticOrg gave you.

    Blocked / exception

    DNS changes can take time to spread; wait and try the check again.

  3. 11
    Verify the hostOwner: AgenticOrg

    Ask AgenticOrg to check the record. On a match it stores the proof and links the host to your merchant.

    Blocked / exception

    A host already linked to another tenant is refused.

  4. 12
    Create your signing keyOwner: Merchant

    AgenticOrg creates one signing key for your shop. Your profile publishes its public half. Rotated keys stay published for at least 7 days.

    Blocked / exception

    Publishing is refused with signing_key_missing until a key exists.

  5. 13
    PublishOwner: Merchant

    Record your opt-in to public discovery. The next Grantex authority request asks Grantex to allow discovery for this host.

    Blocked / exception

    Refusals name the reason, such as serving_host_not_attested.

  6. 14
    Profile goes liveOwner: Platform operator

    When the UCP profile switch is on and Grantex has issued an allowing discovery artifact, the profile is served.

    Blocked / exception

    The profile answers 404 until every condition holds; the UCP status view shows which one is missing.

Your operator must also route your shop host to the AgenticOrg service with the original host name intact.

Phase 4. Open your sales channels

Each channel has its own switch. Turn on one, test it, then the next.

  1. 15
    UCP checkoutOwner: Platform operator and merchant

    The operator turns on UCP checkout and you issue each agent platform its own API key. Agents can then open checkouts at your /ucp address.

    Blocked / exception

    With the switch off, every checkout route answers 404.

  2. 16
    ACP product feedOwner: Platform operator and merchant

    The operator turns on the ACP feed. You export it as JSON, JSON Lines or CSV and upload the files where the agent platform asks.

    Blocked / exception

    The feed is refused until the catalog's verified facts are fresh.

  3. 17
    ACP checkoutOwner: Platform operator and merchant

    The operator turns on ACP checkout, you opt your shop in, and you issue the platform a key with ACP write access.

    Blocked / exception

    Without your opt-in your ACP routes answer 404.

  4. 18
    MCP checkout toolsOwner: Platform operator

    On each MCP server install, set the address of your UCP profile. The checkout tools appear only while your profile lists checkout.

    Blocked / exception

    No profile address, or checkout off, means no tools are registered.

  5. 19
    Grantex mandatesOwner: Platform operator and merchant

    The operator turns on mandates and you name your Grantex commerce tenant and merchant in your settings.

    Blocked / exception

    Without mandates, production refuses checkout decisions as buyer_authority_verified.

Turn mandates on before payments. In production, a checkout without verified mandates is refused.

Phase 5. Payments: off until a sandbox run passes

Live payment execution stays off. It is turned on only after a full run against the payment provider's sandbox has passed in staging, and then one merchant at a time. Until then, a checkout stops at executor_unavailable and no buyer is charged.

  1. 20
    Sandbox credentialsOwner: Platform operator

    The operator stores the provider's sandbox credentials in the secret manager.

    Blocked / exception

    Without credentials the sandbox tests are skipped, not passed.

  2. 21
    Staging runOwner: Platform operator

    In staging, turn on payment execution for one test merchant and run the sandbox tests and the checkout smoke test.

    Blocked / exception

    Any failure keeps payments off.

  3. 22
    Check the ledgerOwner: Platform operator

    Confirm each payment call comes after a consumed allow decision.

    Blocked / exception

    A payment row without a consumed decision is an irregularity; stop and investigate.

  4. 23
    Production, one merchant at a timeOwner: Platform operator

    After owner approval, name the executor for one merchant and watch its first orders.

    Blocked / exception

    Remove the merchant's executor setting to stop it at once.

Quick test before you go live

  • Ask a buyer question and check the source and freshness label.
  • Open a test checkout and confirm it reaches ready_for_complete.
  • With payments still off, confirm Complete answers executor_unavailable and nothing is charged.
  • Export the ledger and run scripts/verify_ledger.py on it.

articles.title: Safety and trust
articles.description: Revocation everywhere, the arbiter's eight rules in plain words, the ledger and its offline check, agent request signatures in log and enforce mode, and how to read a refusal.
articles.html:
In 30 seconds

  • Revoke a fact once and every channel stops using it. If the revocation list cannot be reached, everything refuses.
  • The arbiter checks up to eight fixed rules before money moves. The first rule that fails is the reason, and it is recorded.
  • Every decision is in the commerce ledger. You can export it and check it on your own computer, with no database and no network.
  • Agent requests can carry a signature (Visa TAP or Web Bot Auth). AgenticOrg checks and logs them today; refusing unsigned calls is a separate switch.
  • A refusal is never a mystery: it names the rule, the reason and how to fix it.

Revocation everywhere

Sometimes a fact must stop counting at once. A price was wrong. A product was recalled. A buyer withdrew consent.

With OACP you revoke it once. Grantex marks its slot on a public revocation list as invalid. Every place that relies on it checks that list.

Good to know:

  • AgenticOrg keeps a copy of the list only briefly: never longer than the list itself allows, and never more than 10 minutes.
  • Revoking a mandate also revokes the mandates built on it.
  • A revocation stops new decisions. It does not undo a payment that already ran.

What the arbiter checks

Before a checkout completes, the arbiter runs these rules in a fixed order. Every rule runs. The first one that fails decides the refusal.

# Rule In plain words Example refusal
1 Mandate present There is a buyer mandate, and it has not expired. mandate_expired
2 Consent active The buyer's consent is still active. consent_missing
3 Spending cap The buyer's Commerce Passport allows this amount, in this currency. passport_amount_cap_exceeded
4 Verified buyer authority AgenticOrg verified the mandates itself. A claim in the request is not enough in production. buyer_authority_caller_asserted
5 Facts still valid Catalog, price, stock, policy and other facts are signed, fresh, unexpired and not revoked. artifact_revoked:price
6 Merchant limits The order is within your amount, currency and quantity limits. order_amount_cap_exceeded
7 Not-present limits If the buyer is away, your stricter limits and the Intent cap cover the order. not_present_limits_missing
8 RBI AFA A UPI AutoPay payment has verified AFA evidence when RBI rules need it. afa_evidence_missing

A refund has its own single rule: the refund must be positive, in the order's currency, and within what was captured.

Nobody waits for a person

The arbiter never answers "pending". It decides at once.

  • An allow is single use, bound to the exact cart, and expires after 10 minutes.
  • In production an allow is usable only with a Grantex countersignature. If that is missing, ask for a new decision.
  • You can choose to copy refusals into your review queue. That copy never changes or delays the decision.
  • An operator's note on a decision is only a note. It can never turn a refusal into an allow.

The ledger and offline checks

Every commerce write and every decision is recorded in the commerce ledger, in the same transaction as the change itself.

  1. 1
    ExportOwner: Tenant administrator

    A tenant administrator downloads the ledger export from the ledger routes.

    Blocked / exception

    Only administrators of that tenant can export.

  2. 2
    Verify offlineOwner: Anyone holding the file

    Run python scripts/verify_ledger.py export.json. It uses no database and no network.

    Blocked / exception

    Exit code 2 means the file is not a readable export.

  3. 3
    Read the answerOwner: Auditor or merchant

    Exit code 0 means verified. Exit code 1 reports the first break, such as sequence_gap or link_hash.

    Blocked / exception

    Treat a break as an irregularity, re-export and compare.

Three honest details:

  • Rows are signed with a platform secret (HMAC). The offline check verifies the chain links and the witnessed heads. It checks row signatures only when you supply the secret.
  • Rows are chained only for tenants where audit-chain sealing is on. That switch starts off.
  • To catch someone who rewrites the whole file, compare with a head kept outside it: a Grantex witness (its own switch, off by default) or a head you saved yourself with --expected-head.

Request signing: which agent is calling?

Agents can sign their HTTP requests (RFC 9421). AgenticOrg understands two public profiles:

  • Visa Trusted Agent Protocol (TAP): browsing and payment tags, a short window and a one-time nonce.
  • Web Bot Auth: the agent's key is found through its published signature agent.
Mode Unsigned or bad signature Good signature
log (default) Answered, and the status is logged Answered, logged, and recorded on write routes
enforce Refused with 401 on the commerce API surfaces Answered, logged, and recorded on write routes

Enforce mode covers only the catalog and product JSON reads and the A2A routes. Your public pages, structured data, sitemap and llms.txt are never refused for a missing signature.

What a refusal looks like

A refusal always tells you what failed and why. Here is a shortened, synthetic example for a purchase over the buyer's cap:

{
  "code": "arbiter_refused",
  "failing_rule": "passport_amount_cap",
  "reason": "passport_amount_cap_exceeded",
  "decision_id": "arbdec_5b0e1c7d2a9f",
  "action": "The commerce arbiter refused: passport_amount_cap (passport_amount_cap_exceeded).",
  "required_config": "buyer_authority.passport_ref, passport_max_amount_minor_units, passport_currency, passport_expires_at"
}

Read it like this:

  1. failing_rule is the rule from the table above.
  2. reason is the exact cause.
  3. decision_id finds the sealed decision in the ledger.
  4. required_config says what must change before a new attempt.

In a UCP or ACP checkout the decision comes back inside the checkout answer, as a business message. Nothing is charged.

Related guides

  • Feature switches reference
  • OACP FAQ
  • Technical references: arbiter and ledger, agent request signing and OACP troubleshooting

articles.title: Feature switches reference
articles.description: Every OACP switch, its default and what it does, in plain tables, with the safe order for turning them on and how to turn them back off.
articles.html:
In 30 seconds

  • Every OACP surface that could expose your shop or move money starts switched off.
  • The safety checks start switched on in production: signature checks, verified buyer authority and the Grantex countersignature.
  • Request signatures start in log mode: checked and logged, never refused, until someone chooses enforce.
  • Switches are settings on the AgenticOrg service. They are read at start-up, so a change needs a restart.
  • Turn them on one at a time, in the order below, and write down how to turn each one back off first.

Three kinds of switch

"Strict runtimes" are production, staging, preview and any unknown environment name. Local, dev, development, test and ci are not strict.

Safety checks (on in production)

Switch Default What it does
AGENTICORG_OACP_VERIFY_STRICT On in strict runtimes; log-only elsewhere Refuses to keep any fact whose signature, key, scope, expiry or revocation check fails.
AGENTICORG_ARBITER_REQUIRE_VERIFIED_AUTHORITY On in strict runtimes Refuses buyer authority that AgenticOrg did not verify itself (rule 4).
AGENTICORG_ARBITER_REQUIRE_GRANTEX_GRANT On in strict runtimes An allow decision can be used only with a verified Grantex countersignature.
AGENTICORG_ARBITER_GRANTEX_POST_ENABLED Follows the switch above Sends each decision to Grantex for its countersignature.
AGENTICORG_ROUTE_ENFORCEMENT_MODE enforce A commerce write that skips its ledger row is answered as an error. log only logs it.

Turning a safety check off weakens the shop's protection. Do it only as a recorded decision, for a short window.

Ledger extras (off by default)

Switch Default What it does
AGENTICORG_AUDIT_CHAIN_DEFAULT_ON Off Links the ledger rows of every commerce tenant into a hash chain (the global AGENTICORG_AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED does it for all tenants).
AGENTICORG_AUDIT_WITNESS_ENABLED Off Sends each sealed chain head to Grantex, which countersigns it as an outside witness.
AGENTICORG_OACP_RETENTION_APPLY_ENABLED Off Lets the daily task delete review manifests whose stored retention decision has come due.

Selling surfaces (off by default)

Switch Default What it does
AGENTICORG_UCP_PROFILE_ENABLED Off Serves your UCP profile, catalog and store locations. Off, they answer 404.
AGENTICORG_UCP_VERSIONS 2026-04-08 Which UCP releases are served. Add 2026-08-25 when platforms read it.
AGENTICORG_UCP_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_DAYS 7 (minimum 7) How long a rotated-out signing key stays published.
AGENTICORG_UCP_CHECKOUT_ENABLED Off Serves UCP checkout, cart and order routes. Off, they answer 404.
AGENTICORG_ACP_FEED_ENABLED Off Lets you export the ACP product feed.
AGENTICORG_ACP_CHECKOUT_ENABLED Off Serves ACP checkout sessions (your shop must also opt in).
AGENTICORG_ACP_SIGNATURE_MODE log Keep log. ACP publishes no signing method yet, so enforce would refuse every request.
OACP_PUBLIC_CATALOG_PLATFORM_DISABLED Unset An operator override that withdraws the public catalog pages for every merchant.

Mandates and payments (off by default)

Switch Default What it does
AGENTICORG_GRANTEX_MANDATES_ENABLED Off A checkout Complete gets Intent, Cart and Payment mandates from Grantex and verifies them.

articles.title: OACP FAQ
articles.description: Short answers to the questions sellers ask: standards, certification, Grantex's role, prices, approvals, outages, revocation, UPI and what is switched on today.
articles.html:
In 30 seconds

  • Short answers to the questions sellers ask most about OACP.
  • OACP is a trust layer under UCP, ACP and AP2. It feeds them and does not replace them.
  • Your shop stays the source of truth. Grantex signs. AgenticOrg checks, decides and records. The payment provider moves money.
  • Nothing that publishes your shop or moves money is on by default.
  • For the full picture, start with the overview and the merchant setup checklist.

Who does what

Do I have to choose between UCP, ACP and OACP?

No. OACP sits underneath. It renders your facts into UCP and ACP, and maps mandates to AP2 field names. Buyer agents keep using the standard they already speak.

Is OACP certified or endorsed by the UCP, ACP or AP2 groups?

No. OACP is not a certification, and those groups have not endorsed it. It also does not establish regulatory compliance on its own.

What do I need to start?

A Shopify store, the merchant or administrator role in AgenticOrg, and a platform operator who connects your tenant to Grantex. Follow the merchant setup checklist.

Does every buyer question go through Grantex?

No. AgenticOrg answers questions from its own verified copy of your facts. Grantex takes part in purchases: it issues the mandates and countersigns the decision. It never moves money.

Can an agent buy something at the wrong price?

OACP is built to refuse it. A decision is bound to the exact cart, price and quantity. Change any of them and the decision no longer matches. Stale, expired or revoked prices are refused.

Does a person at my shop approve each order?

No. The arbiter decides at once with fixed rules. You can copy refusals into a review queue, but that never changes or delays a decision.

What happens if Grantex is unreachable?

Plain questions can still be answered from facts that are still valid. In production, anything that commits money is refused until Grantex is back. If the revocation list cannot be read, facts are refused.

How do I stop selling a product to agents at once?

Revoke the fact that covers it. Grantex marks it invalid, and every channel stops using it. For one channel only, turn that channel's switch off.

Does this work with UPI in India?

It is built for it: UPI AutoPay mandates on the Plural rail, with RBI AFA as the buyer's own step in their UPI app. Completion is refused until verified AFA evidence arrives. It has not yet run against the Plural sandbox, and payment execution is off by default.

What if the buyer is not present when the agent buys?

There is no passkey step. Your stricter not-present limits apply, and without them the purchase is refused.

Can I check the records myself?

Yes. Export the ledger and run scripts/verify_ledger.py on your own computer. It needs no database and no network. See Safety and trust.

What is switched on today?

The safety checks are on in production. Every surface that publishes your shop or moves money starts off: the UCP profile and checkout, the ACP feed and checkout, mandates and payment execution. With the defaults no checkout completes and no money moves. See feature switches.

Where can I read more?

  • What OACP is and how it works
  • The blog post OACP explained: one trust layer under UCP, ACP and AP2
  • The technical OACP runtime docs

articles.title: BFSI: business onboarding and KYB review
articles.description: A fictional configured example from business application to evidence investigation, screening review, human decision and signed handoff.
articles.html:
Scenario and boundary

Example Bank wants analysts to spend less time assembling a business-onboarding file and more time reviewing exceptions. This playbook uses AgenticOrg's governed-case path for read-only investigation, cited memo preparation, screening proposals, deterministic policy evaluation and a human decision.

It does not automate account opening, sanctions clearance, loan approval or regulatory reporting. Provider availability, country coverage, bank policy and system-of-record integration are institution-specific. Use fictional businesses until the institution approves real data.

Prepare the pilot

Assign an onboarding owner, screening analyst, authorized approver, provider integration owner and platform/security owner. Configure the tenant-gated case runtime, one active shared agent per required case role, reviewed provider manifest/read tools, exact local purpose controls, Grantex grants and a reviewed policy. Configure the decision issuer and signed handoff destination separately.

The institution's application/LOS system submits cases through the reviewed API/workflow. The approvals console is for queue and review, not a universal business-intake form.

Process map

This map assigns each handoff in the configured case path. A missing source or unresolved review is a stop, not an implied clearance.

  1. 1
    ApplicationOwner: Bank intake team

    A fictional business submits details through the bank's approved intake.

    Blocked / exception

    Incomplete intake stays with the bank; no case outcome is inferred.

  2. 2
    InvestigationOwner: Configured case agents

    Configured agents read approved registry, ownership and screening sources.

    Blocked / exception

    Missing grant, provider error or absent record remains missing evidence, not a clear result.

  3. 3
    Memo and policyOwner: AgenticOrg case runtime

    The case shows cited findings, missing items and the reviewed policy tier.

    Blocked / exception

    Unsupported citations or incomplete evidence require investigation before decision.

  4. 4
    Screening reviewOwner: Screening analyst

    The analyst checks each proposed disposition against the cited record.

    Human decision

    Accept the proposal or override it with a written reason.

    Blocked / exception

    An unresolved hit stays open for human review; the proposal does not clear it.

  5. 5
    Decision requestOwner: Authorized case operator and approval issuer

    The exact case version and action go to the configured approval issuer.

    Human decision

    A designated approver decides on the issuer page; a distinct second approver participates where required.

    Blocked / exception

    Missing, expired or superseded approval cannot record a decision; request a new decision on the current case.

  6. 6
    Bank handoffOwner: Bank system-of-record team

    The signed outcome is delivered for the bank system to interpret and act on.

    Blocked / exception

    Delivery failure or duplicate evidence needs reconciliation; do not infer account opening.

Follow one fictional application

  1. Open Approvals > governed cases at /dashboard/approvals/cases.
  2. Find the fictional case and inspect investigation state.
  3. Read identity, registry, ownership, screening, activity and missing evidence.
  4. Open retained source passages where available; confirm provider record and retrieval time.
  5. Inspect policy ID/version and fired rules. Do not treat missing evidence as passing.
  6. Review screening proposals. Override only with a documented reason; the agent's proposal does not clear the hit.
  7. Request a decision for the current case. The named approver authenticates on the issuer's page, including distinct second approval where required.
  8. Record the verified decision and inspect signed handoff delivery. Confirm what the bank system did with it.

What a successful trial proves

It proves the configured evidence/review/decision/handoff path for that test. It does not prove universal registry coverage, calibrated model accuracy, case-bound pooled grants or regulatory approval. The rollout review must keep visible that AgenticOrg's Grantex SDK call passes no case id or purpose, so token-level case purpose and per-case caps are not checked on that path.

Negative cases to demonstrate

Try a unavailable provider capability, unresolved screening hit, missing grant, cross-company request, machine-credential human decision, changed memo after approval request and duplicate handoff. Expected outcomes are visible missing evidence/refusals or safe idempotent handling, never a manufactured approval.

Measure adoption

Compare manual file-assembly time, missing-information rate, analyst overrides, re-investigation, review age and delivery failures on a reviewed sample. Track reopening causes. Do not publish a numerical accuracy claim from a few happy-path examples.

Next: Capability status and gaps, Governed cases, Approvals, Adoption checklist.
