articles.title: BFSI: reconciliation and finance exceptions
articles.description: Configure a read-only reconciliation assistant for synthetic bank and ledger data, review discrepancies, and hand approved corrections to finance.
articles.html:
Scenario and boundary

Example Bank's finance team wants a daily exception pack comparing a reviewed ledger export with bank/settlement statements. AgenticOrg assists with evidence extraction, comparison, break classification and a reviewable summary. Posting entries, releasing money and certifying balances remain the finance team's authorized process.

This is a configurable reference workflow, not a universally pre-integrated bank reconciliation product. The actual ledger/bank connector contract, matching logic and accounting policy must be implemented/reviewed for the institution.

Prepare the sources

Use synthetic CSV/XLSX statements with transaction reference, date, amount, currency and relevant account mapping. Define timezone, date boundaries, sign conventions, duplicates and tolerances. Avoid real account numbers in training examples.

Upload the reconciliation procedure to Knowledge Base and verify search. Configure read-only exports/connectors with the correct company binding. Make sure the agent's selected tools actually read the required data; a finance template alone does not do so.

Configure and run

For a small reproducible exercise, prepare these two synthetic datasets using the schema expected by your reviewed read tool. Do not infer that uploading CSV to Knowledge Base automatically connects the reconciliation agent to it.

source,reference,date,amount,currency
bank,DEMO-001,2026-09-28,1000.00,INR
bank,DEMO-002,2026-09-28,2500.00,INR
bank,DEMO-003,2026-09-28,750.00,INR

source,reference,date,amount,currency
ledger,DEMO-001,2026-09-28,1000.00,INR
ledger,DEMO-002,2026-09-28,2400.00,INR
ledger,DEMO-004,2026-09-28,500.00,INR

The reviewed expected result is one exact match (DEMO-001), an INR 100 amount difference (DEMO-002), one bank-only entry (DEMO-003) and one ledger-only entry (DEMO-004). Bank total is INR 4,250; ledger total is INR 3,900. These figures are teaching assertions, not reconciled customer balances. Require source-row references and validated calculations in the exception pack.

  1. Review the available reconciliation agent or create a bounded finance candidate.
  2. Specify output: matched items, unmatched items, reason, evidence reference and proposed follow-up.
  3. For exact financial totals, require deterministic calculations/validated tool results; do not ask an LLM to invent or approximate amounts.
  4. Build a manual workflow: read sources, validate schema, compare, prepare exception pack, human review.
  5. Run a synthetic day with known expected matches and deliberate breaks.
  6. Inspect source freshness, totals, duplicate handling and every exception.
  7. Hand approved corrections to the accounting system through a separately authorized process.

Process map

The comparison below assumes a reviewed read tool, mappings and deterministic calculation. It does not imply an automatic ledger posting connector.

  1. 1
    Read-only sourcesOwner: Finance data owner and approved read tool

    Collect reviewed statement and ledger exports for one business period.

    Blocked / exception

    A late, partial or inaccessible source makes the period incomplete.

  2. 2
    Validate and compareOwner: Configured comparison and finance operator

    Apply reviewed schema, currency, duplicate and matching rules with validated calculations.

    Blocked / exception

    Corrupt rows, mismatched currencies or totals become exceptions, not forced matches.

  3. 3
    Exception packOwner: Finance assistant

    List matched pairs and each break with source-row evidence and proposed follow-up.

    Blocked / exception

    Missing provenance or uncertain arithmetic must be checked before review.

  4. 4
    Finance reviewOwner: Authorized finance reviewer

    Recheck ambiguous matches and proposed corrections against the source records.

    Human decision

    Approve, revise or reject each proposed correction through the institution's controls.

    Blocked / exception

    Unresolved breaks remain open and cannot be reported as balanced.

  5. 5
    Authoritative postingOwner: Institution finance and accounting system

    Send approved corrections through a separately authorized accounting process.

    Blocked / exception

    A prepared pack is neither a posted entry nor a verified balance.

Sample acceptance cases

Input Expected evidence
Same reference and amount A documented matched pair
Missing ledger item Unmatched source entry, not a guessed posting
Same amount in different currencies No unsupported cross-currency match
Duplicate reference Explicit duplicate exception
Corrupt/partial source Failed validation or incomplete evidence, not balanced totals

Scheduling and operations

Schedule only after a manual run is reproducible. Confirm timezone, statement arrival, worker availability, rate limits and retry/idempotency. A late source must not be represented as a complete daily reconciliation.

Measure correctly identified breaks, false matches, review effort, source delays and reopened corrections. Compare against an independently reviewed ledger sample. Retest mappings after upstream changes.

articles.title: BFSI: customer service across chat and voice
articles.description: Build a source-grounded service assistant, classify complaints, prepare responses and escalate sensitive account actions to authorized staff.
articles.html:
Scenario and boundary

Example Bank wants a service assistant that explains approved procedures, triages complaints and prepares staff responses through chat and configured voice. Start with general information and synthetic cases. Do not expose account details or perform account/card/payment actions without the bank's approved authentication and integration path.

A phone number, claimed name or free-text account identifier is not identity verification. AgenticOrg's voice/runtime controls do not themselves establish bank-customer authentication.

Prepare a reviewed knowledge set

Upload current product FAQs, branch directory, complaint procedure and escalation policy. Assign effective dates and an owner. Search known answers and confirm citations. Remove or clearly supersede conflicting old procedures. Do not load unapproved financial advice as an operational policy.

Build the service agent

Use a reviewed support-triage candidate or custom operations agent. Define categories, urgency, response-draft structure and escalation. Grant read-only knowledge/approved ticket tools first. Explicitly refuse PIN/OTP collection, balance invention, account changes and payment instructions outside the authorized bank workflow.

  1. Run a general question through the agent detail/chat path.
  2. Test a complaint with missing information.
  3. Test a suspected fraud/card-loss scenario requiring urgent human routing.
  4. Ask for a private account balance and confirm refusal/referral.
  5. Verify any configured ticket write/email action separately before enabling it.

Process map

This is a response-preparation path. The bank's authenticated channel and staff remain responsible for private account servicing and final communication.

  1. 1
    Question or complaintOwner: Bank channel owner

    Receive the request through a configured general-information or authenticated channel.

    Blocked / exception

    A claimed name or phone number alone does not establish customer identity.

  2. 2
    Knowledge checkOwner: Service agent and knowledge owner

    Retrieve the current approved procedure and inspect its cited source.

    Blocked / exception

    Missing, conflicting or outdated guidance goes to staff; do not invent an answer.

  3. 3
    Response draftOwner: Service agent

    Prepare a bounded answer or complaint summary from supported facts.

    Blocked / exception

    Private account data or an unsupported action is refused or referred to the bank's authorized path.

  4. 4
    Human escalationOwner: Authorized service staff

    Review sensitive, urgent or unresolved requests before any staff response.

    Human decision

    Staff decide whether to send, revise or escalate the prepared response.

    Blocked / exception

    Suspected fraud or a failed voice/ticket path follows the bank's urgent human process.

  5. 5
    Confirmed outcomeOwner: Bank service team and system of record

    Record communication and resolution in the bank's approved system.

    Blocked / exception

    A prepared draft is not a sent message or completed account action.

Add voice only after chat is correct

Configure signed Twilio calls using Voice setup. Test with an approved number/window. Check speech recognition, spoken clarity, interruption/silence, safe failure wording and actual provider status. A passing text simulation does not prove acoustic or telephone quality.

Document provider recording/retention and customer-facing disclosures under the institution's process. AgenticOrg's call-history masking does not control the provider's own storage settings.

What to measure

Track correct routing, unsupported-answer rate, unresolved questions, escalation time, call failures and human overrides. Validate different accents/languages and noisy conditions where they are in scope. Do not claim a language is ready merely because it appears in a selector.

Roll out a narrow task population before sensitive account servicing. Re-test whenever the bank procedure, provider number/callback, model or ticketing contract changes.

Next: Capability status and gaps, Run and chat, Knowledge and OCR, Approvals.

articles.title: BFSI: insurance document and claims assistance
articles.description: Use OCR, policy knowledge and reviewed workflows to prepare claim-file checklists without automating coverage or payout decisions.
articles.html:
Scenario and boundary

Example Insurer needs help preparing claim files for manual review. An assistant can extract document text, compare it with an approved checklist, summarize missing items and prepare reviewer notes. It must not decide coverage, reject a claim, determine liability or release a payout.

This is a configurable document/workflow example, not a shipped universal claims-system adapter. The insurer owns the policy wording, adjudication rules, data permissions and integration.

Prepare the exercise

Use a fictional claim, synthetic identity/receipt documents and a reviewed sample checklist. Keep medical or real customer data out of initial testing. Upload the checklist and policy reference to Knowledge Base; verify retrieval against known clauses and effective dates.

For scans, use supported PDF/image formats and inspect extraction method, OCR confidence and page provenance. Manually verify dates, policy numbers, currency, totals and negatives. A confidence value is not permission to accept an amount.

Configure the assistant

Create a custom operations/document-review agent with output fields for document type, cited facts, missing items, unreadable fields and reviewer questions. Require it to quote/cite only available evidence and explicitly mark uncertainty. Limit tools to approved reads during the first pilot.

Process map

The map stops at reviewer preparation. Coverage, liability and payout stay with the insurer's authorized process.

  1. 1
    Approved claim fileOwner: Insurer intake team

    Authorized intake supplies synthetic file references and the current checklist.

    Blocked / exception

    Missing documents stay on the request list; no completeness claim is made.

  2. 2
    Extraction checkOwner: Document-review operator

    Native parsing or OCR supplies page-linked text for inspection.

    Blocked / exception

    Unreadable dates, amounts or identifiers are flagged for manual verification, never guessed.

  3. 3
    Checklist comparisonOwner: Configured document-review agent

    The assistant prepares cited present, missing and uncertain items.

    Blocked / exception

    Conflicting policy versions or absent sources go to the checklist owner.

  4. 4
    Claims reviewOwner: Authorized claims reviewer

    Staff compare the prepared notes with source documents and insurer policy.

    Human decision

    The reviewer requests more evidence or makes the insurer's coverage determination outside the assistant.

    Blocked / exception

    Ambiguous or incomplete evidence remains in review; no rejection or payout is automated.

  5. 5
    System handoffOwner: Insurer claims-system team

    The claims platform records the insurer's own authorized outcome.

    Blocked / exception

    A prepared note is not a customer notification, coverage decision or paid claim.

Run a complete test

Give the fictional file reference DEMO-CLAIM-001 a checklist that requires an application, receipt and incident statement. Supply only the first two documents. The expected reviewer output should contain:

File: DEMO-CLAIM-001
Application: present, with source/page reference
Receipt: present, with source/page reference; amount needs manual verification
Incident statement: missing
Next step: ask the authorized claims team to obtain the missing statement
Coverage decision: not made
Payout: not initiated

This is an expected-result example, not an API schema. Match it to your configured workflow's actual fields and compare its sources against the original file.

  1. Submit a complete synthetic file and compare findings against a human checklist.
  2. Remove one required document and verify the assistant requests it.
  3. Use a blurry amount/date and confirm it is unreadable, not guessed.
  4. Provide conflicting policy versions and confirm escalation.
  5. Ask the agent to approve or pay the claim and confirm refusal.
  6. Inspect run history, sources and reviewer handoff.

If a claims-platform write or customer notification is needed, build/approve that connector contract separately. A prepared missing-document list is not proof that a message was sent.

Operate the process

Assign a checklist owner, claims reviewer, data/privacy owner and integration owner. Define retention for uploaded files, extracted text, run evidence and provider copies. Track document-quality failures, missing-item accuracy, review effort and reopened files rather than a single generalized "AI accuracy" number.

Next: Capability status and gaps, Knowledge and OCR, Workflows, Security and data.

articles.title: BFSI: merchant enablement and agentic commerce
articles.description: A bank-led merchant pilot using Seller Commerce Agents, Shopify, OACP artifacts, buyer channels and provider-owned payment capability evidence.
articles.html:
Scenario and ownership

This is a reference example for an acquiring bank's merchant-enablement pilot, not an already integrated banking product or a claim of live payment execution.

In this synthetic example, an acquiring bank wants to help a fictional Shopify merchant become usable by agentic buyer interfaces. The bank can offer an institution-managed or reviewed hosted AgenticOrg workspace, but merchant/provider/platform contracts still determine actual availability.

AgenticOrg owns seller/buyer runtime. Grantex owns trust/policy/canonical artifacts. Shopify owns merchant catalog/inventory/order truth. The bank/fintech/provider owns payment/mandate execution and customer authorization. OACP is not a reason to make Grantex the engine for every buyer message.

Build one synthetic merchant path

  1. Assign a merchant owner, bank integration owner, provider contact and channel owner.
  2. Configure merchant-scoped Seller Commerce Agent onboarding and source/channel settings.
  3. Obtain read-only access to a sandbox Shopify store with a fictional catalog through the merchant's approved process.
  4. Sync synthetic products/variants/images/price/inventory and compare samples with the sandbox store.
  5. Send the bounded Grantex authority request and verify/cache issued artifacts.
  6. Ask product questions about the fictional catalog through the configured web or agent bridge.
  7. Inspect source, freshness, supported facts and refusal behavior.
  8. Prepare a provider/POS handoff and confirm that no order/payment state is fabricated.

Process map

This is a bank-led reference pilot with configured merchant, channel and provider paths. A prepared handoff is never a completed transaction.

  1. 1
    Bank and merchant setupOwner: Bank integration owner and merchant owner

    Agree identities, read scopes, provider contract and publishing state.

    Human decision

    Owners approve the pilot scope and any channel publication under their own processes.

    Blocked / exception

    Unapproved access or publishing state keeps the channel off.

  2. 2
    Merchant-source evidenceOwner: Merchant source owner and configured AgenticOrg sync

    Read-only sync supplies product, price and inventory snapshots for sample checks.

    Blocked / exception

    Missing scopes or stale source facts stop unsupported buyer promises.

  3. 3
    Trust artifactsOwner: Grantex authority and AgenticOrg runtime

    The bounded authority request and cache retain scope, source and freshness.

    Blocked / exception

    Invalid or stale artifacts cannot support commitment-bound requests.

  4. 4
    Buyer channelOwner: Channel owner and AgenticOrg buyer runtime

    A configured bridge answers from supported merchant artifacts.

    Blocked / exception

    Unsupported channels or facts are refused until the integration is approved.

  5. 5
    Provider capabilityOwner: Bank/provider integration team

    A configured provider path checks non-sensitive capability evidence.

    Human decision

    The customer and provider complete any required authorization outside this map.

    Blocked / exception

    Capability evidence alone does not prove a mandate or payment.

  6. 6
    Authoritative handoffOwner: Provider, POS or merchant system

    A prepared packet awaits provider, POS or merchant confirmation.

    Blocked / exception

    Absent or failed confirmation stays pending or failed; no paid or placed state is fabricated.

Plural/Pine and mandates

Arrange the provider onboarding contact, merchant account, sandbox/live access, allowed capability contract and human authorization journey. AgenticOrg can verify provider-owned capability evidence directly through its configured path. Store non-sensitive references, not raw mandate/payment credentials.

A credential/token capability check is not proof of a completed mandate or an allowed payment in every geography. Live execution needs the provider's real contract, authorization, settlement/error/refund handling and institution approval. The current OACP runtime remains prepared/non-executing for those actions.

Channels and protocol payloads

UCP/ACP/schema.org/AP2/A2A/MCP-style payloads and bridges are not automatic marketplace placement. Agree each target's supported contract, authentication, publication/approval requirements and actual customer journey. WhatsApp/Telegram need configured credentials and channel rollout; ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini/Perplexity need appropriate client/platform setup.

Physical-store POS

An offline POS bridge prepares a store-linked handoff and reconciles authoritative provider/POS confirmation. It must preserve merchant/store context, expiry, source, reference and duplicate handling. Do not call a paid receipt successful because an agent displayed a prepared packet.

Pilot success criteria

Verify accurate catalog facts, stale-source refusal, cross-merchant isolation, invalid webhook rejection, channel authentication and non-fabricated transaction state. Keep public discovery off until the publishing path is approved and validated. Measure the complete buyer journey rather than counting adapter names.

Next: Capability status and gaps, Commerce guide, API and agent clients, Team adoption.

Arrange the provider onboarding contact, merchant account, sandbox/live access, allowed capability contract and human authorization journey. AgenticOrg can verify provider-owned capability evidence directly through its configured path. Store non-sensitive references, not raw mandate/payment credentials.

A credential/token capability check is not proof of a completed mandate or an allowed payment in every geography. Live execution needs the provider's real contract, authorization, settlement/error/refund handling and institution approval. The current OACP runtime remains prepared/non-executing for those actions.

   Channels and protocol payloads

UCP/ACP/schema.org/AP2/A2A/MCP-style payloads and bridges are not automatic marketplace placement. Agree each target's supported contract, authentication, publication/approval requirements and actual customer journey. WhatsApp/Telegram need configured credentials and channel rollout; ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini/Perplexity need appropriate client/platform setup.

   Physical-store POS

An offline POS bridge prepares a store-linked handoff and reconciles authoritative provider/POS confirmation. It must preserve merchant/store context, expiry, source, reference and duplicate handling. Do not call a paid receipt successful because an agent displayed a prepared packet.

   Pilot success criteria

Verify accurate catalog facts, stale-source refusal, cross-merchant isolation, invalid webhook rejection, channel authentication and non-fabricated transaction state. Keep public discovery off until the publishing path is approved and validated. Measure the complete buyer journey rather than counting adapter names.

Next: [Capability status and gaps](/docs/bfsi-capability-status), [Commerce guide](/docs/commerce), [API and agent clients](/docs/api-sdk-mcp), [Team adoption](/docs/adoption-checklist).

articles.title: BFSI capability status and open work
articles.description: See which functional capabilities exist, which remain partial or unavailable, and what a configured pilot still needs to prove.
articles.audience: BFSI sponsors, operators and integration owners
articles.html:
What this status means

AgenticOrg can be configured for evidence-led BFSI workflows, but a process map is not proof that a bank's systems, providers, controls or staff are connected. The current repository assessment has 150 functional capabilities: 24 covered, 97 partial and 29 gaps. A covered component may still need a tenant setting, approved provider, external system or human reviewer. No full BFSI journey has end-to-end acceptance on the strength of these counts alone.

Services built behind default-off settings after this baseline was last refreshed are not yet reflected in these counts; where the table below names one, it is marked (built, off by default). They are document processing, speech and call intelligence, transaction intelligence, conversational services and the supervisor view, workbenches, lineage, content services, personalisation, the agent registry, model cards, and FinOps thresholds and forecast. Each is unavailable until its setting is turned on; see feature switches that ship off and the six screens that ship switched off. The Banking Pack can be installed without a setting, but it is not counted either.

This page describes functional software coverage, not infrastructure location, regulatory approval, certification or permission to process customer data. A feature behind a disabled flag is unavailable in the default installation.

Where the work stands

Area Working foundation Still needs implementation, enabling or validation
Agent governance Agent execution, scoped grants, human review and case evidence paths Registry-grade discoverability, dependency mapping and model cards (built, off by default) and cross-service lifecycle proof
Knowledge and documents Ingestion, OCR and source-aware answers on configured paths Mixed bundles, page-region review and document comparison (built, off by default), hybrid-ranking rollout (off by default) and cited refusal across every tenant path
Conversation and speech Web chat and configured voice runtime Banking intents, speaker separation, spoken sensitive-data redaction and supervised takeover (built, off by default), and channel parity
Transactions and commerce Read-only source evidence and prepared agent handoffs Human disposition of transaction findings (built, off by default), bank-owned source connections, provider-owned execution and reconciliation evidence
Operations Logging, approval controls and evaluation hooks Budget thresholds and synthetic checks (built, off by default), complete trace coverage, measured SLOs, rollback and production-grade recovery

The detailed functional assessment and capability matrix identify individual gaps. The product status records other release boundaries. These files describe the current repository assessment; verify your deployed version and configuration separately.

What to prove in a pilot

  1. Select one narrow use case and name its business owner, system-of-record owner, integration owner, reviewer and support owner.
  2. Use fictional or institution-approved data. Connect each required system through its reviewed API or file contract; a diagram is not a connector.
  3. Run normal, missing, stale, conflicting, unauthorized and cross-company cases. Inspect citations, grants, reviewer decisions and external receipts.
  4. Demonstrate restart, replay, revocation, duplicate events and recovery with the same users and roles that will operate the pilot.
  5. Confirm what the external system actually did. An agent draft, signed handoff or payment-capability reference is not an account change, payment, settlement or regulatory filing.

For a concrete teaching path, open the business onboarding, reconciliation, customer service, insurance or merchant services playbook. Each is a fictional, configured example and carries its own blocked paths and human ownership.

articles.title: Team adoption and launch checklist
articles.description: Assign owners, select a first use case, train operators and reviewers, measure outcomes and expand without skipping real integration work.
articles.html:
Choose the first useful problem

Select one repeatable task with a measurable outcome, manageable data and a human owner. Good first tasks include procedure Q&A, document completeness review, reconciliation exception preparation and complaint triage. Avoid a first rollout that simultaneously requires new voice, payments, core banking and marketplace integrations.

This is a rollout checklist, not an instruction to remain in an endless audit phase. Build the actual authorized path, test it with representative evidence and train the people who will use it.

Assign accountable owners

Owner Responsibility
Business sponsor Outcome, budget and scope
Process owner Current procedure, expected output and exceptions
Administrator Workspace, roles, models and configuration
Integration owner Provider contract, credentials, tool behavior and recovery
Reviewer Human approvals, coverage and escalation
Security/data owner Permitted information, retention and incident handling
Operator/support owner Daily monitoring, user help and rollback

Before inviting the team

  1. Complete Your first agent with synthetic data.
  2. Verify every required knowledge/model/connector path separately.
  3. Test normal, missing, conflicting, stale and forbidden requests.
  4. Confirm a non-admin operator can reproduce the exact task.
  5. Confirm the reviewer can find evidence and make only authorized decisions.
  6. Inspect external system confirmations separately from prepared outputs.
  7. Document failure recovery, support contact and a pause/rollback trigger.

Training session

Walk users through sign-in, company selection, task input, source inspection, run status and escalation. Show one successful task and one intentional refusal. Train reviewers to check evidence, not trust fluent wording. Let each user reproduce the path with their own role.

Use the BFSI playbooks as teaching examples, then replace fictional inputs and procedures only after the institution approves real data and integrations. Bank-specific connectivity and regulated authority must remain explicit.

Follow one complete pilot

  1. 1
    Choose the taskOwner: Business sponsor

    Pick document Q&A, invoice review, a service case or a seller catalogue question. Record the current process and expected answer.

    Blocked / exception

    Do not begin with an unbounded promise to automate everything.

  2. 2
    Connect approved sourcesOwner: Administrator and integration owner

    Upload reviewed knowledge and configure the model and required read-only tools using your own provider credentials.

    Blocked / exception

    Missing credentials or unsupported tools are configuration gaps, not successful integrations.

  3. 3
    Run and inspectOwner: Process owner

    Send a representative request, inspect citations and task status, and repeat with missing, stale and conflicting inputs.

    Blocked / exception

    An unsupported answer or partial run is reviewed, not described as completed work.

  4. 4
    Review the handoffOwner: Authorized reviewer

    Check the prepared output and any required human approval. Verify external writes or messages in their owning system.

    Human decision

    Approve only the scoped action supported by evidence.

    Blocked / exception

    A draft, catalogue artifact or approval packet is not a posted invoice, completed order or executed payment.

  5. 5
    Measure and expandOwner: Sponsor and support owner

    Compare the same cases against the baseline, train users and add the next authorized capability only when its dependency works.

    Blocked / exception

    Pause on unacceptable error, cost, latency or reopened cases; retain a recovery path.

For banks, use Customer service and Capability status. For fintech/platform teams, use API, SDK and MCP. For merchants, follow the External buyer journey.

Operating across countries

Agree on data location, retention, access, supported language, provider coverage, currency and applicable approval requirements for the actual deployment. A deployment option or provider connector does not establish residency, regulatory approval or support in every jurisdiction. Start with approved samples; never put customer records, API keys or passwords in a public demo enquiry.

Discuss a specific pilot at sanjeev@orchestrum.in. Describe the task, systems and expected outcome, not confidential evidence.

Enquiries and external messages

A demo enquiry acknowledgement means the request was received, not that email arrived or a sales agent completed its work. SMTP acceptance, actual inbox arrival and a reply are separate outcomes. Staff should inspect recorded delivery states and confirm receipt in the receiving system before marking a messaging pilot complete. Failed or uncertain sends need review, not repeated submissions.

Operators can use the marketing delivery runbook for mailbox setup, protected credentials, durable worker processing and spend controls. Customer operational messaging and tenant workflows keep their own recipients and credentials.

Pilot scorecard

Track task correctness, source coverage, review effort, queue age, external-action failures, latency, cost and reopened errors. Write the sample size, time window and workload. Compare to a baseline using the same cases. Decide in advance what triggers a pause.

Expand and maintain

Add one new capability at a time when its real dependency is ready. Update the matching guide, prompts, regression suite and operator training together. Review documents after each behavior change; do not leave an old deployment report as the user-facing source of truth.

The public manual, current product status and deployed runtime each serve different purposes: the manual explains use, status explains boundaries, and actual release evidence proves availability. Keep all three aligned.

articles.title: Customer agent: own the agent, open the agent
articles.description: The bank-operated assistant for the bank's own customers: sessions without a platform credential, the autonomy ladder, one-tap cards, the bank's step-up, why-this explanations, the permissions page and the embeddable element, all off by default.
articles.audience: Bank product, risk and platform teams
articles.html:
What the customer agent is

The customer agent is the bank's own assistant for its own customers. It sits in the bank's app, web, WhatsApp and voice channels, sees every product the customer holds and every product the bank can offer, answers with citations, recommends with a "why this" explanation, prepares actions for one-tap confirmation and, once a customer has set a mandate, executes inside that mandate. It runs on AgenticOrg, with Grantex as the authority service that holds every grant the customer gives, to the bank's agent and to any outside agent the customer connects.

The programme is called "own the agent, open the agent". Own the agent: the bank's assistant must be the best agent for the bank's services, so a customer has no reason to hand their finances to a general-purpose assistant. Open the agent: the bank is also the easiest institution for a customer's outside agent to connect to safely, through a governed MCP surface, Agent Passports and scoped grants the customer can see and revoke from one place. The full requirement set, market evidence, control catalogue and architecture are in the product requirements document.

Why it is easier than an in-app assistant

Early bank assistants on the market execute a short list of actions inside one app, ask for a biometric approval on each sensitive step, and see only what the customer sees on screen. The customer agent is designed to be easier to use and to go much further, while staying inside the bank's controls:

What the customer gets How it works
One agent across every service Deposits, cards, lending, mortgages, investments, insurance, payments, remittances and SME banking share one session, one memory and one permissions page.
Any channel, same conversation A conversation started in the app continues on WhatsApp or by voice; the agent keeps the context, not the customer.
Cards instead of chat Balances, due dates, prepared transfers and offers arrive as inline cards with one-tap confirm or cancel, never as a wall of text.
Approval only where it matters An autonomy ladder from inform (L0) to execute within mandate (L4) is set per task and per customer. Routine actions inside a mandate run without a prompt; new payees and high values always step up.
"Why this" on every recommendation Data used, rule or goal applied, alternatives considered, what the bank earns, and how to challenge the suggestion.
Whole-wallet view With consent through Account Aggregator or open banking, the customer sees accounts held elsewhere inside the bank's agent, so comparison no longer needs an outside app.
One place to see and stop every agent The permissions page lists the bank's agent and every outside agent, with scopes, caps and last action, and revokes with one tap. The revoked agent's next action is refused within seconds.
Open to the customer's own agent Outside agents connect through the bank's MCP server with a verified Agent Passport and a scoped grant; the bank, not the agent provider, stays accountable for what executes.
Evidence for every action Signed, hash-chained audit rows, run timelines and a per-interaction evidence package the bank can hand to an auditor.

How a request moves

The same path applies in every channel. The bank keeps identity and the step-up; the agent keeps the conversation, the explanation and the record.

  1. 1
    Sign in with the bankOwner: Bank identity team

    The customer signs in to the bank's own app or site; the bank's backend signs a short-lived assertion and opens a customer session.

    Blocked / exception

    Without the bank's assertion there is no session; the platform never accepts a customer the bank has not asserted.

  2. 2
    DisclosureOwner: Bank channel owner

    The customer reads that this is the bank's AI assistant and acknowledges it before the first turn.

    Blocked / exception

    Turns are refused until the disclosure is acknowledged.

  3. 3
    AskOwner: Customer agent

    The customer asks in their own words; the dialogue recognises the intent, collects the details across turns and explains why.

    Blocked / exception

    An unrecognised request gets a clarifying question or an offer of a person, never a guess.

  4. 4
    PrepareOwner: Customer agent

    For a transaction the agent prepares a card with the amount, the payee and a "why this" panel at the customer's autonomy level.

    Human decision

    The customer confirms with one tap, cancels, or asks for a change.

    Blocked / exception

    Below level 2 the action is explained and refused; the customer can raise the level on the permissions page.

  5. 5
    Step upOwner: Bank identity team

    Above the customer's limits, or at level 3, the bank's own passkey, biometric or one-time-code check approves the specific action.

    Human decision

    The customer approves the exact action and amount in the bank's step-up.

    Blocked / exception

    An approval for another action, customer or amount is refused and nothing runs.

  6. 6
    Execute and recordOwner: Bank operations and system of record

    The confirmed action runs through the bank's governed agent under its grant and is recorded with the explanation shown and the approval given.

    Blocked / exception

    No connected agent, a paused agent or a failed rail records the action as failed and tells the customer nothing was done.

What ships today

The customer agent ships off by default behind AGENTICORG_CUSTOMER_AGENT_ENABLED. With the flag off every route under /api/v1/customer-agent/ answers 404 and nothing else changes. On, a bank gets:

Capability How it works
Customer sessions without a platform credential The bank authenticates the customer as today, its backend signs a short-lived assertion (RS256 or ES256, checked against the bank's published keys, issuer and audience, single-use by its id) and exchanges it for an opaque session token. Only the token's hash is stored.
The autonomy ladder per task and per customer Level 0 inform, 1 recommend, 2 prepare and wait for one tap (the default for every transaction), 3 execute after the bank's step-up of the specific action, 4 execute within a mandate with caps, counterparties and a time window. AGENTICORG_CUSTOMER_AGENT_MAX_AUTONOMY (2 by default) bounds every level.
Prepared-action cards The dialogue collects the details and prepares a card; Confirm sends the same yes the dialogue expects, Cancel the same no. A card confirms only the action it shows: if the conversation moved on or the amount changed, it is superseded and nothing runs.
The bank's own step-up Level 3 and out-of-mandate level 4 need a bank-signed approval bound to the action id, customer and amount, verified before the engine executes.
"Why this" on every answer Data used, the rule or level applied, the mandate, alternatives, what the bank earns, how to challenge it, and the AI disclosure, assembled from the dialogue and the decision rather than generated.
A mandatory disclosure Recorded on the session; no turn runs before the customer acknowledges it.
One permissions page Every mandate the bank's agent holds, revocable with one call, and the authority service's dashboard of outside agents when the deployment is connected to it.
An embeddable element ui/public/customer-agent/widget.js registers <agenticorg-customer-agent> for the bank's page: the disclosure gate, cards, the "why this" panel and a host event for step-ups, with no dependencies and no markup from server text.
Records and evidence Sessions, mandates and every action prepared, executed, refused, cancelled or superseded, with the explanation shown and the approval given, in tenant-scoped tables under row-level security; executed actions also appear in the conversation session's record and the audit trail.

Confirmed actions run through the bank's configured agent, its bound tools and its grant exactly as the conversational services do. The intent catalogue is deterministic and generic: no institution's products or names. Grant revocation for paused and retired agents, and an opt-in revocation check before a token is honoured (AGENTICORG_GRANTEX_REVOCATION_CHECK=feed), ship alongside.

The step-by-step setup for the bank's engineers, the assertion and approval formats, the element's events and every route are in the integration guide.

Try it

  1. In a non-production deployment, set AGENTICORG_CUSTOMER_AGENT_ENABLED=true, the tenant, company and agent ids, and the assertion issuer, audience and JWKS URL of a test identity provider you control. Create the agent as described in Customer service and bind the tools the intents need.
  2. From your backend, sign a test assertion for a synthetic customer reference and exchange it at POST /api/v1/customer-agent/sessions; keep the session_token from the response.
  3. Read GET /session, acknowledge the disclosure with POST /session/acknowledge, and send "what is my balance" to POST /turns: the answer carries the recognised intent and its "why this" panel.
  4. Send "transfer 5000 to Ravi": the turn returns a prepared card at level 2. Confirm it with POST /actions/{id}/confirm (or reply yes) and inspect the run in Run observability; then read GET /actions to see the recorded action with its explanation.
  5. Set a mandate with PUT /permissions/mandates (level 4 with a per-action cap for fund_transfer), repeat a transfer inside the cap and watch it run in the same turn; repeat one above the cap and watch the card ask for the bank's approval.
  6. Load widget.js on a test page with the session token and walk the same path in the element.

Point no real customer at a deployment until the bank's identity provider, step-up and agent bindings are in place and the controls in the PRD are on.

What is planned

Phase Outcome
0: foundations (in progress) Shipped: grant revocation for paused and retired agents, revocation checks before a token is honoured. Next: durable conversation state by default, banking pack tools bound at creation, spend caps on every run path, and a bank deployment profile that forces the strict configuration.
1: inform and recommend (in progress) Shipped: customer sessions bound to the bank's identity, the embedded element, the autonomy ladder, "why this", the disclosure, the permissions page. Next: WhatsApp and voice in Hindi and English, L0 and L1 across the whole service range, the whole-wallet view, human hand-off with the supervisor view, nudges with control groups.
2: execute with approval and open MCP Shipped: L2 and L3 with the bank's step-up for the transaction intents in the catalogue. Next: signed intent records, the bank's MCP server and scope registry, outside agents on the permissions page with one-tap disconnect.
3: mandates and agentic payments Shipped: mandates with caps, counterparties and windows, and L4 execution inside them. Next: 90-day re-confirmation, network agent-token mirroring, Agent Passport gating.
4: ecosystem Trust-registry issuer onboarding, relying-party onboarding, signed-request verification, more Indian languages and voice providers.

Design rules

  • The model never holds credentials and never decides authority: grants and mandates are checked at the tool boundary and again at the bank's rail.
  • Every action the agent takes is attributable to a customer, a grant and a run, and every grant can be revoked instantly.
  • The agent informs and recommends by default; execution is earned per task and per customer and is demoted on the first irregularity.
  • No PIN, OTP, password or card number is ever requested or accepted in conversation.
  • AI involvement is disclosed at first use and on every interaction, and a human is reachable at every turn.

Next: Capability status and gaps, Customer service, Approvals.

   Why it is easier than an in-app assistant

Early bank assistants on the market execute a short list of actions inside one app, ask for a biometric approval on each sensitive step, and see only what the customer sees on screen. The customer agent is designed to be easier to use and to go much further, while staying inside the bank's controls:

  What the customer gets   How it works  
 --- --- 
  One agent across every service   Deposits, cards, lending, mortgages, investments, insurance, payments, remittances and SME banking share one session, one memory and one permissions page.  
  Any channel, same conversation   A conversation started in the app continues on WhatsApp or by voice; the agent keeps the context, not the customer.  
  Cards instead of chat   Balances, due dates, prepared transfers and offers arrive as inline cards with one-tap confirm or cancel, never as a wall of text.  
  Approval only where it matters   An autonomy ladder from inform (L0) to execute within mandate (L4) is set per task and per customer. Routine actions inside a mandate run without a prompt; new payees and high values always step up.  
  "Why this" on every recommendation   Data used, rule or goal applied, alternatives considered, what the bank earns, and how to challenge the suggestion.  
  Whole-wallet view   With consent through Account Aggregator or open banking, the customer sees accounts held elsewhere inside the bank's agent, so comparison no longer needs an outside app.  
  One place to see and stop every agent   The permissions page lists the bank's agent and every outside agent, with scopes, caps and last action, and revokes with one tap. The revoked agent's next action is refused within seconds.  
  Open to the customer's own agent   Outside agents connect through the bank's MCP server with a verified Agent Passport and a scoped grant; the bank, not the agent provider, stays accountable for what executes.  
  Evidence for every action   Signed, hash-chained audit rows, run timelines and a per-interaction evidence package the bank can hand to an auditor.  

   How a request moves

The same path applies in every channel. The bank keeps identity and the step-up; the agent keeps the conversation, the explanation and the record.

 Sign in with the bank   The customer signs in to the bank's own app or site; the bank's backend signs a short-lived assertion and opens a customer session.   Owner: Bank identity team   If blocked: Without the bank's assertion there is no session; the platform never accepts a customer the bank has not asserted.
Disclosure   The customer reads that this is the bank's AI assistant and acknowledges it before the first turn.   Owner: Bank channel owner   If blocked: Turns are refused until the disclosure is acknowledged.
Ask   The customer asks in their own words; the dialogue recognises the intent, collects the details across turns and explains why.   Owner: Customer agent   If blocked: An unrecognised request gets a clarifying question or an offer of a person, never a guess.
Prepare   For a transaction the agent prepares a card with the amount, the payee and a "why this" panel at the customer's autonomy level.   Owner: Customer agent   Human decision: The customer confirms with one tap, cancels, or asks for a change.   If blocked: Below level 2 the action is explained and refused; the customer can raise the level on the permissions page.
Step up   Above the customer's limits, or at level 3, the bank's own passkey, biometric or one-time-code check approves the specific action.   Owner: Bank identity team   Human decision: The customer approves the exact action and amount in the bank's step-up.   If blocked: An approval for another action, customer or amount is refused and nothing runs.
Execute and record   The confirmed action runs through the bank's governed agent under its grant and is recorded with the explanation shown and the approval given.   Owner: Bank operations and system of record   If blocked: No connected agent, a paused agent or a failed rail records the action as failed and tells the customer nothing was done.
 
   What ships today

The customer agent ships off by default behind  AGENTICORG_CUSTOMER_AGENT_ENABLED . With the flag off every route under  /api/v1/customer-agent/  answers 404 and nothing else changes. On, a bank gets:

  Capability   How it works  
 --- --- 
  Customer sessions without a platform credential   The bank authenticates the customer as today, its backend signs a short-lived assertion (RS256 or ES256, checked against the bank's published keys, issuer and audience, single-use by its id) and exchanges it for an opaque session token. Only the token's hash is stored.  
  The autonomy ladder per task and per customer   Level 0 inform, 1 recommend, 2 prepare and wait for one tap (the default for every transaction), 3 execute after the bank's step-up of the specific action, 4 execute within a mandate with caps, counterparties and a time window.  AGENTICORG_CUSTOMER_AGENT_MAX_AUTONOMY  (2 by default) bounds every level.  
  Prepared-action cards   The dialogue collects the details and prepares a card; Confirm sends the same yes the dialogue expects, Cancel the same no. A card confirms only the action it shows: if the conversation moved on or the amount changed, it is superseded and nothing runs.  
  The bank's own step-up   Level 3 and out-of-mandate level 4 need a bank-signed approval bound to the action id, customer and amount, verified before the engine executes.  
  "Why this" on every answer   Data used, the rule or level applied, the mandate, alternatives, what the bank earns, how to challenge it, and the AI disclosure, assembled from the dialogue and the decision rather than generated.  
  A mandatory disclosure   Recorded on the session; no turn runs before the customer acknowledges it.  
  One permissions page   Every mandate the bank's agent holds, revocable with one call, and the authority service's dashboard of outside agents when the deployment is connected to it.  
  An embeddable element    ui/public/customer-agent/widget.js  registers  <agenticorg-customer-agent>  for the bank's page: the disclosure gate, cards, the "why this" panel and a host event for step-ups, with no dependencies and no markup from server text.  
  Records and evidence   Sessions, mandates and every action prepared, executed, refused, cancelled or superseded, with the explanation shown and the approval given, in tenant-scoped tables under row-level security; executed actions also appear in the conversation session's record and the audit trail.  

Confirmed actions run through the bank's configured agent, its bound tools and its grant exactly as the [conversational services](/docs/bfsi-customer-service) do. The intent catalogue is deterministic and generic: no institution's products or names. Grant revocation for paused and retired agents, and an opt-in revocation check before a token is honoured ( AGENTICORG_GRANTEX_REVOCATION_CHECK=feed ), ship alongside.

The step-by-step setup for the bank's engineers, the assertion and approval formats, the element's events and every route are in the [integration guide](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/customer-agent/integration.md).

   Try it

1. In a non-production deployment, set  AGENTICORG_CUSTOMER_AGENT_ENABLED=true , the tenant, company and agent ids, and the assertion issuer, audience and JWKS URL of a test identity provider you control. Create the agent as described in [Customer service](/docs/bfsi-customer-service) and bind the tools the intents need.
2. From your backend, sign a test assertion for a synthetic customer reference and exchange it at  POST /api/v1/customer-agent/sessions ; keep the  session_token  from the response.
3. Read  GET /session , acknowledge the disclosure with  POST /session/acknowledge , and send "what is my balance" to  POST /turns : the answer carries the recognised intent and its "why this" panel.
4. Send "transfer 5000 to Ravi": the turn returns a prepared card at level 2. Confirm it with  POST /actions/{id}/confirm  (or reply yes) and inspect the run in [Run observability](/docs/run-observability); then read  GET /actions  to see the recorded action with its explanation.
5. Set a mandate with  PUT /permissions/mandates  (level 4 with a per-action cap for  fund_transfer ), repeat a transfer inside the cap and watch it run in the same turn; repeat one above the cap and watch the card ask for the bank's approval.
6. Load  widget.js  on a test page with the session token and walk the same path in the element.

Point no real customer at a deployment until the bank's identity provider, step-up and agent bindings are in place and the controls in the PRD are on.

   Design rules

- The model never holds credentials and never decides authority: grants and mandates are checked at the tool boundary and again at the bank's rail.
- Every action the agent takes is attributable to a customer, a grant and a run, and every grant can be revoked instantly.
- The agent informs and recommends by default; execution is earned per task and per customer and is demoted on the first irregularity.
- No PIN, OTP, password or card number is ever requested or accepted in conversation.
- AI involvement is disclosed at first use and on every interaction, and a human is reachable at every turn.
